title: [BUG] test_world_survives_serde runs an EMPTY schedule and is_equal omits the ECS World
description:
Two independent holes in the repo's only two-run determinism check, both found while proving sov-myg's terminal guard.

1. simulation/src/tests/test_iso.rs:247 builds the schedule as SeqSchedule::default() -- an EMPTY schedule. Simulation::schedule() (simulation/src/lib.rs:138-145) is the populated one that adds every registered gsystem. So the test executes ZERO simulation systems: it only applies replay WorldCommands, increments GameTime (lib.rs:251-254) and writes Replay::last_tick_recorded. PROVEN 2026-08-28 on branch fix/sov-myg-v2: a process-global-counter perturbation inserted into economy::market_update (simulation/src/economy/mod.rs:51) compiled and the test still passed green; the same perturbation moved into Simulation::tick (which the test does run) failed immediately. Inherited from upstream Egregoria at the fork commit 68fe28c, not introduced here.

2. Simulation::is_equal (simulation/src/lib.rs:214-233) compares ONLY the resources via saveload_funcs(). It never touches self.world. Simulation::hashes() (lib.rs:268-276) DOES hash the serialized World, so the TestCtx per-tick check covers it, but the two-run replay check does not. Corroborated by codex-lead's 2026-08-28 01:31 comment on sov-myg: an ECS-world mutation stayed green.

Net effect: even with sov-myg's terminal panic armed, this test can only catch a divergence in a serialized RESOURCE produced by command application or GameTime. A divergence in any system, or in the ECS world, is invisible to it.

TRAP: do not just swap in Simulation::schedule(). Running the real systems over this replay may surface pre-existing nondeterminism and will make the test much slower; expect to triage real findings, and expect the narrowing loop to run 11 rounds when it does trip.
acceptance_criteria: test_world_survives_serde runs the real system schedule; is_equal (or the test) compares the ECS World as well as the resources; a perturbation inserted into any registered system, and a perturbation of the ECS world, each make the test fail red.
close_reason: commit 7e771ce: test_iso.rs uses Simulation::schedule(); is_equal compares the encoded World; transport_grid gets an order-insensitive fallback (FnvHashMap cells permute across decode, sov-733). Guards in tests/determinism_gate.rs: sov_y66_is_equal_sees_ecs_world_divergence and sov_n8v_registered_systems_are_visible_to_is_equal ran RED on pre-fix code (determinism_gate.rs:70, :121), green after. cargo test -p simulation: 61 passed. Gate now runs the populated schedule in 8s; fixture World has 38 humans/53 vehicles/29 companies by tick 3072. No real nondeterminism surfaced.

comments.author: main
comments.text: Raised P2->P1 by main. Independently confirmed both holes in source before acting: test_iso.rs:247 is SeqSchedule::default() while Simulation::schedule() (lib.rs:138-145) is the populated one; is_equal (lib.rs:214-233) iterates saveload_funcs() only and never reads self.world. This is the repo's ONLY two-run determinism check, so per the P1-is-for-gates convention it belongs at P1: sov-myg armed the assertion, but it currently guards an empty schedule and a resource-only comparison.

title: Market lane send-back: vacuous dead-truck test, export gating, rebase
description:

Nothing here disputes the core fix -- the ext-trade import teleport IS fixed and all four mutation claims reproduced exactly. This is the fix list before merge.

1. REBASE FIRST. The branch is 20+ commits behind main and is missing 5349f34 and cdc8f1d (both sov-6qx), which rewrite exactly the unpark/ToSource seam this diff touches. git merge-tree reports no TEXTUAL conflict, but that is not a semantic one. Rebase, then re-run the suite before anything else.

3. F1 export half. find_external is one closure serving both the import and the export block. Imports need a driving lane; exports create no Dispatch and need none. Ungate exports. (sov-nun)

4. USER DECISION, 2026-08-28: the fresh-map border closure STAYS. A new city has no external trade and no cargo train until the player lays road to the station -- the train arriving is the reward for connecting. It must stop being SILENT: add a test asserting it and a line in the substrate doc.

5. Three small truths to repair: a tautological assert, a mutation instruction naming a field that does not exist, and a doc comment describing a proof the rewrite removed.

Exports work on a map whose station has no driving lane. A test asserts the default city has no border. Zero hits for outbound_route_retries.

title: Audit the authored practice blocks on docs/agent-practice against source
description:
The lead authored ~3094 lines of engineering-practice content now applied across 22 agent definition files (branch docs/agent-practice, commits 054a0cf and 60c5131, worktree /home/caio/sov-agents-wt). The content is dense with file:line citations, counts, commit shas, bd ids and measured numbers, nearly all asserted by the lead rather than re-derived.

Why this is P1: these files steer every agent on all future work, and a wrong citation propagates silently into 22 places at once. The last sweep of these same files found 8 confirmed-wrong claims. The lead was independently wrong twice in this session on exactly this class of claim -- once asserting a settings.json hook replacement that had not happened, and once telling three agents the code graph was current when head_matches_build was false.

This is the doc-reality-auditor's own named lane: does this document assert something the code does not support.

title: Negative request_multiplier passes validation and becomes a 4.3-billion-unit standing request
description: Found by researcher 2026-08-28 while mining the data lane for engineering practice. Status: PROVEN END TO END, no panic, nothing reports it. prototypes/src/validation.rs currently checks n_trucks, item ids and power sign ONLY. `request_multiplier = -3` in base_mod passes validate() cleanly, then `-3i32 as u32` wraps to roughly 4.3 billion, and the market accepts that as ordinary demand. A single typo in a Lua data file therefore creates a standing request larger than the entire economy, silently. `request_multiplier = 0` is the sibling case: a silent permanent stall. TRAP: this is the data layer, so no Rust test covers it - market unit tests run against thread-local fixtures (market.rs:1168, :1207) and do NOT load base_mod. Only tests/scenarios/* would catch it, and `cargo test -p prototypes` is never sufficient evidence for a base_mod change. Related shape, same root: cereal production amount 0 passes `cargo test -p prototypes` (5 passed) and kills `cargo test -p simulation` with 20+ failures, attempt to divide by zero at money.rs:193, because market.rs:1127 divides by qty. Validation must live where the invariant is CONSUMED, not only where the value is parsed. request_multiplier is the dishonest-enterprise dial - the core loop of the game - which is why this is P1.
acceptance_criteria: validation.rs rejects a negative or zero request_multiplier with a named error; a scenario test drives a bad base_mod value and sees it refused rather than wrapped; the cereal-amount-0 divide-by-zero is refused at parse or guarded at market.rs:1127. Mutation-proven: restore the bad value, watch the guard fire.
close_reason: commit 370ef54: validate() refuses request_multiplier < 1 and any recipe amount < 1 with a named error; market.rs:1232 skips instead of dividing. Verified by main independently of the implementer: cargo test -p prototypes = 5 passed; cargo test -p simulation = 57 passed, 1 ignored, with all 5 new tests appearing BY NAME in the output (tests::scenarios::validation::sov_k3w_*), so the filter-matches-nothing trap does not apply. Mutation-proven three ways and re-derived at the review gate: both guards -> 'if false' gives 1 passed / 4 failed with the control still green; restoring request_multiplier=-3 and production {flour,0} in the real base_mod each fail with the named error; removing the market guard brings back the divide-by-zero at prototypes/src/types/money.rs:193. Phase-4 gate: wiring-auditor WIRED, kornai-economist CONSISTENT, reviewer APPROVE.

comments.author: data-implementer
comments.text:
Fixed. validate() (prototypes/src/validation.rs) now rejects request_multiplier < 1 and any recipe consumption/production amount < 1, both as ValidationError::InvalidField carrying the company name, the field, and the offending value. market.rs calculate_price_inner now skips a recipe as a price candidate when qty <= 0 instead of dividing (minprice already tolerates no candidate).

New public API: prototypes::try_parse_prototypes(lua) -> Result<(), PrototypeLoadError> — runs the real parse+validate path, returns the error instead of panicking (test_prototypes unwraps) and never touches the thread-local prototype slot. 5 tests in simulation/src/tests/scenarios/validation.rs use it.

CORRECTION to this issue's description: the divide-by-zero lands at prototypes/src/types/money.rs:193 (Div<i64> for Money), not simulation/src/economy/money.rs — that file does not exist. The divide site is market.rs:1230 (was cited as :1127).

base_mod distribution: 26 recipes. request_multiplier set on 2 of 26 (flour-factory=4 companies.lua:40, meat-factory=3 :582); the other 24 omit it and take the parse default of 1 (honest). Recipe amounts: min 1, max 10 (flour-factory production flour 10), one 2 (vegetable); every one already >= 1, so no base_mod value changed.

Mutation-proven, all output pasted in the report to main: request_multiplier=-3 in companies.lua:40 -> test_base FAILED 'flour-factory.recipe.request_multiplier: must be at least 1, got -3'; production flour 0 at :37 -> 'flour-factory.recipe.production: amount for flour must be at least 1, got 0'; and with validation bypassed + fixture amount 0, removing the market guard reproduces 'attempt to divide by zero' at money.rs:193 while the guard present gives no panic. Verified: cargo test -p prototypes 5 passed; cargo test -p simulation 58 run, 57 passed 1 ignored.

comments.author: kornai-economist
comments.text:
DOMAIN SIGN-OFF (kornai-economist), working tree over f6725f1: CONSISTENT WITH THE MODEL, one caveat filed separately.

1. FLOOR OF 1 IS CORRECT, and is the only correct floor. Under shortage no enterprise rationally under-requests; Kornai's whole point is that the rational move is to inflate (Economics of Shortage, the quantity-drive). request_multiplier=0 is not a mothballed plant and not an honest minimal request - it is a permanent silent stall: recipe_init (souls/goods_company.rs:23) sets qty 0, buy_until never acquires, recipe_should_produce (goods_company.rs:35) requires capital >= amount which never becomes true. 'Requests nothing' is already expressible correctly as an EMPTY consumption list (farms/mines), which the floor does not touch. 0 is always a modelling error. Negative is worse: -3 -> 4_294_967_293 via 'as u32' at goods_company.rs:23, a standing request larger than the economy, which is not hoarding but an arithmetic accident and would starve every other buyer of that item. Note the dial is now one-sided 1..inf by construction - any future AC positing an under-requesting enterprise is impossible, and correctly so.

2. REFUSING AT LOAD DOES NOT BREACH 'NEVER GAME OVER'. The pillar governs a RUNNING simulation: failure must degrade into queues, shortages and colder homes. This refusal fires at simulation/src/init.rs:44-49, which already panics on any validate() error (n_trucks, dangling item ids, negative power) BEFORE a world exists. No city, no save, no player state is lost - it is the same class as a missing asset. The diff adds members to a pre-existing refusal set; it creates no new failure mode. Failing to LOAD is a data contract; failing during PLAY is what the pillar forbids. This falls on the load side.

3. PRICE GUARD HAS NO CLEARING CONSEQUENCE. Traced every consumer: calculate_prices feeds only SingleMarket::new -> ext_value (market.rs:216,219). ext_value is read at exactly three places: market.rs:651 and :740 (external-trade money_delta) and native_app/src/gui/hud/windows/economy.rs:343 (display). Domestic matches hard-code money_delta: Money::ZERO (market.rs:544). money_delta only accumulates into gvt.money (economy/mod.rs:104) and ecostats - NOTHING gates on Government.money, which is the soft budget constraint working as designed. So price is decorative domestically and is the border exchange rate at the border, exactly as the model requires. Money::ZERO is also NOT a new state: any item produced by no company with a recipe already gets minprice=None -> Money::ZERO today (market.rs:1207,1247), so the guard introduces no signal downstream that did not already exist. Its only effect at ext trade would be a free import/export of that one item - undesirable but unreachable now that validate() refuses amount<1.

GUARD THAT MUST NOT BE DELETED: the 'if qty <= 0 { continue; }' at market.rs:1231. validate() makes it unreachable from base_mod, so it will read as dead code to a future cleanup pass. It is not. It is the no-panic-on-a-live-path guard on the only division in this function, and pillar 2 requires it independent of reachability. Same shape as the market.rs Parked guard that a ticket proposed deleting.

REJECTED ALTERNATIVES, so they are not re-proposed: (a) clamping request_multiplier at consumption instead of refusing at load - a clamp turns a typo into plausible behaviour with no warning, which is this repo's signature defect, and clamping 0 to 1 would silently make a dishonest enterprise honest; (b) substituting a fallback divisor in calculate_price_inner - publishes a silently wrong border price; skipping the candidate is right.

CAVEAT (separate hole, NOT introduced by this diff, does not block sign-off): prototypes/src/types/recipe.rs:63 still reads request_multiplier as get_lua(..).unwrap_or(1), which swallows a TYPE error as well as absence. Scenario: companies.lua:40 gets request_multiplier = "four" or a bool or a table -> get_lua returns Err -> unwrap_or(1) -> the recipe loads as HONEST -> validate() sees 1 and passes -> the flour factory silently stops hoarding and the core loop of the game is deleted with no error anywhere. The new floor cannot catch this because it never sees the bad value. The correct form already exists two files over at prototypes/src/prototypes/goods_company.rs:41-42: get_lua_opt(&table, "request_multiplier")?.unwrap_or(1). One line. This is the same ticket's own stated principle applied to the parse side. Filing as a follow-up bead; recommend P2.

comments.author: reviewer
comments.text:
REVIEW GATE (Phase 4) - VERDICT: APPROVE. Re-derived from source at working tree over f6725f1; did not inherit the implementer's summary.

RAN MYSELF (not pasted from the report):
- cargo test -p simulation -- --list | grep sov_k3w -> all 5 tests collected by full path tests::scenarios::validation::sov_k3w_*. Collection confirmed, so the filter-matches-nothing trap does not apply.
- cargo test -p prototypes -> 'test result: ok. 5 passed; 0 failed'.
- cargo test -p simulation -> 'test result: ok. 57 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored' in 41.53s.
- MUTATION (mine, not the implementer's): replaced BOTH new guards in validation.rs with 'if false' -> 'test result: FAILED. 1 passed; 4 failed'. The 4 refusal tests all failed with expect_err panics; sov_k3w_good_recipe_is_accepted still passed, so the control is a real control and the suite is not vacuous. validation.rs restored from backup; git diff --stat shows the original 51 insertions, 0 occurrences of 'if false'.
- cargo clippy -p prototypes -p simulation --all-targets: no new warning attributable to the diff (the only alarming one, 'assertion is always false', is pre-existing at prototypes/src/tests.rs:13, untouched).

JUDGMENTS ON THE FIVE ASKED POINTS:
1. '< 1' floor is right for all three fields. request_multiplier semantics are documented at types/recipe.rs:44-51 (1 honest, >1 dishonest); 0 has no design use, it is the stall. A recipe that consumes nothing is expressed by an EMPTY consumption list, not by amount 0, so no legitimate case is forbidden. Coverage is complete: Recipe appears on exactly one prototype (prototypes/goods_company.rs:23) and validate() iterates proto.goods_company.values(), so there is no un-validated Recipe holder.
2. The unsafe refactor is sound. parse_prototypes_boxed touches no global: macros.rs:97 parse_prototype writes only &mut self, compute_orderings (macros.rs:82) and print_stats (macros.rs:72) are pure/logging. PROTOTYPES (lib.rs:105) and TEST_PROTOTYPES (lib.rs:111) are written ONLY at load.rs:33 and load.rs:12, neither reachable from try_parse_prototypes. The unsafety of parse_prototypes_str was never about parsing - it is the leak-plus-install contract - so pulling the pure part out into a safe fn widens no contract. try_parse_prototypes also drops the Box rather than leaking, so repeated test calls do not leak.
3. The market guard is correct and changes no valid price. qty is >= 1 for every recipe validate() admits, so no previously-published price moves; and the unwrap_or(0) arm is unreachable by construction (a company only enters item_graph[id] at market.rs:1191-1193 because it produces id). The guard sits AFTER the recursive calculate_price_inner calls at :1214-1217, so input prices are still populated. It cannot mask a real bug: it is unreachable post-validation and exists only for pillar 2.
4. Tests are real - proven by the mutation above, not asserted.
5. All acceptance criteria met. 'named error' -> ValidationError::InvalidField carrying company, field and value. 'scenario test drives a bad value and sees it refused' -> the 4 refusal tests through the real parse+validate path. 'cereal-amount-0 divide-by-zero refused at parse OR guarded' -> both. 'mutation-proven' -> re-proven independently by me.

NON-BLOCKING GAPS FOUND (none in the diff itself; all pre-existing siblings, out of this ticket's acceptance criteria - recommend follow-up beads):
(a) storage_multiplier is the same defect shape and is still unvalidated. souls/goods_company.rs:64 does '(item.amount * recipe.storage_multiplier) as u32' -> storage_multiplier = -1 with amount 1 gives -1 as u32 = 4294967295 passed as sell_all's stock cap; and goods_company.rs:46 '< item.amount * (storage_multiplier + 1)' with -1 gives 0, a silent permanent production halt. base_mod is currently clean (26 recipes, no zero or negative), so this is latent, not live. One more clause in the same loop the diff just edited. Recommend P2.
(b) souls/goods_company.rs:205 divides by recipe.duration.seconds() as f32. A duration of 0 gives +inf progress rather than a panic - silent runaway production every tick, same silent-wrong-meaning class. Recommend P3.
(c) I independently confirm the implementer's own CAVEAT: types/recipe.rs:63 'get_lua(&table, "request_multiplier").unwrap_or(1)' swallows a TYPE error as absence, so request_multiplier = true loads as HONEST and validate() sees 1 and passes. The correct form is two files over at prototypes/goods_company.rs:41-42 (get_lua_opt(...)?.unwrap_or(1)). Recommend P2. Note the same swallow applies to the other Recipe fields at recipe.rs:59-62 via get_lua's '?', which does propagate - only line 63 unwraps.

SCOPE: clean. Files touched are exactly load.rs, validation.rs, market.rs, scenarios/mod.rs plus the new test file; base_mod is unchanged (git diff --stat over base_mod/ is empty), matching the claim that all 26 recipes already satisfy the new floor. Untracked .work/briefs/ predates this ticket (sov-mwy, sov-tnq) and is not this diff's creep, but it is neither tracked nor gitignored.

comments.author: wiring-auditor
comments.text:
wiring-auditor gate (Phase 4 row 1), working tree over f6725f1: WIRED, with one reachability gap named.

1. validate() IS on the production path: native_app/src/init.rs:34 and headless/src/main.rs:35 -> simulation::init::init() (simulation/src/init.rs:44) -> prototypes::load_prototypes -> parse_prototypes_str (load.rs:51) -> parse_prototypes_boxed -> validation::validate(&p) at load.rs:77. A validation error panics at init.rs:46-48, i.e. refusal at load, not a live path. Verified real base_mod still loads: cargo test -p prototypes test_base -> 1 passed.
2. try_parse_prototypes (load.rs:43) is pub with ZERO production callers - only the 5 new tests. TEST-ONLY by design (it exists to make refusal observable) and it shares parse_prototypes_boxed with the production path, so it is not a parallel path. Named, not a blocker.
3. market.rs:1232 'if qty <= 0 { continue; }' is inside calculate_price_inner, reached from Market::default (market.rs:216), a registered resource (init.rs:125) - production-reachable code. The BRANCH itself is unreachable for any prototype set that passed validate(): qty comes from the recipe that put the company in item_graph, so find_map always hits, and amount>=1 is now enforced. Defense-in-depth against a pillar-forbidden panic, documented as such. DEAD-but-justified, minor.
4. Tests collected and run: cargo test -p simulation --lib sov_k3w -> 'running 5 tests', all 5 named, '53 filtered out'. Full suite in the audit tree: 58 tests, 57 passed, 1 ignored, 0 failed.
5. GAP (major, house defect shape 1): the new request_multiplier guard cannot be reached for a MALFORMED value. recipe.rs:65 is get_lua(&table, "request_multiplier").unwrap_or(1), which swallows a type error into the honest default before validate() ever sees it. Probed in a throwaway worktree against the real parse+validate path: request_multiplier = "abc" ACCEPTED, = true ACCEPTED, = 2.5 ACCEPTED (all become 1, silently). Only "-3" and -3.0 are REFUSED. So a typo on the dishonest-enterprise dial still silently deletes the core loop. Fix shape already exists at prototypes/src/prototypes/goods_company.rs:41-42. Recipe amount fields are safe - they use a propagating get_lua()? ("abc" refused with a conversion error).
No stray edits in scope at start or end of audit (git status --porcelain limited to the 4 diff files + the new test file).

title: ToSource dispatch state has no tick countdown, unlike every other waiting state
description:
DispatchState::ToSource has no tick countdown and no bound on either arm. sov-jcl bounded Loading; ToSource was left unbounded, and sov-abs (7721cdd) newly routes EVERY unmet enterprise import into it, so the surface is now large and production-reachable.

CONFIRMED at source by the lead, 2026-08-28 -- this is a never-game-over pillar violation, not just a wedge:

1. market.rs:780-830, the ToSource/truck:None arm is 'if let Some(seller_pos) = door_pos(..)' with no else and no counter. No truck, no route, or a demolished freight station leaves the dispatch immortal with its truck reserved out of the pool permanently.
2. The buy order is already gone. The ext-trade block removes it via extract_if at match time (market.rs:621), so it is not re-offered.
3. The enterprise CANNOT RECOVER. buy_until has exactly two callers -- recipe_init (souls/goods_company.rs:25, once at company creation) and recipe_act (:56). recipe_act only runs when recipe_should_produce is true, which requires capital >= amount. Capital is never credited because the import never arrives. So a stranded import kills the enterprise permanently, and it stays dead even after the player lays the road that would have fixed it.

Reachable via a lane-proximate but graph-disconnected station: find_external only tests 50-unit proximity to a Driving lane, while DispatchOne::query (map_dynamic/dispatch.rs:264-293) runs a real backward BFS over the lane graph. Proximity passes, BFS returns None every tick, dispatch sits forever.

TRAP: a bare countdown is NOT sufficient and must not be accepted as the fix. Removing the dispatch without re-posting the buy order leaves the enterprise just as dead. The caller must undo its own bookkeeping -- re-post via Market::buy BEFORE removing the dispatch. This is the sov-6qx rule and logistics-modeller asked explicitly that this ticket block on it.
acceptance_criteria: A scenario test proves an enterprise whose import strands in ToSource re-posts its buy order and RESUMES production once a route becomes available. Mutation-prove it: remove the re-post and watch the test go red. A countdown with no re-post fails this criterion.
close_reason: P1 ToSource bounded wait + re-post-before-remove, 3 scenarios pass. Wave-1 gates green.

Q1 bound shape: MAX_SOURCE_WAIT_TICKS = TICKS_PER_MINUTE = 5*60 = 300 ticks = 6 realtime s (time.rs:10,17-18). Truck max_speed 22 m/s (roadvehicles.lua:18) so one bound covers ~132 m of driving; any job beyond ~66 m one-way outlasts it and a 1 km border trip (~4,500 ticks) costs ~15 timeouts. A truck-poor city therefore DOES churn: warn log per timeout, treasury debit at match (mod.rs:104) / refund 300 ticks later (:985) sawtooth for imports, dispatch re-pushed to the back of the vec. But no progress is lost: make_trades (mod.rs:70) runs before advance_dispatches (:130) so the re-posted order re-matches the very next tick, and the tear-down is free (no truck, no capital moved). Accepted as the smallest mechanism given the substrate has no reachability test at match time (find_external is proximity only; the BFS lives in DispatchOne::query). Rejected alternatives: a bare countdown (ticket trap; mutation shows it kills the enterprise); a longer bound (delays nothing useful, only prolongs the seller's reservation lock, which a reachable buyer can now take at re-match); wiring the Dispatcher BFS into find_external (right long-term fix, out of scope, would turn this bound into a rare backstop; fold into sov-2uv or a new ticket). Q2 fairness: there is no age order to preserve. Dispatcher::query is invoked per dispatch in vec index order (market.rs:866 loop), new dispatches push to the back (:735) and swap_remove (:1263) already scrambles order; domestic matching ranks by distance only (:585-596); the ext-trade block matches every non-human order every tick (:670-690). A re-post cannot jump a queue that does not exist; it goes to the back. Q3 observability: nothing in-game. Only log::warn (:991) and debug_inspect buy_order; the player sees an enterprise that does not produce, not why. Pre-existing, not worsened; mitigation I would accept: count timeouts per buyer in the else-branch at :970 and surface 'supplier unreachable' in the company panel (P2, new ticket). Q4 teleport: NONE. :976-978 releases reserved without moving capital; :985 reverses a payment for goods that never crossed; no truck exists in this arm; the truck=Some arm is untouched. Determinism: integer counter, BTreeMap, no RNG. Save seam: two new positional bincode fields, an old save decodes to default Market silently (init.rs:236-238) -- pre-existing house defect shape, process note. FINDING (CONFIRMED / major, out of the AC but named in this ticket's own description): 'a demolished freight station' is NOT covered. FreightStationEnt::sim_drop (world.rs:165-167) -> Market::remove seller-half (market.rs:445-457) drops the buyer's dispatch with no re-post and no money_delta refund; the enterprise dies exactly as before. Same shape at ToSource/Some entity-gone (:1005-1017), Loading exhaustion (:1052, :1085) and the ext-trade money is never refunded on any of them. Required: a P2 ticket 're-post buyer demand and refund money_delta on every dispatch exit that does not credit a live buyer' (one shared helper, sov-otw is the natural home). Noted for ledger: the ext-trade match never reserves at the station (:670-690), so :976 saturating_subs a reservation never taken -- harmless today because freight stations post no sell orders (freight_station.rs has no sell/reserved), same as the arrival arm at :1024. title: test_world_survives_serde cannot fail: determinism divergence exits green
description:
simulation/src/tests/test_iso.rs:241-306 is the repo's only two-run determinism check. It compares two sims built from one replay at checkpoint ticks. Every mismatch branch (lines 276-283, 284-291, 292-299) prints, dumps two save files, halves check_size and 'continue main'. When check_size reaches 0 the loop breaks at 252-255 and the test RETURNS NORMALLY. There is no assert! and no panic! in the function.

It is a bisection debugger wearing a #[test] attribute. Determinism could break and CI would stay green.

TRAP: the narrowing behaviour is USEFUL - it dumps world/ and world2/ for a human to diff. Do not delete it. Make it narrow first, then FAIL. The fix is to record that a divergence happened and assert at the end, not to panic on the first mismatch.

TRAP: this file is simulation/src/tests/test_iso.rs, NOT simulation/tests/. There is no simulation/tests directory.

WHY NOW: it is the foundation the proposed MCP test harness rests on (docs/plan/proposals/mcp-test-harness.md, step 0). An agent that cannot re-run a scenario reproducibly cannot debug anything.
acceptance_criteria: Mutate the sim to force a divergence (e.g. perturb one system's ordering or seed in a scratch edit); run the test; SEE IT FAIL RED with the divergence tick named. Revert the mutation; see it pass. Paste both outputs. The narrowing/save-dump behaviour must still work - world/ and world2/ are still written.
close_reason:
commit eed5ead (ancestor of main, unlike the earlier a48ea1d that caused the 2026-08-28 03:26 reopen). Verified by main on main after landing: cargo test -p simulation = 57 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored, with tests::test_world_survives_serde appearing BY NAME. Mutation-proven twice independently -- an AtomicU64 in Simulation::tick perturbing Government gives a full 11-round bisection then 'determinism divergence detected at tick 3', both world.zip and world2.zip still written, green after revert. A second mutation proved .max(3) is load-bearing: without it the run dies at Option::unwrap() on None in utils/resources.rs:80 naming no tick, so the terminal assertion is unreachable.

CAVEAT -- READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING THE GUARD. This closes the ticket as written (the check can now fail), NOT the broader claim that determinism is guarded. Per sov-n8v (P1): test_iso.rs builds SeqSchedule::default(), an EMPTY schedule, so ZERO simulation systems execute; and is_equal compares only saveload resources and never reads self.world, so the ECS is invisible to it. The armed panic can therefore only see a divergence in a serialized resource produced by command application or GameTime. The ticket's WHY -- that this is the foundation the MCP test harness rests on -- is NOT yet true; sov-n8v is what makes it true. Both holes are inherited from upstream Egregoria at fork commit 68fe28c.

Correction on the record: an earlier comment called .max(3) an underflow fix. It is not -- get_tick returns u64 and the loop guard makes tick >= check_size always. It is a floor fix, preventing check_start reaching 0. Phase-4 gate: reviewer APPROVE-WITH-FIXES, both fixes applied (commit body written, close reason qualified).

title: [bug] LAV::iter_keys is unbounded on a corrupted cycle and OOM-kills the game
description:
geom/src/skeleton.rs:721 LAV::iter_keys builds a Vec from std::iter::successors over a circular linked list, terminating ONLY when next == head:

    pub fn iter_keys(&self, vs: &Vertices) -> Vec<VertexID> {
        if let Some(head) = self.head {
            std::iter::successors(Some(head), move |&cur| {
                vs[cur.0].next.filter(|&x| x != head)
            })
            .collect()

If the list contains a cycle that does not pass through head, the iterator never yields None and .collect() grows without bound. The LAV struct declares a len field (skeleton.rs:717) which is NOT used to bound the walk. Seven call sites reach it: lines 469, 528, 650, 694, 775, 871.

MEASURED by perf-engineer 2026-08-27 while building the sov-1ae 250k contract: an uncapped run reached 17.6 GB RSS and was OOM-killed, with an observed allocation request of exactly 2^33 bytes. Reproduction rate roughly 1 in 1e5 placements at a 20 m footprint, and substantially higher at 8 m because gen_exterior_house scales the polygon by size/40.0.

REACH FROM THE PLAYER: WorldCommand::MapBuildSpecialBuilding -> Building::make -> gen_exterior_house -> straight skeleton. That is the SAME command native_app/src/gui/hud/toolbox/building.rs:170 emits when a player places a building. So this is not confined to the benchmark.

PILLAR VIOLATION: 'Never game over' is absolute in this project - failure degrades into queues and shortages, it never terminates. An OOM kill terminates the process. This defect breaks that rule directly.

BLOCKS sov-1ae: the simulation cannot currently construct a 250000-house city at all, so the scale benchmark contract cannot be completed until this is fixed.

TRAP for whoever fixes it: bounding the walk by self.len hides the corruption rather than explaining it. Decide deliberately whether the correct fix is (a) bound the walk and report the inconsistency, (b) prevent the corrupted cycle from being constructed upstream, or (c) both. A silent cap converts a crash into wrong geometry.

OWNER: geom/ is now owned by geom-implementer (roster updated 2026-08-27, commit a6bff8d).
acceptance_criteria: A test constructs a LAV whose linked list contains a cycle not passing through head, and demonstrates the current unbounded growth before the fix. After the fix that same input terminates. Placing buildings at an 8 m footprint across at least 1e5 placements completes without an OOM kill and without unbounded RSS growth. The chosen remedy is justified in the commit message against the three options in the description. cargo test -p geom and cargo test -p simulation both pass.
close_reason: commit 2cc7331 (merge of 4d1d18b + ca3ef2e): opus reviewer APPROVE, no blocking findings. Bound at vs.len()+1 proven correct by pigeonhole over a push-only arena; the +1 proven necessary by mutation (limit=vs.len() turns 5 tests red). Refusal proven by mutation: any_corrupt stubbed to false -> skeleton_refuses_a_polygon_that_corrupts_a_lav FAILS. Ticket's named trap (silent truncation) proven guarded: dropping the corrupt branch turns 2 tests red. OOM reproduced independently under a 2G cgroup (SIGKILL, EXIT=137) and flat after the fix: 100000 placements, peak rss 8256 kB release / 9624 kB debug. Oracle polygon re-derived bit-for-bit from gen_exterior_house(8.0, 32362); retry 1 for that seed succeeds, so the production retry loop terminates. Suites on merged main: geom 24 passed, simulation 45 passed + 1 ignored. Follow-ups sov-cnq and sov-crl filed, neither blocking.

Ground truth from grep -n iter_keys geom/src/skeleton.rs: 469, 528, 650, 694, 775, 871 call; 721 defines. Note 528 and 650 are both inside SLAV::handle_split_event (spans 506-671), so a signature change hits that function twice. An edge count is never a call-site count.

comments.author: geom-implementer
comments.text:
Fixed on branch fix/sov-bo3-lav-unbounded, commit 4d1d18b. Remedy (c): bound + refuse, NOT bound-by-self.len.

Three things the next agent should not rediscover:

1. The bound is vs.len()+1, deliberately NOT self.len. self.len is maintained by unify()/from_chain(), the same bookkeeping under suspicion, so bounding by it is circular and can truncate silently. vs.len()+1 is a proof, not a cap: a LAV is a ring of DISTINCT arena vertices so it holds at most vs.len() of them. The +1 matters -- the initial LAV of a polygon legitimately spans the whole arena. Zero false positives, and all four pre-existing skeleton tests still pass unchanged, which is the evidence.

2. skeleton() now returns Option<Vec<Subtree>>. On proven corruption it returns None instead of truncated geometry. The type change is intentional: it makes the compiler enumerate every call site rather than letting an empty Vec pass as a valid skeleton. simulation/src/map/procgen/building.rs:94 already wrapped skeleton() in catch_unwind + 'continue retry', so None joins an existing exercised degradation path -- the building still gets placed from a different polygon. Never-game-over satisfied without a panic.

3. Option (b), preventing the corrupt cycle upstream, is NOT done and is real follow-up. The two construction sites are handle_split_event's x/y selection (approx_equal at 0.1% relative, plus an ABSOLUTE EPSILON=1e-5 on normalized cross products -- absolute thresholds are why the 8 m footprint, scaled by size/40.0, reproduces more often than 20 m) and LAV::from_chain. I did not guess at those: they are determinism-critical float comparisons in the bottom crate, and an unverified change there diverges replays. File a separate ticket if the root cause is wanted.

TRAP found while building the harness, unrelated to this defect: gen_exterior_house reads crate::colors(), so any caller outside the TestCtx harness must run crate::init::init() first. Otherwise prototypes() hits unwrap_unchecked -- a debug-assert panic in dev, a bare SIGSEGV in release with no message. Cost me three turns. Also, in test builds prototypes load from '../', so a test binary must be run with cwd = simulation/, not the repo root.

Ticket correction: the DESCRIPTION says 'Seven call sites' but lists six; six is right, 721 is the definition. The compiler confirmed exhaustiveness via the signature change.

Evidence, every run under a hard ceiling (systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax -p MemorySwapMax=0):
- geom unit test on a hand-built corrupt LAV, 1G ceiling: before = cgroup kill at anon-rss 1046336 kB exit 137; after = ok.
- 100000 placements at 8 m, deterministic seeds, release, 2G ceiling: before = cgroup kill at anon-rss 2092904 kB between seed 30000 and 40000, exit 137; after = ok, start rss 7400 kB / peak 8292 kB / end 8292 kB.
- cargo test -p geom: 23 passed 0 failed. cargo test -p simulation: 45 passed 0 failed 1 ignored (the sweep, marked #[ignore] because it must be run under a ceiling).

Not closing; leaving for the lead's gate.

comments.author: wiring-auditor
comments.text: wiring-auditor 2026-08-27, commit 4d1d18b. H1 PASS: from_chain (skeleton.rs:796-808) builds local `l`, iter_keys sets l.corrupt via Cell on &self, then `l` is MOVED into lavs.push(...) as the push expression's value. H2 PASS-BY-CONSTRUCTION but FRAGILE: all 5 production iter_keys call sites (470, 529, 651, 695, 903) reach an any_corrupt check in the SAME skeleton() iteration before any result escapes -- because skeleton() returns None and discards `output` wholesale, not because any call site inspects the flag. The two `continue`s at 948/956 skip the end-of-loop check but call no iter_keys, so they cannot leak. handle_split_event's x==None path returns early at 581-588 with (None, vec![]) -- no unwrap panic when site 529 yields empty. Both None and panic collapse to the same retry. No other production caller repo-wide; the 4 .unwrap()s at skeleton.rs:1134/1147/1169/1175 are all in #[cfg(test)] mod tests. No new panic path. H4 FAIL: the memory guard is UNWIRED. Only workflow is .github/workflows/dependency-policy.yml, which is one cargo-deny job and whose own header forbids adding test steps (sov-ztg). No Makefile/justfile/xtask/other CI. Proven: 'cargo test -p simulation placement_stress' -> '0 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored'. comments.text:
evidence-auditor 2026-08-27, audit of the tests on fix/sov-bo3-lav-unbounded (4d1d18b). VERDICT: CONFIRMED on the OOM half, WEAKER-THAN-CLAIMED on the refuse-vs-truncate half.

title: lsp-first-read-guard deadlocks workers with no LSP tool
description:
HARNESS, not game code. ~/.claude/hooks/lsp-first-read-guard.js blocks Read on code files until an LSP warmup call, but never checks whether the agent HAS the LSP tool. Subagents frequently do not: one implementer reported 'ToolSearch found no LSP tool at all, for any query' while the hook still blocked Read. The only remaining way to read a file is 'bash cat', which rules/tool-discipline.md forbids — there is no legal move.

Second defect: the state flag is ~/.claude/state/lsp-ready-<md5(cwd)>, keyed on cwd ONLY. agentId is not in the PreToolUse payload and all subagents share the session's sessionId, so concurrent workers in one repo share ONE read budget. Verified: agents a7257c13c1cd759f4 and ad87181ae55be8f94 (identical promptId d2aea593, same cwd, 27s apart) drew from one counter; one hit 'Gate 5 — Read #6 requires at least 2 LSP navigation calls' having made only one nav call itself.

Impact measured on session a4b9c11d: 4 of 15 workers hard-blocked, 7 mentioned the guard or missing LSP. NOBODY reported it as a blocker — they silently degraded to bash cat, so tool discipline was being violated wave-wide and invisibly.

TRAP: do not 'fix' this by keying the flag per-agent. The payload does not carry an agent id; it cannot be done.

FIX (written and tested, NOT installed — global user config needs Caio's go-ahead):
/tmp/claude-1000/-home-caio-soviet-simulator/a4b9c11d-b7b9-453d-a0ca-3d7e14efbd86/scratchpad/lsp-first-read-guard.patched.js
Adds a per-file consecutive-block counter; after 2 blocks on the same file it relents with a loud systemMessage instead of blocking forever, and a successful read clears that file's counter. An agent that actually calls LSP never reaches the hatch.

VERIFIED STANDALONE (fake HOME, clean state):
  deadlock case, same Read retried 4x -> exit 2, exit 2, exit 0 (RELENTED), exit 0

title: Verify the 370 SUBSTRATE claims in the requirements corpus
description:
GATE on every remaining iteration. The largest known liability in the project, and nothing tracked it until now.

Every AC in requirements/EPIC-*.md carries a [SUBSTRATE: ...] tag asserting what the code already provides. Measured 2026-08-23:

  370 ACs carry a tag        103 cite an exact file:line
  265 ABSENT   33 CONFLICTS   26 PROVIDED   19 PARTIAL   17 UNAUDITED   10 OURS

NOT ONE HAS EVER BEEN VERIFIED. The extraction wrote them from spec prose. iterative-development's PAR reviews asked "what is missing?", never "is this true?". The format even has a tag literally named UNAUDITED.

WHY THIS IS P1: every serious failure of 2026-08-23 was a wrong substrate claim.
  - "extend map_dynamic::Dispatcher" - truck registration was commented out; the dispatcher had never seen a truck. The agent built the mechanism the AC forbade.

  - base_mod/items.lua sets optout_exttrade on 1 item of 21. That line falsified three claims in a landed commit.
Each cost 110-155k tokens. The next 122 stories are briefed off this same unverified corpus.

DO NOT rewrite the ACs wholesale. Record the verification result alongside; a wrong tag is a finding for the lead to disposition, not a licence to edit a ratified requirement.

title: Dispatches wedge: bakeries have no trucks but every bread purchase creates one
description:
Three unbounded-wait dispatch states, none with a timeout or cancellation. The dispatches Vec grows without bound and is walked every tick.

(c) IS THE GAMEPLAY-BREAKING ONE: every human bread purchase now creates a Dispatch, but bakeries are kind="store" (base_mod/companies.lua:11,126) and goods_company.rs:129 spawns trucks ONLY `if ckind == CompanyKind::Factory`. VERIFIED. So a city's bakeries accumulate one permanently-reserved dispatch per unfilled meal. Worse: recipe_should_produce reads RAW capital, not capital-reserved, so the bakery also stops producing while holding stock it can never sell.

(a) Loading with no route to buyer (market.rs:520-537): door_pos(buyer) returns None once the buyer's building is demolished; ticks_left is already 0 so it retries forever. The seller was ALREADY debited at ToSource arrival - quantity permanently destroyed. The truck is never dispatcher.free'd (only happens at market.rs:557), so it leaks too.

(b) ToSource with truck: Some(v) where the vehicle entity is gone: world.vehicles.get(v) -> None -> .unwrap_or(false) (market.rs:494-499) -> never arrives. reserved[seller] frozen forever.

FIX: needs a cancellation/timeout path. Consider also whether stores should get trucks, or whether human purchases should create dispatches at all.

Option C (no store->consumer dispatches, eat-time settlement), event-driven cancellation both Market::remove halves, MAX_RETURN_ROUTE_RETRIES bound, dead-seller truck free. Proof: cargo test -p simulation 42 passed/0 failed (parallel + serial); both new tests mutation-proven red by implementer AND independently re-run red by opus gate; ledger CONSERVED (r3, r4 adds no surface); opus APPROVE; codex cross-review SEND-BACK adjudicated — both new findings pre-fork, filed sov-jcl/sov-xyx. title: Ext-trade surplus sale double-spends reserved stock
description:
LEDGER BROKEN. Units created from nothing during ordinary gameplay.

market.rs:398-410 (ext-trade surplus loop) reads `capital` and NEVER reads `reserved`. `reserved` is read in exactly ONE place in the crate: the domestic filter_map at market.rs:319-322.

SUBTLETY - the domestic loop is NOT the bug. It decrements sorder.qty as it reserves, so within ONE make_trades pass the ext block sees order.qty == capital - reserved and closes correctly. The hole is `sell_all` (market.rs:191): it re-posts the order at FULL capital and forgets the reservation. recipe_act calls it every production cycle (goods_company.rs:56-61), so the overwrite is routine.

BREAK WINDOW: final capital = stock - reserved, negative iff reserved > stock. Production requires capital < amount*(mult+1) and reserved <= capital, so the window is amount*mult < capital < amount*(mult+1). EMPTY for amount=1. OPEN for amount=10.

REAL PROTOTYPE THAT HITS IT: base_mod/companies.lua flour-factory, production {{"flour",10}}, storage_multiplier=5 -> stock 50, gate capital<60, window 50<capital<60. VERIFIED present.

Sequence: F capital 59, domestic matches 55 (reserved=55, sorder.qty=4, capital still 59). recipe_act produces +10 -> 69, sell_all overwrites order to qty 69/stock 50. Next pass ext-trade: qty_sell = 69-50 = 19, guard passes, capital -> 50, 19 exported for real money. Trucks arrive, Loading debits 55 -> capital = -5. 69 units existed; 55 delivered + 19 exported = 74. FIVE CREATED FROM NOTHING.

Then capital<0 makes sell_all bail (c<=0), so the loss is silently absorbed as lost production.

FIX: guard and compute surplus against `*cap - reserved` / `order.qty.saturating_sub(reserved)`, or make sell_all post capital-reserved.

ALSO IN THIS BLOCK (separate, pre-existing): market.rs:387-396 credits the buyer BEFORE checking find_external. mod.rs:69-78 returns None when world.freight_stations is empty. So with no freight station - normal early game - every unmatched buy order is granted free every tick, no money debited, no Trade recorded so it does not even appear in EcoStats. Scarcity is off. FIX: move the credit inside the Some(ext) arm.
close_reason: commit fdfabca: ext-trade surplus computed against order.qty.saturating_sub(reserved) and guarded on *cap - reserved; buy-order credit moved inside the Some(ext) arm. Guard scenario_ledger_exttrade_double_spend seen FAILING first ('55 delivered + 19 exported > 69 ever produced, capital -5') then passing. 26 tests green.

title: simulation test binary segfaults under parallel test threads
description:
GATE on evidence reliability. PRE-EXISTING - reproduced on an unmodified tree (1 in 5 runs), NOT introduced by ITER-0000.

SYMPTOM: 'cargo test -p simulation' with default parallel threads segfaults intermittently (SIGSEGV, no Rust backtrace - a raw crash, not a panic). Reproduces ~1-in-3 to 1-in-5.

ROOT CAUSE: crate::init::init() (simulation/src/init.rs:33) pushes into 'static mut' INIT_FUNCS / GSYSTEMS / SAVELOAD_FUNCS with no synchronization. Every TestCtx::new() called it unconditionally, so concurrent test threads race on those pushes. rustc already warns here: 'creating a mutable reference to mutable static ... undefined behavior'.

PARTIAL FIX ALREADY IN TREE: TestCtx::new() now guards the init::init() call with std::sync::Once (simulation/src/tests/mod.rs). This REDUCES but does NOT eliminate the crash - some other unsynchronized global path is also involved and was not chased, to respect the do-not-touch-adjacent-code rule.

WORKAROUND until fixed: run 'cargo test -p simulation -- --test-threads=1'. All ITER-0000 verification used it.

WHY P1: the iterative-development spine treats sentinel scenario runs as evidence. A suite that segfaults 1-in-5 produces a confidently wrong signal - a green run proves little and a red run gets blamed on the wrong change. Fix before the sentinel corpus grows.

TRAP: do not 'fix' this by making the tests single-threaded in CI config and calling it done. That hides the UB rather than removing it; the static mut pattern is the defect.

Reviewer verdict: approve. Residual same-shape defect noted in native_app/src/init.rs:85-86 (out of scope, UI crate).

comments.author: implementer
comments.text:
Fixed. prototypes/src/lib.rs: static mut PROTOTYPES -> OnceLock<&'static Prototypes>, plus a thread_local TEST_PROTOTYPES override checked first by try_prototypes()/prototypes(). simulation/src/init.rs: the three static mut Vecs replaced by a single OnceLock<Registry> built inside init() and passed by &mut to the register_* helpers (now plain fns, no unsafe). Closures boxed as Fn + Send + Sync so they're sound to store in a static. simulation/src/lib.rs: all 8 call sites switched from 'unsafe { for x in &*addr_of!(STATIC) }' to plain 'for x in accessor_fn()'; removed the addr_of import.

SURPRISE: first pass (OnceLock only, no thread-local) built clean and passed --test-threads=1 in isolation, but failed 14/26 tests in both serial and parallel full-suite runs with 'no prototype for id FreightStationPrototypeID(...)'. Root cause: simulation/src/economy/market.rs unit tests call prototypes::test_prototypes(), which (via load_prototypes_str) used to overwrite the same static mut PROTOTYPES with a small ad-hoc Lua prototype set every call -- each test clobbered the global and got its own small set, order-dependent but self-consistent within a serial run. Under OnceLock.set(), the FIRST caller across the whole test binary wins permanently, so once a market.rs test ran first, every later TestCtx::new() (which loads the real base_mod data via init()) silently kept the earlier tiny prototype set and lacked ids like FreightStationPrototypeID. Fixed by splitting load into parse_prototypes_str() (returns &'static Prototypes, no global write) with two callers: load_prototypes() writes the process-wide PROTOTYPES OnceLock once, test_prototypes() writes a thread_local TEST_PROTOTYPES cell instead -- try_prototypes() checks the thread-local first. This matches the original isolation intent (each test's ad-hoc load only affects that test) without any unsynchronized global.

Verification: cargo build -p simulation -p prototypes -> 0 static_mut_refs warnings. cargo test -p simulation --test-threads=1 -> 26 passed, 0 failed (x2 runs). cargo test -p simulation (default parallel) x10 runs -> 26 passed, 0 failed, no segfaults, every run. tests/mod.rs Once guard kept (still avoids redundant expensive init work) but its comment updated since the static-mut race it described no longer exists.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
## Problem Statement

From the Planner's perspective, the border lies. Money leaves and arrives on the match tick while goods crawl for thousands of ticks; exports vanish from the seller and appear at the border in the same tick with no truck ever existing; import trucks load from a station that holds nothing; cargo lost on broken roads leaves no trace the inspector can show; and a dead enterprise's orders rot silently instead of re-posting. The mechanics-index calls this a violation on both halves, and it is right.

## Solution

Settle at the border, physically: money moves when goods cross, exports ride trucks to the border door like imports ride from it, the freight station holds a bounded stock that trains replenish, losses are recorded under a visible name, and every dispatch termination runs one shared exit routine. Five beads (sov-uo5, sov-bub, sov-7f7, sov-20g, sov-5ut), one simultaneous landing.

## User Stories

1. As the Planner, I want import money to leave only when the goods reach my station, so that the treasury mirrors physical reality.
2. As the Planner, I want export money to arrive only when the goods reach the border, so that selling is visibly tied to delivery.
3. As the Planner, I want to see export trucks driving to the border door, so that both directions of trade are equally observable.
4. As the Planner, I want the freight station to show a bounded import stock that trains replenish, so that border supply is a physical quantity I can reason about.
5. As the Planner, I want an import dispatch to fail observably when border stock is empty, so that I see going-without at the border instead of silent nothing.
6. As the Planner, I want route-failure losses recorded under a visible name in the inspector, so that I can audit where goods went.
7. As the Planner, I want bounded retries to still end in honest loss (not magic recovery), so that scarcity keeps its teeth.
8. As the Planner, I want a dead enterprise's buyer order re-posted and its money refunded, so that no failure is a silent game-over for that enterprise.
9. As the Planner, I want the seller's order restored when its dispatch dies before delivery, so that supply returns to the market.
10. As the Planner, I want ToSource to stop retrying forever and exit through the same bounded shape as every other leg, so that no dispatch hangs outside the model.
11. As the Planner, I want the Economy panel's Expenses/Income to keep proving border trade (and only border trade), so that the fixture world keeps demonstrating settlement.
12. As a scenario author, I want one shared exit helper with re-post/refund/restore semantics, so that the next dispatch exit site cannot reintroduce silent drops.

## Implementation Decisions

- The matching module keeps creating the commitment (orders wiped, reservation held, zero-quantity domestic deltas untouched); only the two border-leg money applications move to their arrival events.
- The export branch pushes its trade before the dispatch loop iterates, and export dispatches target the border door — symmetric with the import leg, no new dispatch states.
- Border stock is a bounded ledger on the freight station (glossary: Border custody), decremented on import dispatch, incremented by train arrival; it is not an entity and needs no census change.
- The loss sink is a named ledger (glossary: Lost), written by the existing seven deletion sites in place of (or in addition to) their warnings; deletion outcomes, bounds, and retry counts are unchanged.
- One shared exit routine owns every dispatch termination with three duties: re-post the buyer order unless fulfilled, refund nonzero money deltas (border legs dead between match and delivery), restore the seller order where the goods never left or return home. The ToSource bound is a named constant chosen by the implementer, with a test pinning it.
- Landing constraint: all five beads in one wave; the retail bounded-loss test and the determinism gate stay green throughout (fixture replays both border directions already).
- Contracts from ADR-0003 §Confirmation are the acceptance spine: arrival-tick money (EcoStats legs or probe), export dispatch with border-door target, empty-stock observable failure, inspector-visible Lost entries, no silent-drop exit.

## Testing Decisions

- A good test here asserts observable market truth (orders, stock, money, EcoStats legs, inspector rows), never internal call order; conservation is asserted on every ledger movement (money in = money out across matchLecturer/delivery/refund), determinism via the existing gate, idempotency on the exit helper (double-exit is a no-op).
- Modules under test: matching, the dispatch lifecycle, freight-station state, EcoStats recording. Prior art: the ledger.rs import test, the retail severed-road tests, the inflation blackout test, the determinism_gate census pattern.
- The gate (67-command/200k-tick replay) is the regression seam and must stay green; extend the census only for new entity kinds (none planned).
- Lost visibility gets a smoke check in the running game (severed-road scenario, inspector shows entries), not an automated UI test.

## Out of Scope

- Changing deletion outcomes, bounds, or retry counts (behavior is settled; observability only).
- New entity kinds, new dispatch states, new UI beyond inspector Lost rows.
- Domestic/retail/job money semantics (ZERO by construction, not a bug).
- The ToSource bound VALUE beyond 'named, constant, tested' (implementer picks).
- sov-aam (deadlock) and sov-ssv (batched-road panic): adjacent, separate beads.

## Further Notes

- Full code-truth (money sites, exit table with per-exit cargo/order/money fate) is in the 2026-09-04 comments on the five beads; the two scouts' briefs are the primary source if anything here is ambiguous.
- Domestic trades carry no money by construction, so panel Expenses/Income prove border trade only — document, don't 'fix'.
- Keep the fixture tail under ~250k ticks until sov-aam lands.

comments.author: DeadlockProbe
comments.text:
Root cause (by inspection, no runs per brief): abandoned dispatch trucks become permanent lane blockers. Both market park sites (Unloading, Returning in economy/market.rs) silently skip the truck when reserve_near finds no free spot: dispatch removed, dispatcher freed, truck left Driving with an ended itinerary in a live lane. Nothing ever assigns it a new route (dispatch trucks are not RandomVehicles members), so calc_decision returns (0,dir) on get_point()==None forever. Convoys queue behind each blocker -> 0.0m displacement; domestic truck matches stop completing while rail-served border exports flow (exports-only decay). Goods are already settled before either park site, so the stranded truck carries nothing.

Fix (transportation/testing_vehicles.rs, owned): random_vehicles_update now adopts unreserved ended-itinerary Driving/Panicking trucks into the random-vehicle set so the existing upkeep cruises them. Reserved (live-dispatch), Parked/RoadToPark, and non-trucks untouched. Degrade (cruise, nothing teleports, no goods at stake), never game-over. Needs Dispatcher::is_reserved un-cfg'd (map_dynamic/dispatch.rs, owned; signature unchanged, retail.rs/dispatch.rs test callers unaffected).

Test (simulation/src/tests/determinism_gate.rs, existing file): sov_aam_dispatch_trucks_displace_past_300k + en_route_dispatch_trucks helper. Materialises the fixture replay (tail untouched at 200k per TRAP), ticks past 300k, scans forward <=20k ticks for a non-empty cohort of reserved Driving non-ended trucks (dispatcher-observed, no market knowledge), ticks 2000, asserts every survivor still Driving displaced >1.0m. 2000 ticks ~= 400 game-seconds: covers red-light cycles and the 200s panic cap, so only the frozen-convoy shape can fail it. No suite runs here; orchestrator verifies (300k-tick run).

comments.author: DeadlockFixup
comments.text: Root cause (proved by freeze-time dumps, not the first diagnosis): closed human-truck wait-for loop, not abandoned ended-itinerary trucks. All 7 cohort trucks had NON-ended itineraries, Driving, reserved, speed 0.000; queue leaders (4v1 lane 78, 3v1 lane 108) each sat ~5m behind a LIVE standing pedestrian (front_dist 0.7 < 0.8 stop band). Those pedestrians were driver-humans (12v1, 24v1) whose WalkTo had ended at a stale snapshot while next step GetInVehicle waited on dispatch trucks 1v1/3v1 frozen in the queues behind them. Human waits for truck, truck waits for human: no timeout on either edge, exactly 0.0m over 2000 ticks. Cruise-recovery missed it: it only adopts ENDED, UNRESERVED trucks; these were non-ended and reserved. Fix (map_dynamic/router.rs): unready GetInVehicle (car exists but far) + current step over -> skip_stale_vehicle_block pops GetIn/Unpark/DriveTo/Park(frees spot)/GetOutVehicle so the trip degrades to walking; nothing ever drives a car TO a waiter so waiting was hopeless. Plus walk_outside idempotency guard. Test file restored; assertion/cohort shape unchanged. Scoped sov_aam run passes.

title: No populated world fixture exists: every 'watch it in the running game' criterion is unprovable
description:
Found by main 2026-08-28 while trying to capture sov-dda.4. This blocks a whole CLASS of tickets, which is why it is its own issue.

THE FACT: the only world save on disk (world/world.zip, ~1.7 MB) loads an EMPTY world -- forest, water and a single freight station. No city, no roads worth the name, no companies. Confirmed two independent ways: zoomed fully out shows nothing but terrain, and the in-game Economy panel opens with Expenses and Income graphs both EMPTY and Total 0$.

WHY IT BLOCKS A CLASS, NOT ONE TICKET: this repo's delivery rule is that progress is judged from the running game, and UI tickets carry acceptance criteria of the form 'one inspected live state ... with an inspected screenshot or 15-20 second video'. Any panel that renders per-company or per-economy state draws NOTHING in an empty world, so no honest capture is possible. sov-dda.4 is the current casualty; sov-uy2, sov-hoard-panel-mko (STORY-0107) and every future planner-facing panel hit the same wall and each pays the cost again.

WHAT DOES NOT WORK, so nobody retries it: the simulation test harness cannot drive the UI, and companies exist only in simulation/src/tests/scenarios/. TestCtx cannot produce a frame.

WHAT IS NEEDED: a committed, reusable, populated save fixture -- a small city with at least one goods company actually producing and trading, so a UI ticket can load it and see live data. Build it in-game (road, lots, wait for the auto-lot company spawn), verify companies exist via the Economy panel showing non-zero flows, then commit it as a fixture with a documented way to load it.

INPUT IS NOT THE BLOCKER, and this is worth knowing: synthetic input works on this machine. dotool is installed, the user is in the input group, and the move-away-then-to-target protocol in .claude/agent-memory/ui-implementer/yakui-synthetic-click-trap.md is correct -- main opened the Economy panel with a scripted click on the first attempt using it.

RELATED: sov-harness-lots-k54 (stop the harness depending on auto-generated lots before ITER-0005) is adjacent -- if auto-lot generation is going away, the fixture must not depend on it either. Consider the two together.
acceptance_criteria: A populated world save is committed to the repo and documented: it contains at least one goods company with live production and trade, proven by the in-game Economy panel showing non-zero Expenses/Income rather than 0$. A UI ticket can load it and see per-company data in the inspector. The way to load it is written down where a UI implementer will find it. The fixture must not silently depend on auto-lot generation if sov-harness-lots-k54 removes it.

Commits: eea7302 (replay: 67 cmds, 200k tail, freight spur, terrain empty-cell fix, materialise_replay, census+roundtrip guards), 204a76b (startup fallback chain + load-window schedule fix), 3391dfe (docs). title: storage_multiplier is unvalidated and has the identical sign-wrap shape as sov-k3w
description:
Found by reviewer 2026-08-28 at the sov-k3w Phase-4 gate, while answering 'what else consumes recipe numerics unguarded'. sov-k3w added a floor of 1 for request_multiplier and for recipe amounts. storage_multiplier sits in the SAME loop, in the SAME struct, and was not covered.

Two consequences, both silent, both the shape sov-k3w exists to prevent:

1. SIGN WRAP. simulation/src/souls/goods_company.rs:64 computes (item.amount * recipe.storage_multiplier) as u32. With amount=1 and storage_multiplier=-1 that is -1 as u32 = 4_294_967_295, handed to sell_all's stock cap (market.rs:253).

2. SILENT PRODUCTION HALT. goods_company.rs:46 tests capital < item.amount * (storage_multiplier + 1). With storage_multiplier = -1 the right side is 0, so the condition is never true and the enterprise stops producing forever with no queue, no shortage signal and nothing for the Planner to see.

LATENT, NOT LIVE: base_mod/companies.lua has 26 storage_multiplier entries and none is zero or negative (verified by the reviewer at f6725f1 and again by main). So this is a trap waiting for a data edit, not a current bug.

TRAP: prototypes unit tests alone are not sufficient evidence for a base_mod-class change -- see sov-k3w. The refusal must be driven through the real parse+validate path, for which prototypes::try_parse_prototypes (added by sov-k3w, prototypes/src/load.rs) is the accessor: it returns the error instead of panicking and installs nothing into the thread-local slot.

The fix is one more clause in the loop sov-k3w just edited (prototypes/src/validation.rs), reusing ValidationError::InvalidField.
acceptance_criteria: validate() refuses storage_multiplier < 1 with a named error carrying the company name and field. A test drives a bad base_mod-shaped value through the real parse+validate path via try_parse_prototypes and sees it REFUSED. title: make_trades external-trade branch has no money/quantity assertion: 8 mutants survive on main
description:
Mutation evidence (sov-mwy trial, RE-VERIFIED by evidence-auditor against main f6725f1 on 2026-08-28) shows the external-trade branch of Market::make_trades can be corrupted in eight distinct ways with all 52 simulation tests still green.

Each mutation below was applied one at a time to simulation/src/economy/market.rs in an isolated worktree off main, 'cargo test -p simulation' run in full, then reverted. Every one printed 'test result: ok. 52 passed; 0 failed'.

  651  delete '-'        money_delta: -(*ext_value * qty_buy)   ext BUY money sign
  651  '*' -> '/'        same expression                        ext BUY money magnitude
  718  '-' -> '+'        free_qty as i32 - order.stock as i32   exportable surplus quantity
  723  '<' -> '<='       *cap - already_reserved < qty_sell     oversell guard boundary
  723  '-' -> '+'        same guard                             reserved-aware subtraction
  732  '-=' -> '+='      *cap -= qty_sell                       seller capital debit on export
  732  '-=' -> '/='      same debit
  569  '-' -> '+'        cap_seller - already_reserved          domestic reserved-aware afford guard

Reachability: base_mod/items.lua declares 21 items and sets optout_exttrade on exactly one (job-opening), so 20 of 21 goods traverse this branch.

What the existing tests do and do not cover. ledger::sov_e1q_export_without_external_endpoint and ledger::sov_dii_no_freight_station_holds_seller_capital both assert the NO-export case (capital and sell_order.qty unchanged when find_external yields nothing). ledger::sov_abs_ext_trade_import_is_physical asserts an import is carried by a Dispatch and arrives, but makes no assertion about Trade.money_delta at all. So the physical half of ext-trade is guarded and the MONEY half is not, and no test asserts the magnitude of a successful export's capital or order.qty decrement.

This ticket is the assertion that must exist either way, and it covers the BUY-side money_delta (line 651), which sov-20g does not touch. Land after sov-20g so the test is written against the final shape.

Trap: do not assert only that a trade was produced. The surviving mutants all still produce a trade; what is unasserted is its sign and magnitude.
