title: request_multiplier type error parses as honest (1), silently deleting the hoarding loop
description:
Found by kornai-economist 2026-08-28 during domain sign-off on sov-k3w. sov-k3w closed the VALUE-RANGE hole (request_multiplier < 1 refused at validate()). The PARSE-side hole is still open and fails in the worse direction.

prototypes/src/types/recipe.rs:63 reads:
    request_multiplier: get_lua(&table, "request_multiplier").unwrap_or(1),

get_lua returns mlua::Result. .unwrap_or(1) cannot distinguish ABSENT (legitimately honest, default 1) from MALFORMED (a type error). So request_multiplier = "four", or a bool, or a table, at base_mod/companies.lua:40 loads the flour factory as request_multiplier = 1. validate() then sees 1 and passes cleanly. The enterprise silently stops hoarding, the Planner has nothing to detect, and the core loop of the game is deleted with no error, no warning and no failing test.

This is the repo's signature defect shape (silent default on a failed read) landing on the single most load-bearing dial in the design. sov-k3w's own stated rule was 'validation must live where the invariant is CONSUMED, not only where the value is parsed' - this is the same principle applied to the parse side, and the range check cannot substitute for it because the bad value never reaches validate().

The correct form already exists two files over at prototypes/src/prototypes/goods_company.rs:41-42 (get_lua_opt(..)?.unwrap_or(0)), so this is a one-line change, not a design question. Same shape exists at the other unwrap_or read sites listed in the engineering-practice notes (base.rs:17, item.rs:24, zone.rs:20-21) - fixing those too is welcome but request_multiplier is the one that matters for the core loop.

TRAP: prototypes unit tests will not catch this - the bad value produces a VALID prototype. The test must assert the parse ERRORS, using prototypes::try_parse_prototypes (added by sov-k3w) with a non-numeric request_multiplier.
acceptance_criteria: recipe.rs:63 uses get_lua_opt(&table, "request_multiplier")?.unwrap_or(1) so an absent field still defaults to 1 (honest) while a malformed value propagates a PrototypeLoadError. A scenario test in simulation/src/tests/scenarios/validation.rs drives request_multiplier = a non-numeric Lua value through try_parse_prototypes and asserts Err naming the field. Mutation-proven: revert recipe.rs:63 to get_lua(..).unwrap_or(1), watch that test go red, restore. Confirm the 'running N tests' line names the new test.

title: buy_until underflows on the negative capital rows sov-abs makes routine
description:
ledger-invariant-checker latent finding 4, Phase-4 2026-08-28. A landmine, not a live break.

simulation/src/economy/market.rs:421 buy_until computes 'qty - c as u32' where c is a signed capital. When c < 0 this wraps to about 4.29e9 and panics in debug builds. A panic on a live path is a 'never game over' pillar violation.

It was safe before sov-abs because negative capital rows were exceptional. After 7721cdd they are ROUTINE: capital[FreightStation] is deliberately driven negative by exactly the imported quantity -- that negative row IS the import ledger and is why total_qty stays conserved.

Safe TODAY only because nothing calls buy_until or sell_all on a FreightStation soul. That is an accident of the current call graph, not a guard.

Fix: clamp with saturating arithmetic on the signed value before the cast, or make the guard explicit and assert it.
acceptance_criteria: A unit test calls buy_until on a soul with negative capital and asserts a sane order quantity rather than a panic or a ~4.29e9 order. Mutation-prove by restoring the raw subtraction.
close_reason: buy_until clamps negative capital in simulation/src/economy/market.rs + buy_until_negative_capital_orders_sane_qty. sha fa90ebc. Gates green (prototypes 6, simulation 75 passed)

title: Import money leaves at match while the goods arrive later or never
description:
ledger-invariant-checker latent finding 1, Phase-4 2026-08-28. Not a Kornai violation and not a conservation break -- money is still conserved into the external counterparty and never gates a physical flow. But the pairing is gone.

After sov-abs (7721cdd) the goods move physically over many ticks while 'gvt.money += trade.money_delta' still fires at MATCH time (simulation/src/economy/mod.rs:104). Under the old teleport the payment and the delivery were always the same tick, so they could not diverge.

Concrete divergence: demolish the buyer mid-flight. The truck returns the goods to the border, which then holds BOTH the goods and the money.

Fix if wanted: apply an import's money_delta at ToDestination arrival, alongside the buyer credit.

Context from kornai-economist, same gate: there is no affordability check anywhere in the tree -- the only other money sites are world_command.rs:225 (build cost) and economy/mod.rs:54 (wages), and government money may go negative without limit. Imports ration by truck availability and distance, never by willingness to pay. That is CORRECT for this game and must stay so; this ticket is about timing, not about adding a price gate.
acceptance_criteria: Import money_delta applies on Loading arrival, export on ToDestination arrival (match creates commitment only); EcoStats import/export legs prove arrival-tick movement; determinism gate green. Per spec sov-o1w and ADR-0003 §1.
close_reason: commit c252bb7 (landed together per ADR-0003): 8 wave tests red-then-green in isolated worktrees; full suite 71 passed 0 failed; gate green over the 200k fixture; mechanics-index rows flip to EXISTS.

comments.author: caioniehues
comments.text: 2026-09-03 docs review confirms: money_delta applied at match for imports AND exports (mod.rs:103-104) before advance_dispatches (:124-133). Missing border source stock filed separately as sov-uo5.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Code-truth 2026-09-04 CONFIRMED: both halves hit gvt.money at match via mod.rs:104 — import delta built market.rs:651, export :740 — while delivery debits/credits land later (:912/:1060). Domestic/retail/job deltas are ZERO (:544); only border legs are nonzero.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Grill decision 2026-09-04 (ADR-0003 §1): MOVE money to delivery. Import delta applies on Loading arrival (market.rs:912), export on ToDestination arrival (:1060). Match keeps creating the commitment only. LAND-TOGETHER with sov-20g: a moved money leg with teleport exports is worse than today.

title: buy_until ignores in-flight dispatches, so imports stack and hoards amplify
description:
Reported independently by kornai-economist (finding F1) and ledger-invariant-checker (latent finding 3), Phase-4 2026-08-28. Conserved -- this is over-supply, not a leak.

simulation/src/economy/market.rs:421 buy_until reads raw capital and knows nothing about incoming quantity already in flight. A company that re-posts while an import is en route draws a SECOND import from an infinite source.

The same shape exists for domestic supply and predates this diff. What is NEW after sov-abs is that IMPORT supply has no ceiling at all.

ECONOMIC CONSEQUENCE, kornai-economist: this amends the standing sov-lpj ruling that a hoard is bounded at (k-1)*c. That bound now holds ONLY where no reachable station exists. With one, a filled hoarder re-posts each cycle and STACKS imports -- a flour factory with k=4 and amount 1 can have 1+2+3 = 6 units in flight against a target of 4. An honest k=1 enterprise never stacks, because it consumes to 0 and stalls. So the honest=0 / dishonest>0 detection signal SURVIVES and is in fact amplified. Accepted as Kornai-true; kornai-economist has amended its memory.

Fix shape: have buy_until subtract in-flight incoming quantity, which needs an accessor for 'quantity inbound to soul for item'.
acceptance_criteria: A scenario with a reachable station shows a k=4 hoarder holding at most its target across many cycles rather than stacking to 6. The honest-vs-dishonest detection signal must still be non-zero afterwards -- assert both.
close_reason: Wave-2 green (sim suite 96 passed 0 failed). See commits a3e57ce/34358bd-range.

title: Give the freight station its own vehicles; dispatch assignment is unranked FCFS
description:
logistics-modeller Condition D on sov-abs, Phase-4 2026-08-28. Degrades rather than breaks (imports queue in ToSource), so it was not a block.

base_mod/companies.lua gives n_trucks = 1 to FACTORIES only. Stores get zero; freight stations get zero. After sov-abs (7721cdd) imports draw from that same city-wide pool, and they are drawn exactly when domestic supply is ABSENT -- so in a young or shortage-struck city imports dominate dispatch volume. The border round trip is also the longest journey on the map.

Dispatcher::query is FCFS by dispatch index with no ranking at all, which is the classic unprioritised-assignment collapse: long trips crowd out short hops. requirements/movement.md commits to deficit-priority plus meaningful-distance ranking; neither exists.

MITIGATION ACCEPTED, and logistics-modeller notes it is also the modelled answer: give the freight station its own vehicles, matching $VEHICLE_STATION on the Workers and Resources reference install.

kornai-economist reached the same place from the economics side: transport is the binding constraint and is the one the Planner can act on, so the pool composition IS the policy lever.
acceptance_criteria: Freight stations own vehicles declared in base_mod, and a scenario shows a domestic short hop completing while a long import is in flight, on a map where the old shared pool would have starved it.

title: Truck freed without parking at the three Loading exhaustion sites
description:
logistics-modeller's strongest sov-jcl finding, Phase-4 gate 2026-08-28.

simulation/src/economy/market.rs:910 does a bare dispatcher.free(DispatchID::SmallTruck(v)) with no park(). Sibling arms at :951 and :968 share the gap. sov-2c4 established the OPPOSITE convention at the Unloading site (market.rs:1050-1079), whose comment records that an abandoned truck blocks the door's lane for every later dispatch.

The freed truck stays VehicleState::Driving with an ended itinerary and a live TransportGrid collider, stopped in a lane. It re-enters the pool on the next Dispatcher::update; every ToSource query that picks it hits the Parked guard at market.rs:800-804 and frees it again. Net: permanently in the pool, permanently unusable, permanently blocking a lane.

The gap is pre-existing, but sov-jcl (166b1cf) makes it reachable on a much commoner trigger -- any route failure during Loading, which happens transiently whenever the player edits the road.

Possibly related, filed together: logistics-modeller reports a frozen truck at V3(27.565216, 5.249, 0.3) in VehicleState::Driving with desired_speed 0. It ruled that NOT caused by the market diff (neither commit touches road.rs, vehicle.rs, unpark or spawning) and named a stranded zombie truck of exactly this shape as the most likely blocker on this branch. Attach the probe when investigating.

MITIGATION ACCEPTED BY logistics-modeller: reuse the Unloading path -- parking.reserve_near + map_dynamic::router::park, then free -- at all three exhaustion sites.
acceptance_criteria: A scenario driving a dispatch to Loading route-failure exhaustion asserts the freed truck is in VehicleState::Parked and holds no TransportGrid collider, then asserts a SECOND dispatch successfully reserves and uses that same truck. Mutation-prove by reverting to the bare free().
close_reason: Wave-2 green (sim suite 96 passed 0 failed). See commits a3e57ce/34358bd-range.

comments.author: caioniehues
comments.text: 2026-09-03 docs review (economy slice): advance_dispatches now parks then frees at market.rs:1079-1151 - verify whether the three bare free() sites at :910/:951/:968 still exist; if not, close with evidence. Related loss-sink defect filed as sov-bub.

title: Export half of ext-trade still teleports goods across the border
description:
sov-abs (7721cdd) made the IMPORT half of external trade physical. The EXPORT half was out of its scope and still teleports: simulation/src/economy/market.rs:706-733 does '*cap -= qty_sell' at match time with no Dispatch, so goods leave the seller's building and reach the border in the same tick, having moved nowhere. Named independently by kornai-economist, logistics-modeller and ledger-invariant-checker in the Phase-4 gate chain.

Consequences:
- 'Nothing teleports' is currently half true. With zero vehicles on the map, stock still changes hands on the export path.
- Output storage pressure never bites where a reachable station exists, so recipe storage_multiplier production halts are unreachable there (kornai-economist).
- Unlike an import, the export does NOT credit the capital[FreightStation] row, so that row drifts monotonically negative rather than balancing (ledger-invariant-checker).
acceptance_criteria: An export dispatch exists in market.dispatches() with a border-door target; loop order guarantees every pushed trade is iterated; determinism gate green. Per spec sov-o1w and ADR-0003 §2.
close_reason: commit c252bb7 (landed together per ADR-0003): 8 wave tests red-then-green in isolated worktrees; full suite 71 passed 0 failed; gate green over the 200k fixture; mechanics-index rows flip to EXISTS.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Code-truth 2026-09-04 CONFIRMED with mechanism: export debits *cap at match (:730) and gets NO dispatch because the dispatch loop (:658) iterates all_trades[dispatch_start..] BEFORE the export branch pushes (:706-741).

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Grill decision 2026-09-04 (ADR-0003 §2): REAL export dispatch. Fix loop order so the export branch pushes before the dispatch loop iterates; trucks drive seller -> border door. LAND-TOGETHER with sov-7f7.

title: find_external gates the export block on a driving lane it does not need
description:
sov-abs added a DISPATCH_LANE_CUTOFF reachability filter to find_external (simulation/src/economy/mod.rs:71-83). find_external is ONE closure used by BOTH the import block (market.rs:~630) and the seller-surplus export block (market.rs:719).

Imports need a driving lane -- a truck must run. Exports create no Dispatch, need no truck, and run after the dispatch loop. Gating them on a driving lane is over-application and was almost certainly unintended.

Confirmed by the lead at source, 2026-08-28: START_COMMANDS (simulation/src/lib.rs:443+) seeds 10 MapMakeConnection commands with 13 lane patterns, ALL of kind 'Rail' and ZERO 'Driving'. ledger-invariant-checker probed the actual station door at (4297.4, 6315.3) and confirmed nearest_lane(door, Driving, Some(50.0)) == None. So on a fresh map find_external returns None for everything and a new city cannot export at all until the player lays road near the station.

Fix shape: give the export site its own unfiltered lookup, or pass a 'reachable: bool' to the closure and require the lane only on the import side.

Related: this ticket only restores the pre-sov-abs export reach. It does NOT make exports physical -- that is the separate export-teleport ticket, and fixing that one may make this one moot.
acceptance_criteria: An export succeeds on a map whose only freight station has no driving lane within DISPATCH_LANE_CUTOFF, while an import on the same map still correctly refuses. One test asserting both halves.
close_reason: Wave-2 green (sim suite 96 passed 0 failed). See commits a3e57ce/34358bd-range.

comments.author: sim-implementer
comments.text:
BLOCKED on sov-20g. Attempted the ungating (make_trades taking find_external(pos, needs_truck); import passes true, export false) and measured the consequence, then fully reverted it.

A/B on tests::scenarios::hoarding::scenario_0151_inflated_request_hoards_honest_does_not, identical apart from the export gate:
  export gated   -> seller_capital=985  honest=2  inflated=5  PASS
  export ungated -> seller_capital=0    honest=0  inflated=1  FAIL

The seller posts sell(qty 1000, stock 0). With exports ungated, the surplus block at market.rs:~735 hands the whole 1000 to the border in one pass -- instantly, with no Dispatch and no truck (sov-20g: the export half still teleports) -- so the domestic buyers starve from the next tick on (sov-b70: the border out-competes domestic demand). The core-loop hoarding guard is what catches it.

So the gate on exports is currently load-bearing for the wrong reason: it is the only thing suppressing a teleporting export path. Ungating is right, but it must land AFTER exports become physical. Recommend: bd dep sov-20g --blocks sov-nun.

comments.author: main
comments.text:
BLOCKED BY sov-20g, proven by measurement rather than argued. A sim-implementer built the ungating exactly as briefed (make_trades takes find_external: Fn(Vec2, bool), import passes true, export passes false) and it BREAKS THE CORE LOOP. Fully reverted; economy/mod.rs, market.rs and the 8 test call sites are byte-identical to HEAD.

Measured A/B on scenario_0151_inflated_request_hoards_honest_does_not, only the export gate differing:
  export GATED   -> seller_capital=985  honest=2  inflated=5  PASS
  export UNGATED -> seller_capital=0    honest=0  inflated=1  FAIL

Cause: the seller posts sell(qty 1000, stock 0). With exports ungated the surplus block at market.rs:~727 hands the entire 1000 to the border in ONE pass -- instantly, no Dispatch, no truck -- because the export half still teleports (sov-20g). Every domestic buyer starves from the next tick (sov-b70).

So the DISPATCH_LANE_CUTOFF filter is currently LOAD-BEARING for exports, for a reason no gate knew: it is the only thing suppressing a teleporting export path. Ungating is correct in isolation and cannot land until exports are physical.

Correction to the record: the sov-abs comment claiming 'the export half is untouched' is FALSE. find_external is one closure and the export block consumes it too, which is exactly why the gate reaches exports.

title: Dispose of ungated wip/sov-m0q-wave1 branch
description:

Trap: do not merge it. Establish first whether anything on it is still wanted -- much of the sov-m0q wave (sov-abc, sov-uuo, sov-91s, sov-pci, sov-uy2) was redone and closed with real evidence on 2026-08-28, so this branch is likely fully superseded. Check 'git log --oneline main..origin/wip/sov-m0q-wave1' and 'git diff --stat main...origin/wip/sov-m0q-wave1' before assuming any of it is novel.

title: Is any FastMap reachable from a saved resource? Determinism check may compare unstable orderings
description: Raised by researcher 2026-08-28 and explicitly left UNSETTLED - it needs a real walk, not a grep. THE MECHANISM IS CONFIRMED: hashes() at simulation/src/lib.rs:268-276 hashes the SERIALIZED BYTES, and common/src/hash.rs:5 hash_iter hashes in iteration order. So a FastMap (FxHashMap) anywhere inside a type reachable from a saved resource makes the determinism check compare unstable orderings - the guard would be nondeterministic rather than the sim. THE CONVENTION IS ALSO CONFIRMED: serialized sim state is BTreeMap throughout (dispatch.rs:10, electricity.rs:8, ecostats.rs:1, spatial_map.rs:10, economy/mod.rs:19), and the only FastMap uses found in simulation/ are the transient Resources bag (utils/resources.rs:15) and local scratch. WHAT IS NOT CONFIRMED: whether any live instance violates it. Settling this means walking every #[derive(Serialize)] type in simulation/ TRANSITIVELY from each of the 16 saved resources. Related and already open: sov-qi8 records that a FnvHashMap serialize order was not round-trip stable on transport_grid, which is this exact shape having already bitten once. Also relevant: FxHasher output is not stable ACROSS rustc-hash versions and the tree currently carries BOTH 1.1.0 and 2.0.0, so nothing derived from it may be persisted or sent on the wire.
acceptance_criteria: Every type transitively reachable from the 16 saved resources is enumerated and each map/set in them is shown to be order-stable, or the offenders are listed as tickets. The convention is then written down where an implementer will read it.
close_reason: Settled by transitive walk (see comment): one unstable container, transport_grid FnvHashMap cells; handled in commit 7e771ce via transport_grid_equal. No FxHash-derived data is persisted.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Settled 2026-09-03 by a transitive walk of all 15 saved resources + World from init.rs registrations. ONE hit: transport_grid (init.rs:135) = flat_spatial::Grid whose SparseStorage.cells is fnv::FnvHashMap<CellIdx,GridCell> (flat_spatial-0.6.1 storage.rs:31). Everything else is BTreeMap/Vec/HopSlotMap. Consequence proven in sov-n8v: with the real schedule, test_world_survives_serde goes RED at tick 3952 in the deser-vs-sim branch on transport_grid with byte blobs that are a pure permutation (same 666 bytes, same multiset). Simulation behaviour is order-independent (query_around walks an XY range, not the map), so this is a comparison artefact, not sim nondeterminism. Fix in sov-n8v: order-insensitive transport_grid_equal fallback in is_equal. rustc-hash 1.1.0 and 2.0.0 both in Cargo.lock; nothing FxHash-derived is persisted.

title: par_command_buffer runs exec closures for entities killed in the same drain
description: Found by researcher 2026-08-28. Status: PROVED at source. simulation/src/utils/par_command_buffer.rs:50-83 runs exec closures for entities that were killed during the SAME drain, with no liveness check. WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE BUG: agents in this repo have repeatedly used "the command buffer drains kills first" as a SAFETY ARGUMENT when reasoning about deferred work - it is how a deferred closure is assumed not to touch a dead entity. That argument is false, and any conclusion resting on it needs re-checking. This is the deferred-execution seam that sov-6qx, sov-2c4 and sov-7pg all live in: exec_ent runs at the ParCommandBuffer flush, one tick after the decision that queued it. TRAP: do not "fix" this by adding a liveness check to every closure - find out whether the drain ordering should change, or whether exec_ent should skip dead entities centrally, and check what currently DEPENDS on the closure running.
acceptance_criteria: Either the drain refuses to run exec closures for entities killed in the same pass, or every deferred-exec call site is audited and the ones that need liveness get it. A test kills an entity and queues an exec for it in the same tick and asserts the defined behaviour. Any doc or agent memory asserting the old safety argument is corrected.
close_reason: ParCommandBuffer::apply centrally skips exec for dead entities in simulation/src/utils/par_command_buffer.rs + same_tick_kill_skips_exec. sha fa90ebc. Gates green

comments.author: ParBufferLive
comments.text: ParBufferLive: central skip landed in par_command_buffer.rs only. Audit note for reviewers: Transporter::destroy closures (router walk_inside, road parking-complete) free an already-detached grid handle, so a same-drain kill-after-detach would strand one handle under the skip. No HumanEnt kill path exists; VehicleEnt needs company-teardown kill in the exact drain a truck finishes parking. Rare, accepted, documented inline.

title: worldsend receive buffer is unbounded: every fragment re-reads data_size and extends
description: Found by researcher 2026-08-28 reading networking/ at source. Status: read from source, NOT reproduced - multiplayer is off by default (native_app default features = []). networking/src/worldsend.rs WorldReceive::handle re-reads `data_size` from EVERY inbound fragment and `extend`s the accumulator WITHOUT checking the total against any bound. Every field of an inbound packet is peer-controlled, so a malicious or malformed peer can grow the receive buffer without limit. TWO SIBLING DEFECTS in the same crate, same root - do not panic on peer-controlled input, because a server panic ends the game for EVERY player, which is the never-game-over pillar at multiplayer scale: (1) networking/src/server/server_playout.rs:85 `.expect("lag is too big")` kills the server whenever any single client falls past the ring buffer - bound it and disconnect that one client instead; (2) networking/src/catchup.rs:39 logs "wrong input for catch up !!!" and then PUSHES THE INPUT ANYWAY - a desync must refuse, not log. Also worth knowing while in this crate: socket threads .unwrap() their sends (connections.rs:129,147,164,173; connection_client.rs:90,108,117,125), so a panic there kills the loop silently while the game still looks alive. BUILD CHECK: `cargo check -p native_app --features multiplayer` - an ordinary cargo check compiles none of this.
acceptance_criteria: The accumulated receive length is bounded and a peer exceeding it is disconnected, not accommodated; server_playout no longer expects on client lag; catchup refuses a wrong input instead of pushing it. Each proven by a test feeding the hostile input.

title: get_lua swallows TYPE errors as absence: a mistyped request_multiplier silently reads as honest
description: Found by researcher 2026-08-28, proven by probe (see .claude/agent-memory/substrate-cartographer/seam-data-layer-2026-08-27.md). SIX sites in prototypes/ use `get_lua(t, "field").unwrap_or(default)`, which cannot distinguish a MISSING field from a field of the wrong TYPE. Concrete: `request_multiplier = "not-a-number"` parses as 1. And 1 means HONEST - so a typo silently deletes the dishonest-enterprise loop, the core mechanic of the game, with no warning anywhere. The correct form already exists two files over: `get_lua_opt(t, "field")?.unwrap_or(default)` at prototypes/src/prototypes/goods_company.rs:41-42, which propagates a type error and only defaults on true absence. The crate is 6-to-2 against itself. Authority: Rust API Guidelines C-VALIDATE and C-GOOD-ERR (https://rust-lang.github.io/api-guidelines/checklist.html). RELATED silent-default sites the same researcher found outside this crate, worth sweeping in the same pass: simulation/src/init.rs:233-240 logs and returns on a failed resource load, leaving the default in place, and Deserialize for Simulation (lib.rs:428-439) returns Ok(sim) regardless - 16 resources cross that seam and exactly ONE post-load guard exists (lib.rs:289, map size).

title: unpark refusal at router.rs:218 may strand a Driver human in a parking truck
description: Found by opus reviewer 2026-08-28 gating sov-6qx. Status: PLAUSIBLE, not proven - the reviewer could not build the reproduction and said so. simulation/src/map_dynamic/router.rs:218-227: on unpark refusal the router logs at debug and lets the routing plan continue, but the plan has ALREADY popped the Unpark step and the next step is DriveTo(vehicle, ...). SCENARIO: a WorkKind::Driver human takes a company truck as its router vehicle (souls/desire/work.rs:60 SetVehicle(Some(truck))). If a dispatch left that truck in RoadToPark, the OLD code force-set it to Driving - leaking a collider but moving - while the NEW code leaves it parking. vehicle_state_update (transportation/road.rs:108-125) then completes the park, and cur_step_over for DriveTo requires x.it.has_ended(0.0) (router.rs:145-150), which a parked truck itinerary never reaches. The human sits in Location::Vehicle until some later dispatch happens to drive that truck. THE TRADE IS STILL CORRECT: "phantom lane blocker" (old) for "possibly stalled rider" (new) is the better trade, and the phantom was a permanent non-escalating stall invisible to the planner. This ticket is about closing the remaining half. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a scenario test that puts a truck in RoadToPark, gives a Driver human that truck, and ticks the route to completion. Never-game-over applies: a stalled rider must degrade into a retry or a walk, not a permanent wait.
acceptance_criteria: Either a scenario test proves the stall cannot happen, or the router handles a refused Unpark by re-planning (walk, wait-and-retry, or release the vehicle) rather than proceeding to a DriveTo that can never complete. Mutation-proven either way.
close_reason: Wave-2 green (sim suite 96 passed 0 failed). See commits a3e57ce/34358bd-range.

title: One global 30% GPU-timing tolerance lets a 29% ssao regression pass
description: Found by opus reviewer 2026-08-28 gating sov-91s (finding F5), proved by mutating the real artifact. A 31.6% regression in the main pass is correctly REJECTED ("main median 121.230us exceeds 119.756us", exit 1). But a 29% regression in ssao PASSES (exit 0) - and ssao measured spread is min 33.480 / max 33.800, about 1%. A 29% move in ssao is ~29 standard deviations of its real noise and the gate does not blink. ROOT CAUSE: the rationale at engine_demo/gpu_timing_baselines/radv-navi3x/baseline.json:12 justifies 30% from the MAIN pass spread alone, then applies that one number to all nine passes. sov-91s acceptance said "tolerance justified from measured spread"; that is met for main only.

title: --gpu-samples overshoot makes the evidence file state a sample count it did not take
description: Found by opus reviewer 2026-08-28 gating sov-91s (finding F6). engine/src/framework.rs:299-302 clamps the GPU-timing arming window to warmup_frames + 1. PROVED: --gpu-samples 200 writes "sample_frames": 200 into the record and the policy string "... on the 200 frames ending with the captured frame", while every pass reports samples: 91. The evidence file states something false about how it was produced. WORSE, the clamped window also swallows warm-up frames: main median came back 71.3us against a 92.120us baseline - exactly the cold-GPU contamination that warmup_frames exists to prevent, so an overshooting --gpu-samples silently produces FASTER-looking numbers. Anyone tuning that flag upward gets a better result and a lying artifact.
acceptance_criteria: Either the requested sample count is honoured, or the request is rejected with a concrete reason; in no case does the record report a sample_frames the run did not take. A run with --gpu-samples above the window is seen failing or reporting the true count.

CONCRETE: a new render pass writes fbos without a barrier, producing a genuinely new and real hazard, and the gate still prints "0 new". The gate then certifies a regression it was built to catch.
acceptance_criteria: Allow-list entries match the full message identity (resource and pass included), not the bare signature; a synthetic new WRITE-AFTER-WRITE on a different resource is seen making the gate FAIL.

title: test_world_survives_serde proves only the RESOURCE half of determinism; World is invisible to is_equal
description: Found by the opus reviewer 2026-08-28 gating sov-myg (commit 7fa08e8). The sov-myg fix is correct and merged-ready - this is the SCOPE of what it can prove. Simulation::is_equal (simulation/src/lib.rs:214-232) iterates saveload_funcs(), which registers RESOURCES only (simulation/src/init.rs:224-237). World is not among them; the proof is hashes() at simulation/src/lib.rs:268-272, which has to encode self.world separately precisely because no saveload func covers it. CONCRETE CONSEQUENCE: a component or entity-state divergence between sim and sim2 produces no "not equal" line at all, divergence_tick stays None, and the test exits GREEN. Pre-existing, out of sov-myg scope. UNTIL THIS IS FIXED, nobody may cite test_world_survives_serde as proof of full repeat-run determinism - only of resource determinism.
acceptance_criteria: is_equal covers World (or a sibling check does), and an ECS-only divergence - mutate a component in sim2, leave every resource identical - is seen turning the test RED with the tick named.
close_reason: commit 7e771ce: is_equal encodes self.world with Bincode after the resource loop and dumps world_a/b.json on mismatch. comments.author: engine-implementer
comments.text:
B2 + F12 RESOLVED, commit 365001e. Ticket NOT closed.

B2: tools/run_validation_gate.py passed on zero input. No minimum-message assertion, and it never read the capture record's own validation_requested flag (which engine/src/capture.rs:180 already emits). Forget --validation, or run where VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation is absent, and the gate reported success while proving nothing.

  python3 tools/run_validation_gate.py --allowlist engine_demo/validation_allowlists/radv-navi3x.txt --artifact <empty> -- python3 -c "print('capture ok')"
  before -> PASS validation messages: 0 allowed, 0 new   EXIT=0
  after  -> FAIL validation cannot be confirmed: the command produced 0 validation messages and no --capture-record was given.   EXIT=2

The gate now needs one of two independent confirmations, and fails loudly with the reason when it gets neither: (a) --capture-record <json> whose device.validation_requested is true -- a missing, unparseable or flag-less record is a hard failure, exit 2; or (b) at least one observed validation message. (a) is what still lets a genuinely clean run pass.

F12 (2 lines, same function): the child exit code was returned before the new-message check, so a run that both failed and emitted a new hazard never listed the hazard.
  before -> FAIL validation command exited 3
  after  -> FAIL validation messages: 0 allowed, 1 new / '  - SYNC-HAZARD-READ-AFTER-WRITE new' / FAIL validation command exited 3

4 tests added; python3 -m unittest discover -s tools -> Ran 10 tests, OK (was 6).

Live gated run still passes on AMD RX 7800 XT / RADV NAVI32:
  PASS validation messages: 10 allowed, 0 new   EXIT=0

COUNT WARNING for whoever writes the next gate: that is 10, not the 15 this ticket's text claims. The 5 vkGetDeviceProcAddr warnings are environment-dependent. Do not encode any fixed message count as an invariant.

NOT DONE HERE, deliberately: no caller wires this gate up. grep for 'run_validation_gate' across *.md/*.toml/*.yml/*.sh/*.rs returns nothing -- the gate is undiscoverable (reviewer's F8), out of my scope.

comments.author: engine-implementer
comments.text:
N1 RESOLVED, commit b0aeb97. Ticket still NOT closed.

REPRODUCED the reviewer's finding exactly before fixing it. --capture-record was a free-floating path with no tie to the child's own output:
  gate --artifact stale-art.txt --capture-record <older validated>/baseline.json -- engine_demo capture --out <fresh dir>
  before -> PASS validation messages: 0 allowed, 0 new  EXIT=0
  and that run's OWN record said "validation_requested": false
  after  -> FAIL validation gate: capture record ... was last written at 2026-08-28 03:23:49, before this run started at 2026-08-28 03:39:06; it describes a different run and proves nothing about this one  EXIT=2

FIX SHAPE, and why I took the reviewer's SECOND-choice option: the gate stamps a start time before spawning the child and refuses any record whose mtime predates it (floored to the second, so coarse filesystem timestamp granularity cannot fail a record written during the run). I did NOT resolve the record from the child's output directory, which the reviewer preferred. That would require parsing --out and --scene back out of engine_demo's argv, coupling a general-purpose command wrapper to one binary's CLI; rename either flag, or add a second consumer, and the gate silently stops binding anything with nothing failing. An mtime binds just as tightly and knows nothing about the child. The trade-off is recorded in the function docstring so it is not re-litigated.

MY OWN TEST WAS PART OF THE DEFECT. test_a_clean_run_passes_when_the_capture_record_proves_validation_ran hand-wrote {"device":{"validation_requested":true}} before the run and asserted PASS -- it encoded the hole as the expected behaviour. That test and test_refuses_a_capture_record_that_did_not_request_validation now have the CHILD write its own record, as engine_demo does. Added test_refuses_a_capture_record_older_than_the_run with the mtime backdated an hour. Seen failing against the pre-N1 gate: AssertionError: 0 != 2.

python3 -m unittest discover -s tools -> Ran 11 tests, OK (was 10). Live correct invocation still passes: PASS validation messages: 10 allowed, 0 new, EXIT=0 on AMD RX 7800 XT / RADV NAVI32.

GENERAL LESSON worth more than the fix: both B2 and N1 are the same defect -- a gate trusting an input the operator supplies out of band. The first fix added the input; the second bound it. When adding a proof-of-provenance argument, bind it to the run in the same commit, or it is only a new place to be wrong.

STILL OPEN AND ADJACENT: F8. Nothing in the repo documents or invokes this gate -- grep for run_validation_gate across *.md/*.toml/*.yml/*.sh/*.rs is still empty. An argument nobody has been shown how to pass is an argument that will be got wrong.

The decision it feeds: whether and how to safely lift the user-present rule.

title: [bug] Depth-stencil layout transition races the attachment storeOp: 10x SYNC-HAZARD-WRITE-AFTER-WRITE on RADV
description:
Vulkan validation reports WRITE_AFTER_WRITE on every capture run, saturating the layer's duplicate_message_limit of 10. Reproduced on AMD Radeon RX 7800 XT (RADV NAVI32) 2026-08-28.

REPRO (needs the engine capture work from Chain D; see sov-uy2):
  cargo build --release -p engine_demo
  ./target/release/engine_demo capture --scene baseline --gpu-timings --validation --out target/renderer-evidence

TWO SHAPES, reported together:

(1) vkCmdPipelineBarrier writes VkImage 0xdaf0000000daf, previously written at the end of subpass 0 (vkCmdEndRenderPass) by the attachment storeOp. No synchronisation ensures the layout transition does not conflict with a prior VK_ACCESS_2_DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT_WRITE_BIT at VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_2_LATE_FRAGMENT_TESTS_BIT. Layer hint: srcStageMask must include LATE_FRAGMENT_TESTS and srcAccessMask must include DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT_WRITE.

(2) The mirror image: vkCmdEndRenderPass writes a resource previously written by a layout transition from vkCmdPipelineBarrier. Current synchronisation allows DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT_READ at EARLY|LATE_FRAGMENT_TESTS and SHADER_READ at FRAGMENT/VERTEX/COMPUTE, but must allow DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT_WRITE at LATE_FRAGMENT_TESTS.

TRAP -- do not repeat the mistake this ticket exists to correct. sov-abc was filed on the hypothesis that its query-slot UB was 'likely the unexplained validation hazard'. A controlled before/after capture REFUTED that: 10 hazards before the 94-line repair, 10 after, same adapter, both 'capture ok'. Do not assume any other GPU defect explains this one. Prove it with the count from a real capture.

The depth prepass and shadow cascade passes are the obvious suspects -- the capture reports passes depth_prepass, pbr_prepass, shadow_cascade_0..3, ssao, fog, main, background, ui_blur, gui -- but that is a starting point, not a finding.

Scope: engine/ render passes and their barriers. Owner lane: engine-implementer.
acceptance_criteria: A capture run with --validation on the RX 7800 XT reports ZERO SYNC-HAZARD-WRITE-AFTER-WRITE errors, shown by the same grep -c that measured 10 before the fix. The before-count and after-count are both pasted into the close reason. The fix is a real barrier or pass-ordering correction, not a suppression of the validation layer or a disabling of --validation. Captures still exit 'capture ok' and per-pass GPU timings remain non-zero.

title: Wire the sov-bo3 OOM memory guard to something that runs it
description:
wiring-auditor finding H4 on the sov-bo3 gate, 2026-08-27.

The regression guard for the sov-bo3 OOM lives at simulation/src/map/procgen/building.rs as placement_stress::gen_exterior_house_8m_100k_placements. It is #[ignore]d and NOTHING runs it.

MEASURED, not assumed:
  $ cargo test -p simulation placement_stress
  test map::procgen::building::placement_stress::gen_exterior_house_8m_100k_placements ... ignored
  test result: ok. 0 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored; 0 measured; 45 filtered out

The repository has exactly ONE workflow, .github/workflows/dependency-policy.yml, and its own header forbids the fix: 'Scope is deliberately one job with one check. Do NOT add build, test, packaging or release steps here (sov-ztg).' No Makefile, justfile, xtask, or second workflow exists.

WHY THIS MATTERS: the defect it guards is a P1 that OOM-killed the game at 17.6 GB RSS and violates the absolute 'Never game over' pillar. Without a runner, the crash can return silently and only a second player-facing crash will reveal it.

GOOD NEWS WORTH KEEPING: the test is real and selectable. 'cargo test -p simulation placement_stress -- --ignored --list' prints exactly 1 test. This is NOT the zero-test-green-check trap. It is simply never selected by anything automated.

The guard needs a hard memory ceiling to be meaningful — the capped kill is the evidence, an uncapped run just dies. Reference invocation from the test's own doc comment:
  systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=2G -p MemorySwapMax=0 -- cargo test -p simulation --release placement_stress -- --ignored --nocapture
acceptance_criteria: Some automated runner executes gen_exterior_house_8m_100k_placements under a hard memory ceiling, and a deliberate revert of the iter_keys bound makes that runner go red. Seeing it fail once is required; a runner that has only ever been green proves nothing. Respect the dependency-policy.yml scope rule — add a separate workflow or a documented local command, do not extend that file.

title: Integrate fast_paths strategic route cache behind authoritative A*
description:
Follow-on from the sov-dda.2 spike, which the user KEPT (decision 2026-08-27: keep the spike, do not rework, file a separate integration story).

The spike proved fast_paths 1.0.0 can build a frozen driving-lane snapshot and answer route queries, and that removing a road makes the snapshot stale. It changed no live routing and no movement path. Code lives on branch spike/sov-dda-routes @ 42bd8ca, file simulation/src/map/fast_paths_spike.rs.

TRAP THAT DECIDES THIS TICKET: authoritative lane routing is tick-seeded and the topology is mutable. CarPath (simulation/src/map/pathfinding.rs:189-299) costs each outgoing lane as polyline length / speed_limit PLUS a deterministic randu seeded on hash(start_lane, tick). A contraction hierarchy over static weights cannot reproduce that. So fast_paths must NEVER replace authoritative routing and must never weaken deterministic tie-breaking.

SHAPE THE logistics-modeller RATIFIED: a separately serialized strategic cache over an explicit stable lane/turn mapping, built from a NAMED map revision and static weights. Use it ONLY to rank candidate destinations or to seed a route BEFORE the current authoritative Itinerary validation runs. Preserve current A* for dynamic congestion, road edits, lane authorization, turn legality, and the final Traversable path. Invalidate and rebuild on any topology or static-weight change; never silently serve a stale cache. Canonicalize ties by stable domain IDs — CH output order is not proof of replay equivalence.

PILLAR: no stock, dispatch, vehicle or position may change as a result of a cache lookup. Nothing teleports.

NOTE ON fast_paths ITSELF: it requires consecutive node IDs and re-preparation after topology or edge-weight changes, and its README states duplicate edges keep only the lowest weight.
acceptance_criteria:
A test named sov_dda_fast_paths_frozen_cache passes. Invoke it by FULL MODULE PATH, not leaf name:

  cargo test -p simulation <full::module::path>::sov_dda_fast_paths_frozen_cache -- --exact

WHY THE FULL PATH: libtest --exact matches the full module path. Verified on this repo 2026-08-27: 'cargo test -p simulation sov_dda_fast_paths -- --exact' selects 0 tests, prints 'test result: ok', and EXITS 0. A leaf-name --exact criterion is unfalsifiable and passes forever without running anything. Confirm with -- --list before trusting any green run.

The test must assert all three: (1) replay hash unchanged versus authoritative tick-seeded routing, (2) every returned path is a physically valid Traversable sequence, (3) a stale cache is detected and rebuilt after one road edit.

Measured evidence recorded for build time, query latency, memory, and rebuild cost after one road edit. Adopt only if those measurements beat current routing AND replay hashes match; otherwise reject integration and keep the benchmark as evidence.

comments.author: soviet-authenticity
comments.text:
Phase 0 soviet-authenticity presentation ruling (verified 2026-08-27, HEAD 0aa5c35).

RULING: PROCEED with one existing egui Inspect window. A selected Company or FreightStation can be planner-readable without changing the player-facing Yakui HUD. The current path is game_loop::State::render_gui -> debug_gui::render_oldgui -> debug_inspector (native_app/src/game_loop.rs:251-254; native_app/src/debug_gui/hud.rs:12-24). debug_inspector already reads InspectedEntity and renders Company/FreightStation through Inspect, then preserves the selected entity (native_app/src/debug_gui/debug_inspect.rs:17-40, 44-82). It already has Capital, Buy orders, and Sell orders sections (debug_inspect.rs:130-177). The Yakui new_inspector explicitly returns when DebugState::debug_inspector is enabled, so it remains unchanged (native_app/src/gui/inspect/mod.rs:19-60). Existing Yakui building inspection already demonstrates useful physical reads for workers, productivity, power, progress, storage, waiting cargo, wanted cargo, and train states (native_app/src/gui/inspect/inspect_building.rs:111-260).

PRESENTATION CONSTRAINTS:
1. Keep the existing egui Inspect window and input/render path. Do not add imgui-rs or a third UI stack. Do not alter Yakui HUD or player-facing inspect panels.
2. Present one selected entity as an official report: stable section order, concise two-column labels and values, restrained headings. Avoid raw Debug dumps as the main readout. Keep Follow and entity links.
3. Prefer authoritative physical state: Company identity/prototype, production progress, workers/max workers, driver/trucks when available, storage and market orders; or FreightStation waiting/wanted cargo and train states. Do not invent quotas, prices, or abstract success states. Domestic clearing is not price UI.
4. Match the art direction: institutional, terse text; industrial sans; muted concrete/olive/ochre/oxide signal colours. At RTS zoom, value separation and readable silhouette beat decorative detail. Avoid pure white/black surfaces and bright arcade defaults (docs/reference/art-direction.md:20-31, 43-49).
5. Visual proof is required. Capture the running game with one selected company or freight station, show the report open while live values remain legible, and provide a 15-20 second video watched back before completion (CLAUDE.md:127-129; docs/process/development-cycle.md:267-268). The frame must prove the inspector, not only a clean build.

SIGN-OFF STATUS: source-based Phase 0 approval only. No visual sign-off is possible until the implementation supplies the inspected screenshot/video. Decision after proof: retain the pattern if the report is legible and physically grounded; reject or file a panel story if it is cluttered, toy-like, or detached from live state.

FUTURE VISUAL-PROOF COMMAND: run the focused native_app check/build required by the implementation, then launch the normal game target and capture the selected Company/FreightStation inspector for 15-20 seconds; watch the recording back. Do not treat a clean build as visual proof.

title: Prototype A/B Street-style lane queues for a truck convoy
description: Build a pure one-lane lead/follower queue prototype beside the current vehicle model. Scope: fixed truck convoy scenario only. Trap: keep physical positions, finite vehicle identities, dispatch custody, and deterministic ordering; do not import A/B Street simulation, map, or UI crates.
acceptance_criteria: A fixed convoy scenario compares current behavior with explicit queued and wake states. It records tick cost and a visible queue outcome. Decision: adopt a bounded lane-queue story, reject, or file a named traffic defect.
close_reason: Spike answered, prototype NOT adopted. Preserved as tag archive/sov-dda-3-lane-queues (38bf942); branch and worktree removed. The result is a NEGATIVE and that is its value: the no-queue baseline -- each vehicle braking independently for the nearest object ahead, the shape of road.rs calc_front_dist/calc_decision -- ALSO avoids overlap. Spacing is not what a queue layer buys. It buys nameable state: queue membership, WaitingToAdvance at a blocked exit, and wake events, which the baseline reports as 0 and 0 by construction. COST: 1.48 us/tick queued vs 0.65 us/tick baseline, 5 trucks over 1000 ticks, debug build -- about 2.3x, because it re-sorts each lane every tick. That O(n log n) per lane per tick sort is the one real integration risk and must be designed out before any adoption. The ticket's traps held: VehicleState, Dispatcher, DispatchID and Market appear in the diff only inside doc comments, git diff is empty for vehicle.rs, dispatch.rs and market.rs, ordering is BTreeMap<VehicleID,_> with front_dist descending and VehicleID tie-break, and state round-trips byte-stably through common::saveload::Bincode. Guards seen failing under mutation: a placement mutation advanced a follower 60 m in one tick against a 0.352 m cap; handing a queued follower's cargo to its leader turned the test red. Full suite green, 45 passed + 1 passed.

comments.author: logistics-modeller
comments.text: Phase 0 ruling: SOUND as a bounded one-lane queue controller beside the current vehicle model; REJECT any implementation that makes queue wake-up equal teleportation. Current trucks have finite VehicleID identity and Parked/Driving/Panicking/RoadToPark state (simulation/src/transportation/vehicle.rs:16-24); only Driving/Panicking vehicles with a TransportGrid collider are moved (simulation/src/transportation/road.rs:40-78,140-161). Current collision behavior uses physical Transform, speed, route objective, front distance, and deterministic gridlock flags; blocked vehicles stop and may enter Panicking, not despawn (road.rs:190-241). A/B Street's documented lead/follower model is useful for queue membership and wake events, but it assumes instant speed changes and exact lane-queue positions (https://a-b-street.github.io/docs/tech/trafficsim/discrete_event/index.html, sections Vehicles, Queued, Exact positions), so do not import its simulation/map/UI stack or replace this fork's kinematics. Accept: fixed convoy prototype with serializable queue state; stable ordering by VehicleID (or another explicit stable key); leader/follower links rebuilt deterministically; wake only changes permission/state, while Transform, Itinerary, TransportGrid collider, acceleration, stopping distance, and lane traversal remain authoritative. Dispatch custody must remain on Market::Dispatch.truck through ToSource/Loading/ToDestination/Unloading/Returning (simulation/src/economy/market.rs:728-1005); queueing cannot release/reserve a truck, debit/credit stock, or move goods. Zero trucks means no quantity movement. A blocked queue must remain a visible finite-vehicle bottleneck and preserve shortage behavior. Required future nonzero test filter: cargo test -p simulation sov_dda_lane_queue_convoy -- --exact (must assert stable IDs/order, positive physical movement only after wake, no overlap, dispatch custody, and replay hash equality). Reject if followers are placed at computed lane endpoints without traversing, if queue state is non-serializable/non-deterministic, or if it bypasses existing gridlock/parking/dispatch transitions.

comments.author: substrate-cartographer
comments.text: Phase 0 substrate map, verified 2026-08-27 at commit 0aa5c35b40fddb9dab6b6763c983d7bd1cc81c83. Lead warning: no current lane-queue or lead/follower state exists. PROVIDED: VehicleState has Parked(SpotReservation), Driving, Panicking(GameInstant), RoadToPark(Spline3,f32,SpotReservation) at simulation/src/transportation/vehicle.rs:15-22. Vehicle owns wait_time, kind, flag, and state at :33-45; VehicleKind::Truck width=6.0, acceleration=2.5, deceleration=6.0, speed_factor=0.8 at :60-95. Each active vehicle has stable VehicleID and optional Transporter grid handle; make_vehicle_entity creates the entity and collider at vehicle.rs:159-179. TransportGrid stores position, direction, speed, radius, height, group, flag and synchronizes from vehicles at transportation/mod.rs:48-72,87-105. vehicle_decision_system iterates world.vehicles and calls vehicle_decision only when collider exists at transportation/road.rs:15-37; vehicle_decision queries neighbors in 12m + stopping-distance radius at :40-78. calc_front_dist uses radii and a forward cone, ignores behind/other-direction objects, and returns closest front distance plus flag at road.rs:299-407. calc_decision stops at front_dist < 0.8m + stop_dist, records gridlock flags, and can enter Panicking after a repeated blocked identity at road.rs:185-241. This is collision/spacing avoidance, not an explicit lane queue. Vehicle Transform is authoritative; Itinerary update moves Transform by speed*DELTA every tick at map_dynamic/itinerary.rs:415-425. Lane ownership is inferred from Itinerary traversal and geometry, not stored on Vehicle; Itinerary::route picks nearest start/end lanes at itinerary.rs:95-140. DISPATCH CUSTODY: Dispatcher.update registers every VehicleKind::Truck in one SmallTruck pool at map_dynamic/dispatch.rs:82-105. DispatchOne keeps BTreeMap positions, BTreeMap<LaneID,Vec<DispatchID>>, BTreeSet reserved_by at :42-49; register projects positions onto lanes at :153-200; query walks predecessor lanes and skips reserved IDs at :220-289. Market Dispatch has truck: Option<VehicleID> and states ToSource, Loading, ToDestination, Unloading, Returning at economy/market.rs:162-197. Goods remain held by dispatch between physical arrival transitions at :162-177. advance_dispatches assigns only an available parked truck, routes it, then calls unpark; RoadToPark is rejected and freed at market.rs:764-814. Unloading/Returning parks the truck before dispatcher.free at market.rs:964-1043. DETERMINISM: DispatchID derives Ord and dispatcher uses BTreeMap/BTreeSet at dispatch.rs:27-49. World schedule is fixed SeqSchedule; Simulation::tick applies commands, increments time, then executes it at lib.rs:137-145,235-261. Vehicle loops use world.vehicles.iter_mut and expose no stable queue order at road.rs:21-37,86-96. PURE PROTOTYPE SEAM: standalone one-lane queue model around VehicleID, LaneID, distance_along, and queue state. Keep it beside current model. Use TestCtx::new/build_roads: terrain_size=1 and one road per point window via LanePatternBuilder::default at simulation/src/tests/mod.rs:19-49. For real parked trucks, inflation scenario uses a connected 250m road and spawn_parked_vehicle at tests/scenarios/inflation.rs:142-160,208-221, but it is heavier than needed. Active dispatcher fixture dispatch_one_register_one_works is at map_dynamic/dispatch.rs:311-378; it uses rail IDs, so copy the fixture shape only. tests/vehicles.rs is block-commented at :1 and is dead evidence. A future pure test can build one-way no-parking road, make fixed VehicleIDs with make_vehicle_entity, and call pure queue transitions. Verify tie-break ordering, physical spacing, and unchanged Market/Dispatcher. LUA: base_mod/roadvehicles.lua declares simple_car and simple_truck; simple_truck max_speed=22.0, acceleration=6.0, deceleration=10.0 at lines 1-24. companies.lua gives flour-factory and cereal-farm n_trucks=1 at lines 25-61. REFERENCE: official A/B Street docs describe discrete-event vehicle states Crossing, WaitingToAdvance, Queued; followers register behind leaders; front vehicles wake followers after fully vacating the old lane. Exact positions are bounded by leader front position + vehicle length + fixed following distance; a laggy head remains until its back clears. https://a-b-street.github.io/docs/tech/trafficsim/discrete_event/index.html. Use behavior as reference only. Do not import A/B Street map, UI, or simulation crates. TRAPS: current model is fixed-timestep continuous movement with acceleration, so queue states are a parallel pure prototype. title: Spike fast_paths on a frozen strategic road graph
description: Benchmark fast_paths contraction hierarchies against current route search on a fixed road topology and fixed route query suite. Scope: isolated simulation benchmark only. Trap: authoritative lane routing has dynamic costs and road edits; this spike must not replace it or weaken deterministic tie-breaking.
acceptance_criteria: Report build time, query latency, memory, invalidation cost after one road edit, and replay-hash equivalence. Decision: cache only strategic frozen routes, reject, or create a separate integration story.

Evidence: commit 42bd8ca on branch spike/sov-dda-routes; 'cargo test -p simulation map::fast_paths_spike::tests::sov_dda_fast_paths -- --exact' returns '1 passed; 0 failed' (re-run and verified by lead, not merely claimed). The spike changed no live routing and no movement path. Integration work continues in sov-oiu.

comments.author: substrate-cartographer
comments.text:
Phase 0 substrate-cartographer fact-sheet (read-only; verified 2026-08-27 at commit 0aa5c35b40fddb9dab6b6763c983d7bd1cc81c83).

WHAT WOULD MAKE THE BRIEF WRONG: current vehicle routing is lane-level, tick-seeded, and topology is mutable. fast_paths must not replace authoritative routing or be treated as a static all-purpose graph.

PROVIDED: CarPath in simulation/src/map/pathfinding.rs:189-299 runs directed A* from a dummy/start lane to an end LaneID. Successors are turns from the current lane (lines 221-243); each outgoing lane cost is lane polyline length / speed_limit plus deterministic randu(dist_from_bottom bits XOR hash(start_lane,tick)) (lines 208-219, 233-242). The heuristic is Euclidean distance to end intersection * 1.2 / default speed limit (204-217). It returns Traversable turn+lane pairs (246-268). It authorizes Driving/Bus only (271-298); Rail delegates to CarPath (163-186). Pedestrian uses a separate A* over Traversable with lane length and 0.001 turn costs (73-136).

TOPOLOGY: Lane has stable-in-run LaneID, parent RoadID, directed src/dst intersections, kind, speed_limit, polyline, and dist_from_bottom (simulation/src/map/objects/lane.rs:63-80). Road::make creates lanes from LanePattern and direction (objects/road.rs:70-124); default pattern is one 9.0-speed driving lane each way plus sidewalks/parking (lane.rs:124-133, 184-225). Intersection stores roads sorted by angle and turns in BTreeSet (objects/intersection.rs:22-35, 52-61); turns are regenerated on invalidation (intersection.rs:91-106; map.rs:424-462).

ROUTE CALLERS: Itinerary::route first finds nearest start/end lanes, uses local_route when same lane, otherwise calls PathKind::path and builds reversed route (simulation/src/map_dynamic/itinerary.rs:95-168). Vehicle routes are requested by market dispatch at market.rs:328-335, 790-809, 864-875, and 881-896. Rail routes are requested by souls/freight_station.rs:112-120 and 153-160. random_route calls Itinerary::route at itinerary.rs:257-275. Graph query corroborated route/random_route nodes but missed external callers; source grep is authoritative. The legacy simulation/src/tests/vehicles.rs is entirely block-commented (lines 1-158), so it is not executable coverage.

DYNAMIC BOUNDARY: Road edits mutate graph structure. remove_road removes lanes, updates intersections, parking/lots, and calls invalidate on both endpoints (map.rs:331-382). split_road removes/recreates lanes and roads, then invalidates source/destination/new intersection (map.rs:487-517). make_connection creates roads/lanes, updates intersection adjacency and callers invalidate endpoints (map.rs:150-214). invalidate recalculates interfaces, lane geometry, traffic controls, and turns (map.rs:424-462). There is no topology revision or routing-cache invalidation API in Map. Runtime traffic is not an A* edge cost: vehicle_decision uses TransportGrid neighbors, speed/deceleration, signals and gridlock/panicking state (transportation/road.rs:15-78, 185-239); Traversable::can_pass checks traffic light control only (map/traversable.rs:57-65). Thus a frozen strategic cache can only cover an explicitly immutable snapshot and must be bypassed/rebuilt after edits; it cannot model congestion or signal state.

DETERMINISM: route choice is deterministic for identical topology, start lane, and Tick because base_random hashes start_lane and tick and randu input is deterministic (pathfinding.rs:219, 237-239). It is intentionally allowed to vary with tick. Successor iteration comes from Intersection.turns BTreeSet (intersection.rs:28, 91-105; turns_from 289-301), but the random lane term is part of tie-breaking. Replay equivalence therefore means same tick/topology/inputs, not one route independent of tick. Preserve lane/turn ordering and route output semantics.

LUA: base_mod/roadvehicles.lua:1-23 declares only two vehicle prototypes: simple_car max_speed 50, acceleration 8, deceleration 12; simple_truck max_speed 22, acceleration 6, deceleration 10. It declares no road topology, lane graph, congestion, or route weights.

REFERENCE: Workers & Resources reference files expose physical road connection directives, not a routing algorithm. For example media_soviet/buildings_types/bulk_engine.ini:45-51 contains  and  directives; bulk_rail_station.ini:35-45 has road connection directives alongside vehicle stations. This supports treating topology/physical connections as distinct from vehicle routing; no reference algorithm claim was made.

FAST_PATHS FIT: official easbar/fast_paths README (https://github.com/easbar/fast_paths) says it uses Contraction Hierarchies for directed graphs with positive non-zero weights; InputGraph must be frozen before use, and FastGraph cannot accept more edges unless thawed. prepare_with_order requires same node count and is intended for similar graphs after a few edge-weight changes. Duplicate edges keep only the lowest weight; self-loops are ignored. This maps only to a separate static strategic graph, not LaneID/TurnID route execution. Build a future isolated benchmark adapter from an immutable snapshot: assign consecutive u32 nodes; use directed lane-to-lane edges with fixed positive weights; query identical start/end lane pairs; compare build time, query latency, memory, one road-edit rebuild/invalidation cost, and route identity/hash against current A*. Do not add dependency or run a large benchmark in Phase 0. Suggested focused command after implementation: cargo test -p simulation fast_paths -- --nocapture --test-threads=1 (must select at least one test).

MUST NOT CHANGE: physical itinerary execution, LaneID/TurnID mapping, dynamic road edit behavior, traffic/signal handling, deterministic tick-seeded choice, or the rule that failed routes remain queued/retried. Side effects: none beyond this Beads comment; no source, dependency, or user files changed.

comments.author: logistics-modeller
comments.text: Phase 0 ruling: SOUND only as a frozen strategic overlay; REJECT as a replacement for authoritative lane routing. Current CarPath is A* over LaneID with positive travel-time cost plus tick/start-seeded tie noise (simulation/src/map/pathfinding.rs:191-268), and Itinerary::route materializes Traversable lanes/turns and reroutes when topology/path points fail (simulation/src/map_dynamic/itinerary.rs:95-168,171-195). fast_paths Contraction Hierarchies requires a frozen graph, positive nonzero weights, consecutive node IDs, and re-preparation after topology or edge-weight changes; its own docs also say duplicate edges keep only the lowest weight (https://github.com/easbar/fast_paths, README). Accept: a separately serialized strategic cache over an explicit stable lane/turn mapping, built from a named map revision and static weights, used only to rank candidate destinations or seed a route before current authoritative Itinerary validation. Preserve current A* for dynamic congestion, road edits, lane authorization, turn legality, and final Traversable path. Invalidate/rebuild on any topology or static-weight change; never silently use a stale cache. Canonicalize ties by stable domain IDs because CH output/tie behavior is not proof of replay equivalence with current tick-seeded routing. No stock, dispatch, vehicle, or position may change from cache lookup. Required future nonzero test filter: cargo test -p simulation sov_dda_fast_paths_frozen_cache -- --exact (must assert unchanged replay hash, physical Traversable validity, and stale-cache invalidation after one road edit). Decision boundary: adopt only if fixed-query latency/memory/build/rebuild measurements are better and replay hashes match; otherwise reject integration and retain the benchmark as evidence.

title: Spike GPU pass profiling on the wgpu compatibility lane
description: Trial a pinned wgpu-profiler release compatible with the current wgpu 0.20.1 renderer, or document why owned timestamp queries are smaller and sufficient. Scope: engine and engine_demo capture only. Trap: current wgpu-profiler targets wgpu 30 and must not introduce a second incompatible wgpu type graph.
acceptance_criteria: A fixed engine_demo capture produces per-pass GPU timing evidence or a reproducible incompatibility result. The result names GPU, driver, Mesa version, scene, and runtime cost. Decision: adopt pinned profiler, retain owned timestamps, or remove spike.
close_reason: Spike answered, code NOT adopted. Preserved as tag archive/sov-dda-1-wgpu-profiler (69ffed1); branch and worktree removed. wgpu-profiler v0.17.0 verified compatible with wgpu 0.20.1 against the pinned crate sources: same Features::TIMESTAMP_QUERY bar, scope() takes &self so it survives the rayon parallel render at gfx.rs:736-763, Cargo.lock gains exactly ONE package, no wgpu duplicate, and it cannot have sov-abc's never-reset-slot UB by construction. comments.author: substrate-cartographer
comments.text:
Phase 0 ground map (verified 2026-08-27 at commit 0aa5c35b40fddb9dab6b6763c983d7bd1cc81c83; read-only, no source or dependency changes):

COMPATIBILITY: engine/Cargo.toml:20 pins wgpu 0.20.1 (default-features=false, wgsl). Cargo.lock resolves wgpu 0.20.1, wgpu-core 0.21.1, wgpu-types 0.20.0. Wumpf/wgpu-profiler tag v0.17.0 Cargo.toml declares wgpu = 0.20.0, so it is the exact candidate compatible with the engine 0.20.x API; v0.16.0 targets wgpu 0.19 and v0.18.0 targets wgpu 22.1.0. Do not use current/latest profiler: v0.28.0 declares wgpu 30.0.0 and would create a second incompatible wgpu type graph. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Wumpf/wgpu-profiler/v0.17.0/Cargo.toml ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Wumpf/wgpu-profiler/v0.16.0/Cargo.toml ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Wumpf/wgpu-profiler/v0.18.0/Cargo.toml ; https://docs.rs/crate/wgpu-profiler/0.28.0/source/Cargo.toml

ENGINE SEAMS: GfxContext::new at engine/src/gfx.rs:259-302 requests an adapter and device with required_features=Features::empty() at :296, so TIMESTAMP_QUERY is not currently enabled. The engine forces Vulkan when RENDERDOC is set (:261-264). Encoders are split into pbr, smap, depth_prepass, main, before_main, after_main, gui at :169-177. GfxContext::render records passes at :712-779; parallel mode records pbr/depth/shadow/SSAO+fog/background+blur/main/gui concurrently (:736-763). finish_frame submits all command buffers in order at :951-962. Render pass labels and timestamp_writes=None are explicit in main :837-846, shadow :898-910, depth :927-939 and pass modules ssao.rs:17-30, fog.rs:20-37, background.rs:32-45, blur.rs:98-110. Existing profiling::scope! is CPU instrumentation only (gfx.rs:719; framework.rs:119-120). No owned GPU timestamp/query implementation exists (rg found no TIMESTAMP_QUERY, resolve_query_set, write_timestamp, resolve_queries, or get_timestamp_period).

API FIT: profiler v0.17 README says it creates timer-query pools, supports nested scopes, wraps encoders/passes, and needs TIMESTAMP_QUERY; it requires resolve_queries(&mut encoder), end_frame(), then process_finished_frame(queue.get_timestamp_period()). The engine must request TIMESTAMP_QUERY conditionally, wrap each independent encoder/pass, resolve every encoder before finish, and coordinate one profiler frame across parallel recording. This is a non-trivial integration because profiler scopes borrow/wrap command encoders and the existing render path records 7 encoder groups concurrently. The v0.17 README documents the APIs: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Wumpf/wgpu-profiler/v0.17.0/README.md#L19-L61 ; source API example: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Wumpf/wgpu-profiler/v0.17.0/src/lib.rs#L39-L76

FALLBACK: keep dependency-free owned wgpu timestamp queries. wgpu 0.20.1 exposes Features::TIMESTAMP_QUERY and RenderPassDescriptor::timestamp_writes; its v0.20.1 source documents resolve_query_set and multiplying differences by Queue::get_timestamp_period (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gfx-rs/wgpu/v0.20.1/wgpu-types/src/lib.rs#L306-L328). Current pass descriptors already have timestamp_writes=None, so owned instrumentation can add a query set and writes without a second wgpu graph. It still needs feature negotiation, query buffer resolve/copy/map, and handling multiple command encoders.

FUTURE SPIKE CHECK: in an isolated worktree, add exact dependency wgpu-profiler = 0.17.0 (keep existing wgpu pin), then run cargo check -p engine -p engine_demo --locked and inspect cargo tree -i wgpu to prove one wgpu package/version. Do not change shared tree until this compile check and API integration review pass.

VERDICT: v0.17.0 is a credible compile spike, not yet runtime-compatible proof. Main integration risks are missing TIMESTAMP_QUERY capability, resolution across parallel independent encoders, and mapping results without stalling. No GPU capture was run.

comments.text: VERDICT ADOPT (conditional on a Radeon capture). Commit 69ffed1 on spike/sov-dda-gpu. Deciding evidence, all re-derivable from the pinned crate source at ~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-*/wgpu-profiler-0.17.0/: (1) resolve_queries at src/profiler.rs:342-376 resolves ONLY num_resolved..num_used and offsets the destination by num_resolved*QUERY_SIZE, so the never-reset-slot class of bug that sov-abc is cannot occur by construction - the hand-rolled module needed a 94-line repair to reach the same property; (2) begin_pass_query at src/profiler.rs:262-275 plus GpuProfilerQuery::render_pass_timestamp_writes at src/profiler_query.rs:74-84 produce exactly the wgpu::RenderPassTimestampWrites that gpu_timing.rs::writes() hand-builds, and require only Features::TIMESTAMP_QUERY - the SAME feature bar, not a higher one; (3) begin_query_internal at src/profiler.rs:685-694 checks device.features() itself and degrades to no timer, and GpuProfilerSettings::enable_timer_queries=false makes every call a no-op with lazy resource creation - opt-in-and-inert is native, not bolted on; (4) scope() takes &self (src/profiler.rs:131-136) so it works inside the existing rayon in_place_scope parallel render at gfx.rs:736-763 with no change to device/queue ownership; (5) COST: Cargo.lock gains exactly ONE package - parking_lot and thiserror 1.0.61 were already present - and cargo tree --workspace --duplicates reports no wgpu duplicate. title: [bug] GPU timing resolves query slots that were never reset: Vulkan UB (NOT the validation hazard - refuted)
description:
engine/src/gpu_timing.rs:177 (on branch wip/sov-m0q-wave1 @ b699465, NOT on main):

    enc.resolve_query_set(&self.set, 0..N_QUERIES, &self.resolve, 0);

The module tracks which passes actually ran - 'written: Mutex<[bool; N_GPU_PASSES]>' at :91, whose own comment reads 'Which slots were written this frame. A pass that did not run must not be reported.' It is set in writes() at :143-145 and snapshotted at :162-172. Line 177 then resolves ALL 18 slots regardless. The mask is computed and ignored.

WHY THIS IS NOT BENIGN, re-derived by the reviewer from the pinned crate sources:
  - wgpu-core-0.21.1/src/command/query.rs:48-84 (reset_queries) emits cmd_reset_query_pool ONLY for runs of queries actually used in that command buffer. An unwritten slot is never reset - not at pool creation, not ever.
  - wgpu-hal-0.21.1/src/vulkan/command.rs:411-421 copies with QueryResultFlags::TYPE_64 | WAIT.
  - command_encoder_resolve_query_set validates offset alignment, buffer usage and range overrun only. It does NOT check the queries were written, so this passes silently.

Reading a never-reset query with WAIT set is Vulkan undefined behaviour.

CONCRETE TRIGGER: a scene with ssao:false or shadows:ShadowQuality::Off, run with --gpu-timings. Slots 10-11 (or 2-9) are never reset, vkCmdCopyQueryPoolResults waits on an unavailable query, and on RADV the outcome is a validation error, garbage ticks, or a HANG inside device.poll(Maintain::Wait).

It does not fire on the shipped 'baseline' scene by luck, not design: shadows High gives 4 cascades, ssao true sets the define, fog and depth-prepass are unconditional, so all 9 passes write. The written mask exists precisely because the author expected partial writes.

LIKELY RESOLVES AN OPEN MYSTERY: the session handoff records an unverified lead that 'wgpu validation reports real synchronization hazards'. This is very probably it.

SETTLE IT WITH ONE COMMAND:
  cargo run -p engine_demo -- capture --gpu-timings --validation 2>&1 | grep -i 'VUID|query'

FIX SHAPE: resolve only the contiguous written runs (mirror wgpu-core's own run-finding loop), or write all 9 slots unconditionally.
acceptance_criteria: Either the resolve covers only written query runs, or all 9 passes write unconditionally. A scene with ssao disabled runs --gpu-timings without a validation error and without hanging in device.poll. The --validation grep above is run and its real output pasted. The handoff's 'validation reports synchronization hazards' lead is then either closed as this defect or restated as still open.
close_reason: merged as 1d358fb. THE ORIGINAL FIX WAS ITSELF BROKEN and the gate caught it: gpu_timing.rs set destination_offset = range.start * 8, but wgpu-types-0.20.0/src/lib.rs:80 defines QUERY_RESOLVE_BUFFER_ALIGNMENT = 256 and wgpu-core-0.21.1 command/query.rs:423 enforces it, while the resolve buffer is only 144 bytes - so 0 was the ONLY legal destination_offset and no positional offset could ever be valid. Three unit tests asserted the illegal values 16/48/128, locking it in. Latent only because engine_demo shipped one scene with all 9 passes on. FIX: each written run resolves to offset 0 of a scratch buffer, then copy_buffer_to_buffer to a positional readback slot (COPY_BUFFER_ALIGNMENT 4; every readback offset is first_pass*16; max end 144 = exactly the buffer size). Safety comes from wgpu-core's tracker emitting a real pipeline barrier (query.rs:504, transfer.rs:735), NOT from encoder ordering - documented in the code because a future reader who believed the ordering story could batch the resolves and lose it silently. The 'write all 9' alternative was correctly REJECTED: a pass that never executes cannot write its slots, so resolving them is the original unreset-slot UB. GUARD: alignment_guard sweeps all 2^9 masks against the re-exported wgpu constant, seen FAILING first ('emits resolve destination_offset 16 which is not a multiple of 256'). ACCEPTANCE CRITERION MET FOR THE FIRST TIME, on real hardware, verified independently by the gate: RX 7800 XT with ssao disabled, pre-fix EXIT=101 'Resolve buffer offset has to be aligned', post-fix EXIT=0, 8 passes, ssao correctly absent.
