comments.author: main
comments.text:
REFUTATION, measured by lead in main session 2026-08-28. The ticket's own hypothesis -- that this defect is 'likely the unexplained validation hazard' -- is DISPROVEN by a controlled before/after capture on the real target hardware.

Command, run identically in both worktrees:
  ./target/release/engine_demo capture --scene baseline --gpu-timings --validation --out target/renderer-evidence

Adapter both runs: AMD Radeon RX 7800 XT (RADV NAVI32) (Vulkan, DiscreteGpu), 1280x720, both exited 'capture ok'.

  BEFORE (wip/sov-m0q-wave1 @ b699465, unfixed):  10 x SYNC-HAZARD-WRITE-AFTER-WRITE
  AFTER  (fix/sov-abc @ ecca3ab, 94-line repair): 10 x SYNC-HAZARD-WRITE-AFTER-WRITE

10 is the validation layer's duplicate_message_limit, so both runs saturated it. The fix changes the count not at all.

The hazard is a different defect entirely: vkCmdPipelineBarrier writes a depth VkImage previously written at end of subpass 0 by the attachment storeOp, needing srcStageMask VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_2_LATE_FRAGMENT_TESTS_BIT and srcAccessMask VK_ACCESS_2_DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT_WRITE_BIT. It is a render-pass synchronisation bug, not a query-pool bug. Filed separately.

What this ticket still fixes, on its own merits and unaffected by the above: resolve_query_set covered all N_QUERIES while the 'written' mask at gpu_timing.rs:91 was computed and ignored, so slots that no pass wrote were resolved having never been reset. Per wgpu-core-0.21.1 src/command/query.rs:48-84, cmd_reset_query_pool is emitted only for runs actually used, so an unwritten slot is never reset. That remains real UB.

ALSO PROVEN by the same capture, and new: the hand-rolled gpu_timing module produces real non-zero per-pass numbers on this GPU. Medians over n=30: main 92.1us, ssao 33.7us, fog 28.4us, depth_prepass 25.1us, background 24.4us, shadow_cascade_0 12.5us, cascades 1-3 ~10.2us each. This was listed UNVERIFIED on sov-dda.1.

comments.author: engine-implementer
comments.text:
B1 SEND-BACK RESOLVED, commit 8c8c4d0. The original sov-abc repair (in 45a87b1) was invalid: it resolved only written runs -- right shape -- but at positional destination offsets range.start*8. wgpu-core-0.21.1/src/command/query.rs:423 rejects any destination_offset % QUERY_RESOLVE_BUFFER_ALIGNMENT != 0, and wgpu-types-0.20.0/src/lib.rs:80 defines that constant as 256. The resolve buffer is N_QUERIES*8 = 144 bytes, SMALLER THAN ONE ALIGNMENT UNIT, so offset 0 is the only legal destination that can ever exist. Verified at the pinned crate sources.

FIX: each run resolves to offset 0 of the scratch buffer, then copy_buffer_to_buffer moves it to its fixed readback slot (copies need only COPY_BUFFER_ALIGNMENT = 4). Commands in one encoder run in order so runs cannot clobber each other. Unwritten slots are still never resolved -- the Vulkan-UB constraint holds.

FALSE PREMISE WORTH RECORDING: the three original unit tests at gpu_timing.rs:264-330 ASSERTED the illegal offsets 16, 48 and 128. They were green, pure-CPU, and locked the bug in. A passing unit test that encodes an API precondition it never checks is worse than no test.

GUARD: alignment_guard::every_resolve_offset_is_alignment_legal_for_all_masks sweeps all 2^9 masks. Seen FAILING against the pre-fix code (mask [F,T,F,...] -> offset 16, not a multiple of 256), then passing.

LIVE PROOF of the ticket's own acceptance criterion, AMD RX 7800 XT / RADV NAVI32, by locally setting the baseline scene ssao to false (reverted after):
  pre-fix:  panicked at 'wgpu error: Validation Error / Resolve buffer offset has to be aligned to QUERY_RESOLVE_BUFFER_ALIGNMENT'  EXIT=101
  post-fix: capture ok, 8 passes timed, ssao correctly absent, no validation error, no hang in device.poll  EXIT=0

cargo test -p engine: 30 passed (was 29).

STILL TRUE AND NOT FIXED HERE: engine_demo ships ONE hard-coded scene with all 9 passes on, so nothing in CI would have caught this. That coverage gap is the reviewer's F10, out of my scope.

comments.author: engine-implementer
comments.text:
FOLLOW-UP on commit d47a11a (was 8c8c4d0 before a history rewrite; see the report for the sha remap). Two corrections carried from the re-gate, code content otherwise unchanged.

WRONG REASON, RIGHT CONCLUSION -- worth recording because a future reader could act on it. My comment justified the interleaved resolve/copy with 'commands in one encoder execute in order, so run N+1 cannot clobber run N'. That is NOT sufficient: in-order submission does not by itself prevent a read-after-write hazard in Vulkan; a barrier does. The safety actually comes from wgpu-core's resource tracker, which I verified emits one on each side of every iteration:
  wgpu-core-0.21.1/src/command/query.rs:504
    raw_encoder.transition_buffers(dst_barrier.into_iter());  before copy_query_results
  wgpu-core-0.21.1/src/command/transfer.rs:735
    cmd_buf_raw.transition_buffers(src_barrier.into_iter().chain(dst_barrier));  before copy_buffer_to_buffer
Both read verbatim at the pinned sources. The code comment now says so, and warns explicitly: do NOT batch all resolves ahead of all copies, and do NOT lower this to raw hal -- either drops the interleaving those barriers are derived from and loses the guarantee silently.

DEAD REF in 45a87b1's message: it claims the cancelled sov-1ae 250k benchmark lane is 'preserved as tag archive/sov-1ae-bench'. NO SUCH REF EXISTS. git tag -l lists five tags (archive/sov-dda-1-wgpu-profiler, archive/sov-dda-2-fast-paths, archive/sov-dda-3-lane-queues, archive/sov-m0q-wave1, bevy-track-final) and git for-each-ref | grep -i 1ae is empty. title: Renderer capture: three provenance and exit-code defects from the sov-ba8 review
description:
Three CONFIRMED medium findings from the opus review of wip/sov-m0q-wave1 @ b699465. All local fixes. None on main.

1. framework.rs:184-187 - --gpu-samples N silently truncates AND includes cold warm-up frames.
       let first = cap.warmup_frames.saturating_sub(samples.saturating_sub(1));
       t.set_armed(frame_ix >= first && frame_ix <= cap.warmup_frames);
   With warmup 90 and --gpu-samples 200: first = 90.saturating_sub(199) = 0, so frames 0..=90 are armed. That is 91 samples including the frames where shader compilation and mipmap generation dominate - exactly what the comment two lines above says it prevents. The record then writes 'sample_frames: 200' while the per-pass entries say 'samples: 91'. The evidence file contradicts itself and max_us is polluted by compile stalls. gpu_samples is validated >= 1 at engine_demo/src/capture.rs:182 but never bounded above warmup_frames + 1.

2. engine_demo/build.rs:18-19 - git_dirty can be stale, defeating the record's provenance. The script reruns on ../.git/HEAD and ../.git/index, but 'git status --porcelain' sees UNSTAGED working-tree edits and .git/index does not change when a file is edited without staging. So: build clean, edit engine/src/passes/fog.rs, run capture. Cargo reruns rustc but NOT build.rs, and the sidecar reports 'git_dirty: false' with a clean sha for a binary built from modified source. That is the single most misleading value the file can carry.

3. engine_demo/src/main.rs:387-389 - every CLI error exits 0, on stdout.
       Err(msg) => { println!("{msg}"); return; }
   parse_args returns Err for --help, --list-scenes, an unknown option, an unknown scene, and a bad --gpu-samples. All five print to STDOUT and exit 0, while a genuine capture failure exits 2 (main.rs:207, :232). So 'capture --scene baselien' prints 'unknown scene' and exits 0; a CI job or an && chain treats it as a successful capture and diffs a PNG that was never written.

Also worth folding in, both LOW and both CONFIRMED:
  - gpu_timing.rs:231 median_us is not a median: sorted[len/2] returns the upper middle on an even count, always the 16th of 30 at the default.
  - engine_demo/src/capture.rs:222-229 the per-pass timings are NOT additive - four shadow cascades go into separate command buffers submitted together and the GPU may overlap them, and the timestamps are top/bottom-of-pipe. The nine numbers can sum to more than the frame's GPU wall time, but the units string says only 'microseconds of GPU time per pass'. One sentence fixes it.

TRAP: fix 3 must keep --help and --list-scenes exiting 0. Only the genuine errors become exit 2 on stderr.
acceptance_criteria: --gpu-samples N arms exactly N frames, none of them cold, or is rejected when N exceeds what the warmup window allows; sample_frames in the record equals the per-pass samples count. build.rs detects an unstaged working-tree edit, or git_dirty is removed rather than left misleading. CLI errors exit non-zero on stderr while --help and --list-scenes still exit 0. median_us is a real median or renamed. The units string states the per-pass numbers are not additive.

title: [bug] cargo-deny sources gate passes egui git dependency with no rev pin: policy proven, reproducibility not
description:
The dependency-policy gate is now PROVEN to work as a gate (sov-ztg / sov-m0q.1 closed 2026-08-27 on run 33106713230, job conclusion FAILURE on PR 120). But it does not yet prove what the epic actually wants.

Cargo.toml allow-lists https://github.com/emilk/egui as a git source with NO rev key. cargo-deny 'sources' passes it because the URL appears in sources.allow-git, not because the commit is pinned. The check answers 'is this source permitted' and never asks 'is this source fixed'.

CONSEQUENCE: the build tracks a branch HEAD belonging to someone else. Anyone pushing to that upstream branch changes our build, silently, with a green gate. Two clones taken a day apart can produce different binaries while cargo-deny reports 'sources ok' both times.

This is the standing distribution blocker named in the release-engineer charter: the project is not reproducible. The gate proves POLICY. It does not prove REPRODUCIBILITY.

FOUND BY: release-engineer 2026-08-27, while closing sov-ztg. Reported as explicitly outside that dispatch's scope, so it was not fixed there.

RELATED CONTEXT: yakui is also a git source (git+https://github.com/Uriopass/yakui?branch=dev) and appears in Cargo.lock lines 402-406. Check whether it and every other git source carry a rev, not just egui.

TRAP: adding a rev pins the input but freezes upstream fixes. Decide the update cadence at the same time, or the pin becomes a different kind of debt. Do not pin to a branch name - a branch name is not an immutable reference.
acceptance_criteria: Every git dependency in Cargo.toml carries an explicit rev pinned to an immutable commit sha, or is documented as deliberately unpinned with the reason. cargo-deny sources still passes. A stated update cadence exists for the pinned revs. Two fresh clones taken from the same commit produce identical Cargo.lock git entries.

title: [bug] HUD pause button cannot un-pause: dead restore clobbered by unconditional assignment
acceptance_criteria: Clicking the pause button while the game is already paused resumes it at the previously saved warp speed. Clicking pause while running pauses and saves the speed. The speed buttons (b_warp != 0) still set their speed on click. The keyboard PausePlay toggle is unchanged. The unused_assignments warning at time_controls.rs is gone because the dead store was removed, not silenced. Proven by the running game, watched by the user or captured on video.
close_reason: merged as a8ab12f (fix commit 09cdf01): extracted the correct keyboard toggle into fn toggle_pause() and called it from BOTH the key path and the b_warp==0 button path; non-zero speed buttons set speed in an else branch. Gate: opus reviewer APPROVE, no findings, all four items re-derived independently. Guards proven non-vacuous by a REVIEWER-planted mutation, not the implementer's: pause_toggle_round_trips and pause_while_paused_resumes_saved_speed both went red (left (0,1000) right (1000,1000); 'speed 1 did not resume' left 0 right 1), 1 passed 2 failed, then restored md5-identical. Clean run: 'running 3 tests' naming all three, 'test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed'. Warning removed not silenced, verified BOTH directions: main's version rebuilt emits 'value assigned to *warp is never read' at time_controls.rs:75:29; the branch emits zero warnings there and grep for 'allow(' exits 1. Trap discharged: time_button has exactly 4 call sites, all local to the file, b_warp in {0,1,3,1000}; the else branch serves exactly {1,3,1000} so no speed value was lost. Manual observation recorded on the running game: pause, un-pause, and resume at speed 3 rather than 1.

comments.author: ui-implementer
comments.text:
FIXED on branch fix/sov-odw, commit 09cdf01 (worktree /home/caio/sov-wave-ui-wt). Not pushed, ticket left open.

FIX: extracted the (already correct) keyboard toggle into `fn toggle_pause(warp: &mut u32, depause_warp: &mut u32)` and called it from BOTH the PausePlay key path and the b_warp==0 button path; the non-zero buttons now set their speed in an else branch. The dead store was removed, not silenced.

=== LINE-BY-LINE TRACE, EVERY CLICK PATH ===
Notation: W = current non-zero warp, D = depause_warp, S = a non-zero b_warp.

--- BEFORE (buggy) ---
  if b_warp == 0 {
      if *warp == 0 { *warp = *depause_warp; }  // L75
      else          { *depause_warp = *warp; }  // L77
  }
  *warp = b_warp;                               // L80 unconditional

1. pause, running (b_warp=0, warp=W): L77 -> D=W; L80 -> warp=0.  PAUSES + SAVES. correct.
2. pause, paused  (b_warp=0, warp=0): L75 -> warp=D; L80 -> warp=0. STAYS PAUSED. **THE BUG**; L75 is the dead store rustc flagged.
3. speed S, paused (warp=0):   inner if skipped; L80 -> warp=S. correct, and DEPENDS on L80.
4. speed S, running (warp=W):  inner if skipped; L80 -> warp=S. correct, and DEPENDS on L80.

--- AFTER (fixed) ---
  if b_warp == 0 { toggle_pause(warp, depause_warp); }
  else           { *warp = b_warp; }
  // toggle_pause: if *warp==0 { *warp=*depause_warp } else { *depause_warp=*warp; *warp=0 }

1. pause, running (warp=W): else-arm -> D=W, warp=0.  PAUSES + SAVES. unchanged.
2. pause, paused  (warp=0):  if-arm  -> warp=D.       RESUMES AT SAVED SPEED. **FIXED**.
3. speed S, paused (warp=0):  else branch -> warp=S.  preserved.
4. speed S, running (warp=W): else branch -> warp=S.  preserved.
5. keyboard Space: now calls the same toggle_pause; logic byte-identical to the previous inline code.

=== THE TRAP, DISCHARGED BY ENUMERATION ===
The ticket warned that the b_warp != 0 buttons relied on L80 running unconditionally. `grep -rn time_button` gives exactly 4 call sites, ALL in this file: b_warp in {0, 1, 3, 1000}. The closure is a local `let mut time_button = |..|`, so no other caller can exist. The else branch therefore covers exactly {1,3,1000} -- every non-zero case L80 used to serve. Paths 3 and 4 above are preserved by construction.
(code-review-graph returned not_found for `time_button` -- a FALSE ZERO: the graph does not model local closures, and it was stale anyway, built_at 2cc7331 vs head 345a79a. Absence confirmed by grep, per the standing rule.)

=== EVIDENCE ===
A. unused_assignments gone because the dead store is gone, not silenced:
   BEFORE (main, unmodified): cargo check -p native_app ->
     warning: value assigned to `*warp` is never read
       --> native_app/src/gui/hud/time_controls.rs:75:29
     75 | *warp = *depause_warp;  ^^^ this value is reassigned later and never used
     80 | *warp = b_warp;         --- `*warp` is overwritten here before the previous value is read
   AFTER (branch): grep for 'unused_assignments|never read|time_controls' in cargo check output -> no match.
   The only remaining native_app warnings are the 6 pre-existing static-mut ones in init.rs.

B. Unit tests. toggle_pause takes two &mut u32 and touches no ECS state, so it IS unit-testable even though TestCtx cannot drive the UI. Added 3 tests in-file:
     cargo test -p native_app
       test gui::hud::time_controls::tests::pause_toggle_round_trips ... ok
       test gui::hud::time_controls::tests::pause_while_paused_resumes_saved_speed ... ok
       test gui::hud::time_controls::tests::pause_while_running_saves_speed ... ok
       test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed

comments.author: researcher
comments.text:
External research (2026-08-27; primary sources; configuration is a technical policy, not legal advice)

Current tool: cargo-deny 0.20.2, MSRV Rust 1.88.0, license MIT OR Apache-2.0. Pin the install in project tooling to 0.20.2 and use cargo install --locked cargo-deny --version 0.20.2; record both facts in the policy evidence. Sources: https://github.com/EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny/releases/tag/0.20.2 and https://github.com/EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny/blob/0.20.2/Cargo.toml

Command: cargo deny check runs the advisories, bans, licenses, and sources checks. Run the same command locally and later in CI, with --workspace --all-features only if the baseline intentionally covers every member/feature. Source: https://embarkstudios.github.io/cargo-deny/cli/check.html

Recommended baseline fields (inference from the current tree plus upstream schema):
[graph]
all-features = true
targets = ["x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu", "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc"]

[advisories]
ignore = []
yanked = "deny"
unmaintained = "warn"
unsound = "deny"

[licenses]
confidence-threshold = 0.8
# Set allow only after the observed lockfile license inventory is recorded. Do not infer GPL compatibility from a short permissive list.
allow = []
exceptions = []

[bans]
multiple-versions = "warn"
wildcards = "deny"
skip = []
skip-tree = []

[sources]
unknown-registry = "deny"
unknown-git = "deny"
allow-registry = ["https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"]
allow-git = ["https://github.com/emilk/egui", "https://github.com/Uriopass/yakui"]

Observed basis for the Git allowlist: Cargo.toml declares emilk/egui and Uriopass/yakui; Cargo.lock resolves both. Treat branch-based yakui as a reproducibility finding, not an exception: Cargo.lock pins the resolved commit, but Cargo.toml still tracks dev.

Why these fields: graph targets limit checks to actual shipping targets; cargo-deny warns that excluded graph nodes prune their dependencies too. The template documents structured advisory ignores with reasons, per-crate license exceptions and clarifications, duplicate skip/skip-tree rules, and exact registry/Git source control. Keep every future exception as an object with a reason and add a project review date in a nearby comment or policy record; cargo-deny itself has no generic review-date field. Sources: https://github.com/EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny/blob/0.20.2/deny.template.toml and https://embarkstudios.github.io/cargo-deny/checks/

Unresolved before implementation: determine actual release target triples from project release policy; obtain a complete dependency-license inventory with the final cargo-deny execution; decide whether unmaintained should be deny after seeing findings; do not add GPL-3.0 to allow solely because the repository LICENSE is GPL-3.0, since workspace manifests currently mostly omit package licenses and this tool checks dependency package metadata.

title: Tooling evidence roadmap
description: Problem: the project needs checked CI, dependency policy, mutation-test policy, fixed renderer capture, and GPU timing evidence. The user cancelled the 250k benchmark and Criterion lanes on 2026-08-27; their WIP artifacts remain preserved and unmerged. title: Export debits stock before border endpoint exists (conservation)

1. World with a producing company holding surplus and NO reachable border endpoint (no ExternalTrading building), e.g. demolish the seeded one as inflation.rs does.

3. Observe seller capital decremented at market.rs:702 while find_external at :705 returns None and the loop continues — stock gone, no trade, no sink.

title: unpark() leaks a phantom collider when called on a non-Parked vehicle
description:
Root cause found while fixing sov-2c4/sov-7pg (2026-08-26), deliberately scoped OUT of that fix because unpark has many callers.

transportation/vehicle.rs:107 unpark(): when the vehicle is NOT VehicleState::Parked, it logs warn 'Trying to unpark X that wasn't parked' and then CONTINUES ANYWAY — calls put_vehicle_in_transport_grid and overwrites v.collider. The previous collider entry is never removed from the transport grid (only Transporter::destroy does that). Result: a phantom collider with speed=0, is_vehicle=true, permanently occupying a lane position. That is exactly the blocker signature the debugger traced in sov-2c4.

sov-2c4's fix works around this at the CALL SITE (a guard in DispatchState::ToSource's grab path only unparks a confirmed-Parked truck) rather than fixing unpark itself. The warn path no longer fires from that route (grep -c went 1 -> 0), but every OTHER unpark caller can still hit it.

## Steps to Reproduce
Call unpark() on a vehicle in any state other than VehicleState::Parked (e.g. Driving or mid-RoadToPark). Observe the warn line, then inspect the transport grid: the vehicle's prior collider entry remains, with the new one added alongside.
acceptance_criteria: unpark() either removes the stale collider before overwriting, or refuses to act on a non-Parked vehicle and returns a signal the caller must handle. A test drives unpark on a Driving vehicle and asserts no orphaned grid entry remains. All existing unpark callers still pass cargo test -p simulation.
close_reason: merged as 1359509 (fixes 5349f34 + cdc8f1d): unpark() returns #[must_use] bool and refuses on a non-Parked vehicle, touching neither ParkingManagement, the transport grid nor v.collider. THE TICKET UNDERCOUNTED THE CALLERS - three, not two (router.rs:218, market.rs:805, world_command.rs:359); a prior bd comment asserting 'both agents confirm these are the ONLY two' was wrong. RED, re-planted independently by the reviewer: 'unpark on a non-Parked vehicle must not add a transport-grid entry, left 1 right 2' - the mutation-proof reproduction an earlier debugger could not build in ~55 runs. SECOND DEFECT CLOSED, unclaimed by the ticket and found by the ledger gate: the old unconditional mem::replace in the if-let scrutinee dropped a RoadToPark vehicle's SpotReservation, which ParkingManagement frees only via free() and which has no Drop - that parking spot leaked permanently. cdc8f1d adds the rollback logistics required: on refusal the ToSource caller calls release_tosource_truck + Dispatcher::free instead of logging; without it the dispatch, truck and reserved[seller] froze forever because ToSource has no timeout. Three mutations, each red on its own assertion. Gates: wiring WIRED 0 dead, all three callers handle the bool meaningfully; logistics SIGN OFF (condition met); reviewer APPROVE-WITH-FIXES; ledger CONSERVED twice, the second scoped to cdc8f1d and refuting the earlier PLAUSIBLE freeze. Clean-tree run: 48 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored.

comments.text:
MOVEMENT DOMAIN SIGN-OFF (logistics-modeller, Phase 4 row 4) on 5349f34: SIGN OFF WITH ONE CONDITION. cargo test -p simulation: 47 passed, 0 failed, exit 0.

1. REFUSAL IS THE RIGHT SEMANTIC. Confirmed all three callers can act on false. router.rs:157 and :171 both say 'RoutingStep::Unpark(_) => true' for cur_step_over AND next_step_ready, so the step is popped and done regardless of the return value -- a refused unpark cannot stall the router. In the reachable refusal case (vehicle already Driving/Panicking) the postcondition unpark exists to establish already holds: the vehicle has Driving state plus a live Transporter, so road.rs moves it on the next tick. Refusal there is idempotent success, not a dropped movement request. world_command.rs:359 is unreachable by construction and its 'continue' is harmless.

2. THE market.rs:783-786 GUARD MUST STAY -- implementer's reasoning CONFIRMED at source, and this REFUTES the 2026-08-27 comment suggesting it may have become dead code. unpark cannot free a Dispatcher reservation; it has no Dispatcher. Remove the guard and the sequence is: query reserves a mid-RoadToPark truck -> ve.it = route -> deferred unpark refuses -> truck = Some(v) set anyway -> the park spline completes, the collider is DESTROYED (road.rs vehicle_state_update at t>=1.0) and the state becomes Parked -> vehicle_decision_system early-returns on collider None and physics() snaps a Parked vehicle to its spot, so it.has_ended(0.0) is false FOREVER. ToSource with truck=Some(v) has NO timeout; its only exit is the vehicle entity vanishing. Dispatch, truck reservation and the seller's reserved qty are held permanently. That is exactly the sov-jcl / sov-dispatch-wedge-ab4 shape one state earlier.

3. NEVER GAME OVER -- the fix REMOVES a hard violation, it does not add one. transport_grid_synchronize (transportation/mod.rs:87) only iterates entities that HOLD a Transporter, so an orphaned handle's speed/dir/flag/position are frozen forever. calc_front_dist's 'speed <= 0.01' filter is only in the ray-crossing branch; the FRONT-CONE branch has no speed filter, so a phantom passes it whenever cos_direction_angle > 0 and clamps min_front_dist. Worse, calc_decision escalates to Panicking only when me_u64 == flag, and the phantom's flag is frozen at 0, so the blocked vehicle flags ITSELF, never matches, and never panics. A phantom produced a PERMANENT NON-ESCALATING stall with no 'gridlock!' log -- invisible to the planner and unrecoverable. Post-fix behaviour degrades correctly everywhere: router no-ops, world_command skips, market retries next tick.

4. ROUTING/CONGESTION INTERACTION -- strictly positive, and load-bearing for the roadmap. movement.md commits to BPR volume-delay with beta=4 over EMA-smoothed per-lane load. A phantom is permanent occupancy that no EMA can decay: a static v/c offset that, at beta=4, inflates a physically clear lane's cost enormously and permanently and pushes all routing off it. Removing phantoms is a PRECONDITION for congestion pricing meaning anything. Secondary: each spurious unpark added one grid entry that nothing ever removes, so the grid grew unbounded across a session and through save/load.

CONDITION (small, must land before or immediately after merge): market.rs:804-811 logs the refusal but still executes 'self.dispatches[i].truck = Some(v)'. The Parked check and the deferred unpark run on DIFFERENT TICKS (cbuf_vehicle.exec_ent), so the window is narrow but real. If it ever fires, item 2's permanent wedge happens anyway -- logged, but with no recovery path, because ToSource/Some has no timeout. On false it must instead call dispatcher.free(DispatchID::SmallTruck(v)) and leave the dispatch in ToSource/None to retry next tick. General rule: a refusal signal is only safe where the caller can undo its OWN bookkeeping; a caller that already took a reservation or recorded ownership must roll it back on false, not merely log.

RECOMMENDED FOLLOW-UP TICKET (not blocking): ToSource with truck=Some(v) has no tick countdown at all, unlike Loading, the return path, and retail_claims which all bound their waits. That is a standing wedge surface independent of this fix. Same family as sov-jcl.

title: Second dispatch stalls in ToDestination near the new parking spot, distinct from sov-2c4
description:
Found by sim-implementer (2026-08-26) while verifying the sov-2c4 fix end-to-end in sov-lpj's inflation.rs scenario. sov-2c4's fix (route truck to a reserved parking spot on Unloading-complete instead of abandoning it mid-lane) is verified correct in isolation: the FIRST delivery cycle now completes cleanly, dispatches=[], stock reaches 4 at tick 2683.

But a SECOND, later dispatch (different delivery cycle) then freezes in DispatchState::ToDestination: truck decelerates smoothly then stops dead at one exact coordinate (~141.5, 2.0) and stays there 20,000+ ticks, has_ended() never true. Reproduces identically with and without the parking-reservation-leak fix (ruled out as a cause, not a duplicate of that). The frozen coordinate is close to but NOT identical to the other truck's now-permanently-reserved parking spot (~125.0, 5.25) -- proximity only, causation NOT confirmed.

Implementer stopped here rather than guess further; said it would need road.rs gridlock-breaker/Panicking-state instrumentation to diagnose properly -- exactly the debugger lane's job, not implementer's.

TRAP: this looks superficially like sov-2c4 (also a ToDestination freeze near a parking/lane area) but is confirmed distinct -- reproduces even with sov-2c4's fix in place, so it is not the same abandoned-truck mechanism. Do not assume it is; re-derive from source.

Working tree state when this was found: economy/market.rs has the sov-2c4 fix (parking reserve+forget), economy/mod.rs has the matching signature threading, simulation/src/tests/scenarios/inflation.rs still carries diagnostic probes (kept deliberately, not reverted, since the test is still red).

close_reason: Duplicate of sov-2c4, same defect family — confirmed by sim-implementer and lead. Root mechanism: freed-but-still-Driving trucks re-grabbed by ToSource, unpark() called on non-Parked truck, phantom collider leaked into transport grid. Fixed by the sov-2c4 fix (park() + ToSource grab guard); no separate work needed. Verified: cargo test -p simulation --lib -> 44 passed 0 failed, and grep -c "wasn't parked" went 1 -> 0.

title: Truck abandoned mid-lane after Unloading blocks all later dispatches to the same door
description:
Found by debugger agent (2026-08-26), diagnosing a stuck dispatch in sov-lpj's inflation.rs test. Root cause: economy/market.rs DispatchState::Unloading completion (~977-989) frees the dispatch and sets ve.it = Itinerary::NONE but never re-parks or moves the truck — it stays Driving at its stop position. A ponytail comment in that code already names the gap: 'leave the truck Driving wherever it stopped instead of re-parking ... upgrade to the RoutingStep::Park spline machinery if idle trucks start blocking traffic.' They now do.

CHAIN: abandoned truck sits in the live lane at the destination door -> every later dispatch to the same door queues behind it (confirmed: blocker has is_vehicle=true, speed=0) -> ToDestination's only exit is Itinerary::has_ended(), which a truck that never arrives cannot reach -> the vehicle-gridlock breaker (transportation/road.rs calc_decision, Panicking state) never fires because it needs the queue to loop back to the checking vehicle's own flag, not just stall behind one parked truck -> zero 'gridlock!' log lines across 62,000+ ticks.

CONFIRMED by mutation: changing Unloading's Itinerary::NONE to cbuf_vehicle.kill(v) made the dispatch cycle resume immediately (dispatches went ToSource -> ToSource,ToSource; stock reached upper bound 4). Reverted, zero residual diff.

Only the Unloading branch has this shape; ToSource/Loading/ToDestination/Returning all correctly free the dispatch without leaving a live truck. Possibly related to sov-jcl (unbounded Outbound Loading retry) but NOT confirmed the same defect -- debugger flagged this as plausible-distinct, unverified.

SUGGESTED FIX (not applied): route the truck to a nearby parking spot on Unloading completion via the existing Itinerary::route + park/unpark mechanism already used elsewhere in market.rs (e.g. ToSource's unpark call), instead of only clearing its itinerary. Full fix per the ponytail comment is the RoutingStep::Park spline machinery.
acceptance_criteria: A scenario with sustained repeat deliveries to one door (e.g. sov-lpj's flour-factory once unblocked) completes 10+ dispatch cycles without any truck ever left Driving with Itinerary::NONE for longer than one tick; ledger-invariant-checker or wiring-auditor confirms no truck permanently occupies a live lane.
close_reason: Fixed and gated. park() made pub(crate) (router.rs:274) and called from both DispatchState::Unloading completion and DispatchState::Returning arrival (market.rs) — real RoadToPark->Parked transition replaces the Itinerary::NONE abandonment; dispatcher.free moved after park() starts, with a guard in ToSource's grab path rejecting non-Parked trucks. Verified by lead: cargo test -p simulation --lib -> 44 passed, 0 failed. grep -c "wasn't parked" went 1 -> 0. Opus reviewer (sov-mol-bv7) approve-with-fixes: cleared livelock/starvation (Q1), free-park ordering (Q2, guard is load-bearing), and reserve_near failure stranding (Q3) with traced call paths; probed end state dispatches_now=0, abandoned_driving=0. Root cause unpark() deferred to sov-6qx (two unguarded paths noted there).

Verdict: fix as-built does NOT meet this ticket's own AC (10+ sustained cycles, no truck ever occupies a live lane) -- cycle-1 completing is not the bar, walked that claim back. (2) end-position grep confirmed the truck whose route completed reached the real off-lane spot (V3(125.0, 5.25/5.007, 0.3)) but the frozen truck never got there -- it sits on-lane (V3(136.09062, 2.0, 0.3), y=2.0 matches the live lane, not the y~5.25 spot) -- consistent with being corrupted mid-route by the unpark bug, not by anything in my parking-spot logic itself. Advisor also surfaced that the private fn park (map_dynamic/router.rs:274) already implements the full VehicleState::RoadToPark spline machinery this ticket said not to build -- making it pub(crate) and calling it from Unloading (keeping the reservation, which the current fix already does) would close both gaps: truck ends genuinely off-lane in Parked state (fixes the y-coordinate finding), and future re-grabs become legitimate unparks (no more warn-and-corrupt). Filed the unpark-on-Driving root cause as sov-7pg per lead ruling, handed to debugger, NOT chased further by me -- it's outside this ticket's 'market.rs only' scope. Current state: fix in market.rs (reserve_near + route + kept reservation, no VehicleState::Parked flip) stands as verified for what it does fix -- cycle 1 completes cleanly, matches the debugger's original mutation-proof target -- but sov-2c4's full AC is blocked on sov-7pg. Full suite: cargo test -p simulation --lib -> 43 passed, 1 failed (only sov_lpj's flour-factory test, expected), no regressions from the market.rs/mod.rs edits.

comments.text:

So sov-7pg's 'second, distinct freeze' is the SAME defect family, not a separate mystery: freed-but-still-Driving trucks get re-grabbed by ToSource, unpark is called on a non-Parked truck, phantom collider leaks, lane blocks. title: Seller surplus ext-trade computation destroys capital unconditionally when no freight station exists
description:
Found during sov-lpj fix pass (sim-implementer, 2026-08-26). economy/market.rs ~686-699: the seller-surplus-to-external-trading path does '*cap -= qty_sell' BEFORE checking find_external().is_some(). With no freight station the check fails, the trade record is skipped, but the capital deduction already happened — quantity silently destroyed, no accounting. Violates 'nothing teleports' (units vanish without moving). Related: sov-abs (backfill teleports goods IN); this is the outbound twin. TRAP: any test or map without a freight station slowly drains every seller with stock=0 sell orders; inflation.rs works around it with stock=1_000_000 so qty_sell never goes positive.

## Steps to Reproduce
City with no freight station; a seller with a sell order at stock 0 and positive capital; run market_update long enough for the surplus computation to fire; watch capital drain with no trade records.
acceptance_criteria: Capital deduction happens only when the external trade is actually recorded; a scenario with no freight station holds seller capital constant; ledger-invariant-checker signs off the seam.
close_reason: merged in de4a4b9 (test 98dcab5). Guard: tests::scenarios::ledger::sov_dii_no_freight_station_holds_seller_capital. Verified by main on clean main at 370ef54: cargo test -p simulation = 57 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored, with the guard appearing BY NAME in the output (so the filter-matches-nothing trap does not apply). NOTE ON WHAT THIS CLOSES: the ticket's premise was already STALE when reviewed -- at 7721cdd market.rs:719-723 the 'let Some(ext) = find_external(order.pos) else { continue; }' already precedes '*cap -= qty_sell', so the unconditional capital destruction was not live. The ticket's durable value was its acceptance scenario, and that is what landed: a test that demolishes the seeded freight station, drives real market_update ticks, and asserts capital, the surviving sell order and total_qty. Closing on the guard, not on the original premise.

comments.author: reviewer
comments.text:
REVIEWER VERDICT (opus adversarial gate, sov-lpj): APPROVE-WITH-FIXES.

Verified myself: cargo test -p simulation = 44 passed / 0 failed. cargo test -p prototypes = 5 passed / 0 failed (AC A: all prototypes load with only 2 of ~19 companies declaring the field). Mutation proof run by me: forcing base_mod/companies.lua:40 flour-factory request_multiplier 4->1 fails BOTH inflation tests -- 'left: Some(1)' on AC C and 'flour-factory must converge to the bounded hoard [3, 4], got 1' on AC D. Reverted exactly; git diff confirms only the original sov-lpj diff remains.

ACs A,B,C,E,F,G,H all MET. AC D is only PARTIALLY met -- see finding 1.

F1 CONFIRMED (medium): sov_lpj_flour_factory_hoards_bounded_no_freight_station never exercises consumption. flour-factory has n_workers=10 and the scenario spawns zero humans, so raw_productivity (goods_company.rs:84-86) = 0/10 = 0, progress never reaches 1.0, and recipe_act NEVER RUNS. I probed the live trajectory: stock pins at a constant 4 for all 20k ticks (max_stock=4, last 20 samples all 4), flour_stock=0, progress=0.0 for both companies. So the test proves recipe_init's initial buy_until(4) and that nothing pushes past 4 -- it does NOT prove the [k*c-c, k*c] OSCILLATION the ruling calls 'the single most important number in this ticket', because the lower bound 3 is never reached. The doc comment at inflation.rs:98-103 claims 'driven by the ordinary company_system tick loop (real recipe_init/recipe_act...)' and 'converges to the bounded hoard' -- recipe_act is not reached, so that claim is inaccurate. The assertion still passes and still catches the mutation (both bounds sit above the honest value 1), so this is a coverage/doc-accuracy gap, not a false green.

F2 REFUTED (the brief asked me to build or clear it): the .unwrap() at goods_company.rs:55 cannot panic on any current path. company_soul (souls/mod.rs:41) is the ONLY production spawn and always runs recipe_init before the entity is reachable; the truck-shortage early return (goods_company.rs:136-141) returns None BEFORE world.insert, so no orphan CompanyEnt exists. There is no prototype hot-reload path in the tree. Market.remove wipes 'requested' only from sim_drop (world.rs:196), i.e. the entity is already dead. Kill and exec_on are mutually exclusive within one company_system pass (the kill branch returns at :196), and ParCommandBuffer::apply drains kills then execs within the same scheduler slot (scheduler.rs:46-51), so no queued recipe_act survives its entity. SingleMarket rows are never removed from Market.markets. All three recipe_provided.rs callers pair recipe_init with recipe_act. Cleared.

F3 REFUTED: no save-compat break. 'requested' was already a serialized SingleMarket field before this diff (added by commit 6ea4553), so sov-lpj changes no bincode layout. Recipe itself is not Serialize -- it is rebuilt from Lua each boot.

F4 (nit, unverified impact): inflation.rs:113-116 doc says the mutation proof uses 'a substitute achievable without touching base_mod' and points at 'the report'; the actual mutation (edit companies.lua) is trivial and I ran it, so that comment points at a report no future reader has.

Boundary-crossing pair checked: Lua field name request_multiplier (companies.lua:40,582) vs the get_lua key (recipe.rs:63) -- exact string match both sides, unwrap_or(1) matching the zone.rs:20-21 precedent. assets_gui's Recipe is a DIFFERENT type (has 'complexity', no storage of this field), so it is correctly untouched.

Scope: clean -- exactly the 6 named files, no creep.

SUGGESTED FIX (smallest first): either (a) soften the inflation.rs:98-103 doc to say what the test actually proves (initial inflated request is placed and never exceeded, with no freight station and no money movement), or (b) staff the factory so recipe_act actually cycles and the [3,4] oscillation is genuinely observed. (a) is sufficient to close honestly; (b) is what would make AC D fully met.

comments.author: reviewer
comments.text:
REVIEWER RE-REVIEW (opus gate, sov-lpj + dispatch fix sov-2c4/sov-7pg): APPROVE-WITH-FIXES.

Ran myself: cargo test -p simulation --lib = 44 passed / 0 failed. Mutation (companies.lua:40 flour-factory 4->1) kills BOTH sov_lpj tests: 'left: Some(1) right: Some(4)' at inflation.rs:95, and 'stock must stay within the bounded hoard [3, 4], observed [0, 1]' at inflation.rs:287. Reverted exactly; only the intended diff remains.

MY FIRST-REVIEW FINDING IS FIXED AND I VERIFIED THE FIX IS REAL, not a lucky snapshot. Instrumented the sampled window and collapsed it to runs: [(3,39),(4,334),(3,66),(4,1)] -- four alternating runs, i.e. two full 4->3->4 oscillations, with flour=20 actually produced. recipe_act genuinely cycles now. The window-sampling design (inflation.rs:271-276) plus the two exact-bound asserts (:296-314) is the right shape; a single end-of-run snapshot could not tell [3,4] oscillation from pinned-at-4, and this can.

Q1 ToSource grab guard -- CLEARED, no livelock/starvation. Dispatcher::free only removes from reserved_by (dispatch.rs:110-117); Dispatcher::update re-registers EVERY truck from world.vehicles each tick unconditionally (dispatch.rs:99-104), and dispatch_system (init.rs:59) runs before market_update (init.rs:98), so a freed truck is back in positions next tick. The dispatch stays in ToSource with nothing debited and retries -- identical to the pre-existing no-route branch. RoadToPark is bounded: TIME_TO_PARK=4.0s (vehicle.rs:13), so the reject window is a few ticks, not indefinite.

Q2 free()/park() ordering -- SAFE at the dispatch grab site, but only because the guard carries it. park() sets RoadToPark then free() runs immediately, so yes, the truck IS grabbable mid-RoadToPark within the same tick -- the guard at market.rs:783-786 is what rejects it. Ordering + guard together are sound. I enumerated all three production unpark call sites: market.rs:803 (now guarded), world_command.rs:359 (a Car it just spawned Parked -- unreachable for trucks), and router.rs:217. router.rs:217 unparks UNCONDITIONALLY with no Parked check, and it IS reachable for a dispatcher-pool truck: WorkKind::Driver pushes SetVehicle(Some(truck)) (souls/desire/work.rs:60), so a company truck becomes the router's vehicle. That is the sov-6qx shape on a second path. It is PRE-EXISTING and untouched by this diff (git diff of router.rs is only the fn park visibility change; last touch was the fork commit 68fe28c), so it is correctly out of scope -- but it means the call-site guard does NOT cover every caller. sov-6qx should note router.rs:217 explicitly.

Q3 Returning + reserve_near failure -- CLEARED, does not strand. If reserve_near returns Err the truck simply stays Driving, i.e. degrades to the exact pre-diff behavior; dispatcher.free still runs and remove=true still fires, so no dispatch is stranded. park()'s warn-and-return branch is unreachable from these two new sites: reserve_near and park share one immutable &Map with no tick between, so the spot cannot vanish. A killed truck does not leak either -- VehicleEnt::sim_drop frees both Parked and RoadToPark reservations (world.rs:74-78).

Q4 2 cycles vs sov-2c4's '10+ sustained cycles' -- I AGREE WITH THE WORKER, with evidence rather than on argument. Probed end-of-run state: dispatches_now=0 and abandoned_driving=0 (trucks Driving with an ended itinerary). The sov-2c4 symptom is a truck that never leaves the lane -- a permanent state, so it shows up on cycle 2 as surely as on cycle 10. Note though: sov-2c4 is IN_PROGRESS in bd, not closed as the re-review brief states.

Q5 first-review ACs -- all still hold. AC E: freight-station demolition + is_empty assert retained (inflation.rs:50-53); the added solar-panel has NO recipe (base_mod:74-95) so it cannot perturb the cereal market. AC C: unchanged and still mutation-proven. AC G: honestly weakened to strict-decrease because real humans now incur upkeep; that is correct and the reasoning at :250-257 matches economy/mod.rs:53-55. Still has teeth -- an ext-trade credit would move money UP and fail it.

FIXES (both cosmetic, neither blocks):
1. inflation.rs:302-305 -- the assert message still says 'BLOCKED as of this commit: the flour-factory is permanently electricity-blacked-out ... expected to fail until that is fixed.' That is now FALSE; the test passes. A future reader hitting this failure will be actively misled. Delete those two sentences.
2. sov-6qx should name router.rs:217 as the second unguarded unpark path.

Scope: the dispatch fix is a real scope expansion beyond sov-lpj but it is justified -- sov-lpj's AC D could not be met without it, and it is the root-cause fix at the two market.rs sites rather than a test-local workaround. Visibility widening (fn park, mod router) is the minimum needed. No creep beyond that.

title: BuyFood BoughtAt is an inescapable sink when the store building is demolished
description: CONFIRMED pre-fork (HEAD buyfood.rs:86-94 + router.rs:87-92; adjudicated by opus gate 2026-08-26, found by codex-reviewer). Every exit from BoughtAt(b) requires loc==Building(b), but the router on a demolished building marks dest reached WITHOUT pushing GetInBuilding — loc never becomes Building(b). Human stuck forever: hunger ramp rises, BuyFood re-scores highest, GoTo swallowed every tick, never re-queues a buy order. Ledger is fine (claim TTL frees reserved) which is why no conservation test catches it. Violates never-game-over in spirit AND silently deflates observed bread demand — misleads the Planner core loop. FIX (lazy+correct): guard at top of BoughtAt arm — if b doesn't resolve to a live building, reset to Empty WITHOUT advancing last_ate (went-without semantics, matches the claim-expired branch). apply already receives binfos, no signature change. TRAP: apply is not polled every tick — state check, not event subscription (see buyfood.rs:96-104).
acceptance_criteria: demolishing a store with in-transit customers returns them to Empty (hunger intact); test drives real demolition, mutation-proven; no change to eat-time settlement semantics
close_reason: merged as 1359509 (fix 36997b6): guard at the top of the BoughtAt arm resets a human to Empty without advancing last_ate when the store building is not live. Test scenario_demolished_store_releases_bought_at_customer drives a REAL WorldCommand::MapRemoveBuilding. RED seen by implementer AND independently re-planted by the opus reviewer: 'a demolished store must not keep emitting GoTo, got GoTo(Building(BuildingID(3v1)))'. THE BRIEF'S PREMISE WAS FALSE and the implementer caught it: BuildingInfos has no remove method and slotmapd 1.0.11 SecondaryMap::get (secondary.rs:479-485) version-checks only its own slot, so binfos entries survive demolition; apply() now takes &Map, which human.rs:231 already held. Gates: wiring WIRED (one production call site, on the real per-tick path via update_decision_system, init.rs:62); reviewer APPROVE-WITH-FIXES; ledger CONSERVED - no coin exists to strand (domestic match sets money_delta ZERO at market.rs:530) and the reservation is released by Market::remove or the unconditional TTL sweep at market.rs:1068-1078. Eat-time settlement semantics unchanged. Clean-tree run: 48 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored.

comments.author: codex-diagnosis
comments.text: CONFIRMED at HEAD 8531d3c (post-wedge, sim code unchanged since 7e4b82f). Evidence: router.rs routing_changed_system, Destination::Building arm, lines 87-93: when map.buildings.get(build) is None (demolished), sets router.cur_dest = router.target_dest and returns WITHOUT pushing RoutingStep::GetInBuilding -- h.location never becomes Location::Building(b). human.rs HumanDecisionKind::update (line 91): GoTo(dest) => router.go_to(dest); Router::go_to (router.rs:325-333) returns true once cur_dest==dest, i.e. update_decision (human.rs:187) treats the GoTo as COMPLETE every tick once cur_dest was force-set, re-scores desires, calls food.apply again (buyfood.rs:117 BoughtAt arm), sees loc != Location::Building(b) still (loc never advanced), re-emits GoTo(Destination::Building(b)) (buyfood.rs:146) -- infinite loop, soul permanently wedged (not self-recovering; hunger ramps per the ticket, last_ate never advances, matches never-game-over in letter but not spirit since the human can never eat again). Trigger sequence: human matched to a store via retail claim, walking there (BoughtAt(b), loc=Outside/Vehicle), building b demolished mid-walk -> next routing_changed_system tick takes the None branch -> permanently stuck GoTo loop. Minimal fix (buyfood.rs BoughtAt(b) arm, ~5-8 lines): guard at top of the arm using the same existence check the ticket names -- mirror market.rs's door_pos()/find_trade_place(TradeTarget(seller), binfos) pattern already used elsewhere in this file (buyfood.rs:89 uses find_trade_place for the WaitingForTrade->BoughtAt transition) -- if map.buildings().get(b) is None (need &Map threaded into apply's signature OR resolve via binfos.building_owned_by/find_trade_place against the claim's seller, whichever needs no new param), reset self.state = BuyFoodState::Empty WITHOUT setting last_ate (went-without semantics, same as the 'claim expired' branch at buyfood.rs:138-142), and do NOT call market.settle_retail (seller/building gone, nothing to settle -- claim TTL will separately clean the reservation per ticket's note that ledger is already fine). TRAP confirmed: apply() is not polled every tick (decision.wait jitter, human.rs:186-187), so this must be a state check inside the arm, not an event subscription -- matches ticket's buyfood.rs:96-104 citation. Signature note: apply() currently receives binfos (buyfood.rs:69) but not &Map -- ticket claims 'apply already receives binfos, no signature change' -- true IF the existence check goes through binfos (e.g. binfos.building_owned_by(b) or checking find_trade_place still resolves b) rather than map.buildings().get(b) directly; recommend using binfos to honor that no-signature-change claim, since map is not currently threaded to apply. Test: TestCtx scenario -- human reaches BoughtAt(b) state (or force via existing set_state_bought_at_for_test test hook), demolish building b before loc reaches Building(b), tick, assert state resets to Empty and last_ate unchanged; mutation: remove the guard, watch human never leave BoughtAt (GoTo loop) / test hang or state assertion red. No interaction risk with sov-lpj: that ticket's wiring is confined to goods_company.rs recipe_init and Market::set_requested/requested(), no touch to buyfood.rs, router.rs, or retail_claims.

comments.author: sim-implementer
comments.text:
Fixed on branch fix/sov-wave-souls, commit 36997b6. TEST: tests::scenarios::retail::scenario_demolished_store_releases_bought_at_customer. Seen red first: panicked 'a demolished store must not keep emitting GoTo, got GoTo(Building(BuildingID(3v1)))'.

BRIEF WAS WRONG on one point: 'apply already receives binfos, no signature change' is FALSE. Nothing removes a demolished building from BuildingInfos (binfos.rs has no remove method), and slotmapd SecondaryMap::get (secondary.rs:479) only version-checks its OWN slot -- it never consults the primary map. So binfos.get(b) and binfos.owner(b) both stay Some after the bulldozer. binfos is not a liveness oracle for a BuildingID. The guard needs ⤅ update_decision (human.rs:170) already had map in scope, so apply() gained one param and the single production call site (human.rs:231) passes it. The test asserts binfos.get(seller_b).is_some() after demolition so the next reader cannot repeat this.

Everything else in the ticket held: guard at the top of the BoughtAt arm, reset to Empty, last_ate NOT advanced, no settle_retail, eat-time semantics untouched. cargo test -p simulation: 47 passed, 0 failed.

comments.author: ledger-invariant-checker
comments.text:
Ledger audit (ledger-invariant-checker) at 5349f34: CONSERVED, ticket premise re-derived not inherited.
- No money exists to strand: the domestic match sets money_delta: Money::ZERO (market.rs:530); only ext-trade attaches money (:680/:715) and humans are carved out of it. settle_retail credits the buyer nothing. Money is not a gate on this path.
- At the moment the guard fires the human has NOT paid: the retail leg debits nothing until eat-time (settle_retail, market.rs:466-477). The loaf is still in the store's capital, merely reserved.
- The reservation is released on both orderings: Market::remove(seller) drops claims naming it (market.rs:274) then wipes its capital/reserved row (:275-282); otherwise the TTL sweep at the end of advance_dispatches (market.rs:1068-1078) releases reserved. Nothing is frozen.
- No double claim: retail_claims is keyed by buyer, and make_trades releases a displaced claim's reservation on the OLD seller's row (market.rs:614-637) before overwriting.
- Only goods_company.rs posts sell orders in production, so a retail seller is always a GoodsCompany, killed by company_system the tick its building dies (goods_company.rs:195).
COMMENT CORRECTION (buyfood.rs:127-129): 'the seller soul died with its building and Market::remove already released its reservations' is FALSE at guard time. init.rs registers update_decision_system (:62) BEFORE company_system (:65), so on the demolition tick the guard runs while the seller soul is still alive and its reservation still stands. The outcome still conserves (removal or TTL follows), but the stated reason is wrong and a future reader should not rely on it.

comments.author: sim-implementer
comments.text:
ROUND 3 comment correction, commit cdc8f1d on fix/sov-wave-souls. No behavior change; the fix and its test are unchanged.

My guard comment claimed 'the seller soul died with its building and Market::remove already released its reservations'. That is FALSE at guard time (caught by ledger-invariant-checker). init.rs registers update_decision_system BEFORE company_system, and company_system (goods_company.rs:195) is what kills a company whose building is gone. So on the demolition tick the guard runs while the seller soul is still ALIVE and its reservation still stands.

The outcome is still conserved, and the comment now states the real reason: the reservation is released either by Market::remove(seller) when that kill lands (market.rs:274 drops claims naming it, :275-282 wipes the seller row), or by the unconditional retail-claim TTL sweep at the end of advance_dispatches (market.rs:1068-1078, TTL = TICKS_PER_HOUR) -- which still reaches the claim because abandoning BoughtAt does not remove it. Re-queueing before then is safe because retail_claims is keyed by BUYER: one human holds one claim, and make_trades (market.rs:614-637) releases a displaced claim's reservation on the OLD seller's row before overwriting. A human that abandons and re-queues in the same tick cannot hold two reservations.

Also trimmed the half of the guard comment that duplicated the note already at buyfood.rs:96-104.

Ledger gate returned LEDGER: CONSERVED. Clean tree, cargo test -p simulation: 48 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored.

title: Outbound Loading retry is unbounded: live buyer, no route holds truck+cargo forever
description: CONFIRMED pre-fork (HEAD f89bc3b market.rs:546-566; adjudicated by opus gate 2026-08-26, found by codex-reviewer). advance_dispatches Loading arm: buyer building alive (door_pos Some) but Itinerary::route None (e.g. road bulldozed) -> stays Loading at ticks_left=0, retried every tick, NO bound. Seller already debited at ToSource arrival: cargo credited to nobody, truck never freed (same pool leak shape as round 4), dispatch entry immortal. The sibling RETURN leg IS bounded (MAX_RETURN_ROUTE_RETRIES=20, market.rs:874/:138) — the asymmetry proves oversight. FIX: bound the outbound leg identically — reuse/sibling the retry counter, honest logged loss + dispatcher.free at exhaustion. TRAP: do NOT fold into the wedge diff (three gate signoffs, byte-identical ledger baseline). Same wedge THEME as sov-dispatch-wedge-ab4 but a sibling instance the ticket never named.
acceptance_criteria: outbound Loading bounded like the return leg; at exhaustion: honest loss logged, dispatcher.free called, dispatch removed; mutation-proven test (remove the bound, watch red); ledger conserved
close_reason: merged in de4a4b9 (fix a16c065). Guard: tests::scenarios::ledger::sov_jcl_outbound_loading_route_failure_is_bounded, which asserts handed_out == reachable_trucks with reachable_trucks >= 2 and no vehicle destroyed -- confirmed non-vacuous at the gate. Verified by main on clean main at 370ef54: cargo test -p simulation = 57 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored, with the guard appearing BY NAME in the output (so the filter-matches-nothing trap does not apply). The outbound Loading leg is now bounded like its RETURN sibling. Known and accepted: the off-by-one 'return_route_retries + 1 >= MAX' drops after 19 attempts rather than 20, judged harmless at the gate.

comments.author: codex-diagnosis
comments.text: CONFIRMED at HEAD 8531d3c (post-wedge; wedge commit 7e4b82f only added the wedge, this commit only touched agent config, no sim code changed). Evidence: market.rs advance_dispatches DispatchState::Loading arm, the 'buyer_pos is None' else-branch at market.rs:851-903 (route-to-buyer search fails silently — comment at 858-859 says stay in Loading, retry next tick — no counter is incremented on THAT path). The bounded return_route_retries logic exists only inside the door_pos(buyer)==None sub-branch (wedge b, 862-903), which is a DIFFERENT trigger (demolished buyer) from wedge a's trigger (buyer alive, door_pos Some, but Itinerary::route to buyer_pos returns None e.g. road severed) at line 843-853. That second path has zero bound: 'No route found: stay in Loading (ticks_left at 0) and retry next tick' (comment at 851-852) — reruns forever, truck+cargo (already debited from seller) never freed. Trigger sequence: dispatch reaches Loading, truck exists, buyer building alive (door_pos Some) -> Itinerary::route(tick, start, buyer_pos, ...) returns None every tick (e.g. road to buyer bulldozed, no path exists) -> falls through both branches (route Some/None) without touching ticks_left or return_route_retries -> ticks_left stays 0 -> re-enters this arm next tick identically -> immortal. Minimal fix (~10-15 lines): reuse Dispatch::return_route_retries as a general 'route search failures at this stage' counter (rename optional) for the outbound leg too, incrementing it in this branch and checking it against MAX_RETURN_ROUTE_RETRIES with the same honest-loss-and-free shape as market.rs:874-887 (dispatcher.free + remove=true + log::warn). Do NOT add a second field; the counter is unused while a dispatch is in Loading-outbound (only used later for the Returning leg), so it's free to reuse across both. Test: TestCtx scenario that severs the road between seller and buyer buildings while a dispatch is in Loading (buyer_pos Some, route None every tick), assert dispatch count decrements to 0 within MAX_RETURN_ROUTE_RETRIES ticks and truck is freed (dispatcher can reissue it) -- mutation: delete the new bound check, watch dispatch count/truck freed assertion go red (infinite loop or leaked truck). No interaction risk with sov-lpj: that ticket is pre-wiring (Market::set_requested has zero production callers yet per its bd description), touches recipe_init/goods_company.rs and requested()/set_requested only -- zero overlap with dispatches/DispatchState/market.rs's advance_dispatches state machine.

comments.author: sim-implementer
comments.text:
CONFIRMED and FIXED in commit 166b1cf. Root cause exactly as the codex-diagnosis comment describes: market.rs Loading arm, 'if let Some(route) = route {...}' with only a trailing comment on the None side — no counter, no ticks_left change. Fix reuses Dispatch::return_route_retries against MAX_RETURN_ROUTE_RETRIES (20) with the same honest-loss + dispatcher.free + remove shape as the return leg; no second field. Const doc updated to say it now covers both legs out of Loading.

TEST-CONSTRUCTION NOTE for the next agent (two dead ends cost real time): the obvious trigger — bulldoze the road between seller and buyer — does NOT work. (a) Removing ALL roads then re-laying one makes ctx.build_roads panic 'unreachable' at map/map.rs:175, because MapProject then resolves to a Building/Lot rather than Ground. (b) Removing only the middle of three segments DESTROYS vehicles: truck count went 3 -> 1, which silently routes the dispatch through the sibling 'truck vanished while loading' branch and makes the test vacuous. What works, with zero map mutation: build TWO DISCONNECTED road networks (0..80 and 600..760), seller company on one, buyer company on the other. The truck reaches the seller (dispatch gets to Loading, seller debited) and Itinerary::route to the live buyer returns None forever. Second gotcha there: Dispatcher::query walks lanes outward from its target, so it can only hand out trucks on the SELLER's network — compare handed_out against trucks with pos.x < 300, not against the whole world truck count.

Mutation proof (bound deleted, test red): panicked at 'an unroutable outbound Loading dispatch must be given up on, not retried forever: [Dispatch { buyer: GoodsCompany(CompanyID(2v1)), seller: GoodsCompany(CompanyID(1v1)), kind: ItemID("cereal"), qty: 10, state: Loading, ticks_left: 0, truck: Some(VehicleID(1v1)), return_route_retries: 0 }]'. Full suite after: 47 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored.

comments.author: logistics-modeller
comments.text:
logistics-modeller Phase-4 movement sign-off on 166b1cf: SIGN OFF WITH CONDITIONS.

ACCEPTED. Shared counter is correct. return_route_retries is read and written ONLY inside the Loading arm (market.rs:889/915 outbound, :939/954 return); ToDestination (:977) and Returning (:1006) never touch it, and Loading is entered from exactly one site (:856). So there is no cross-state contamination. Burn-through IS real -- k ticks failing outbound, then the buyer is demolished, and the return branch has 20-k left -- but both branches increment only on route FAILURE, so a healthy return route succeeds on attempt 1 whatever the budget. Degradation only where both legs fail, i.e. where the dispatch is doomed anyway. Sharing also caps total Loading residency at 20 ticks instead of 40. GUARD THAT MUST NOT BE REMOVED: do not reset the counter when the leg switches. A reset re-opens the 40-tick worst case and lets an alternating demolish/rebuild pattern keep a dispatch alive indefinitely.

ACCEPTED. Not re-crediting the goods is the right movement-model disposition. They are on a truck; a refund would be the teleport this pillar forbids.

CONDITION 1 (tuning, not correctness). 20 ticks is too aggressive. common/src/timestep.rs:3 UP_DT = 20ms => 50 ticks/s, so MAX_RETURN_ROUTE_RETRIES = 20 is 0.4 SECONDS of game time at 1x. Itinerary::route fails transiently while the map is edited, and 0.4s is well inside a single player road-drag: bulldoze one segment and every truck city-wide that is mid-Loading silently loses its load. The bound was chosen for a demolished buyer (permanent); the outbound trigger is usually a transient. Recommend 250-500 ticks (5-10s). Does not violate a pillar -- the loss is honest and logged -- so it does not block.

CONDITION 2. log::warn! is not planner-visible. requirements/movement.md requires a stall to escalate to a planner-visible bottleneck event. Cargo destroyed by a road edit with no in-game signal is frustration, not gameplay.

CONDITION 3, the strongest finding. The truck is freed but NOT parked. At :910 the new arm does a bare dispatcher.free with no park(). sov-2c4 already established the opposite at the Unloading arm (:1050-1079) with the comment 'an abandoned truck sits in the door's live lane and blocks every later dispatch to the same door'. The freed truck is left VehicleState::Driving with an ended itinerary and a live TransportGrid collider, stopped wherever it was. It re-enters the pool on the next Dispatcher::update, and every future ToSource query that picks it hits the Parked guard at :800-804 and frees it again -- so it is back in the pool and permanently unusable, while blocking a lane. The sibling Returning-exhaustion arm (:951) and the both-gone arm (:968) share the gap; sov-jcl makes it reachable on a far more common trigger (a bulldozed road rather than a demolished building). MITIGATION I ACCEPT: reuse the Unloading path -- parking.reserve_near + map_dynamic::router::park before dispatcher.free -- at all three exhaustion sites.

Verified: cargo test -p simulation in /home/caio/sov-wave-market-wt, 48 passed 0 failed 1 ignored, 58.11s.

comments.author: wiring-auditor
comments.text: wiring-auditor (Phase 4 row 1): WIRED. New else-if arm at market.rs:889-911 is inside advance_dispatches' Loading state, reached every tick via market_update (init.rs:98). Guard sov_jcl_outbound_loading_route_failure_is_bounded is SOUND, not vacuous: its truck stays alive, so Dispatcher::update re-registers it and a missing dispatcher.free() would leave it in reserved_by and drop handed_out below reachable_trucks. comments.author: ledger-invariant-checker
comments.text: ledger gate (ledger-invariant-checker), commit 7721cdd: CONSERVED. The honest logged loss is the right disposition - the goods were debited at ToSource arrival and are physically on a truck that can reach nobody; re-crediting would be the teleport the pillar forbids, and it matches the existing precedent in the truck-vanished and Unloading arms. Shared-counter concern REFUTED: return_route_retries is only consulted on the return leg when the route home ALSO fails, so a budget spent failing to reach the buyer can only pre-empt a return that was itself impossible. Test sov_jcl_outbound_loading_route_failure_is_bounded is NOT vacuous - 'handed_out == reachable_trucks' with the 'reachable_trucks >= 2' guard genuinely detects a leaked reserved_by entry. Adjacent latent, not this ticket: DispatchState::ToSource has NO retry bound at all - no truck or no route leaves the dispatch immortal one state earlier than the leg this ticket bounded, and sov-abs newly routes imports into it. Nothing is debited there so quantity is conserved, and it is bounded in practice because a starved factory stops re-posting buy orders, but it is the same wedge shape one state upstream.

comments.text: MarketFixups wave-2 fixup (expectation update, boundedness property kept): sov-13h raised MAX_RETURN_ROUTE_RETRIES 20->300, so the 40-tick give-up wait was stale (dispatch showed return_route_retries:37 mid-count).
