title: Ext-trade backfill teleports goods into enterprise capital, bypassing shortage
description:
market.rs:650-680. The old free-goods leak (sov-ledger-exttrade-cbh) IS fixed: find_external returning None now continues BEFORE crediting capital (market.rs:667-671), so with no freight station unmatched buy orders are correctly denied.

REMAINING DEFECT: once ANY freight station exists, every unmatched non-human enterprise buy order is satisfied instantly. capital is credited directly at market.rs:671 with NO Dispatch created -- the dispatch loop at market.rs:604 iterates all_trades[dispatch_start..] and has ALREADY RUN by the time ext trades are pushed at market.rs:673. Goods appear in the buyer's larder in the same tick, having moved nowhere.

Breaks pillar 'nothing teleports' (CLAUDE.md, charter-1.0.md:29) and defeats shortage for enterprises: no enterprise can ever experience an unmet input need in a city with a freight station. Downstream consequence for sov-lpj: a hoarding enterprise's withdrawal has no victim, because everyone downstream is backfilled free at the border. The dishonest-enterprise loop is dramatically inert wherever this path is live.

Found during Phase 0 consult on sov-lpj (see the kornai-economist ruling comment there, section 4). Successor to sov-ledger-exttrade-cbh.
acceptance_criteria: Ext-trade acquisition of a physical good creates a Dispatch (or the freight-station equivalent) and credits buyer capital only on physical arrival; no path credits capital in the same tick as the match. Mutation-proven: a test in a city WITH a freight station where an enterprise's input need remains unmet for at least one tick.
close_reason: merged in de4a4b9 (fix 1d29b01). Guard: tests::scenarios::ledger::sov_abs_ext_trade_import_is_physical. Verified by main on clean main at 370ef54: cargo test -p simulation = 57 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored, with the guard appearing BY NAME in the output (so the filter-matches-nothing trap does not apply). An ext-trade import now creates a real Dispatch instead of crediting capital at match time, so the import moves physically and 'nothing teleports' holds on the import half.

comments.author: lead
comments.text: sim-lpj evidence strengthening this bug: find_external (economy/mod.rs) picks min_by_key(distance) freight station with NO reachability check and NO distance cutoff, and TestCtx/production both always have one from hardcoded START_COMMANDS in Simulation::new_with_options. Every city has a working zero-cost export market from tick 0. Fix should include a cutoff or road-reachability check. See inflation.rs remove_default_freight_station() for the test-side workaround.

comments.author: lead
comments.text: Ledger gate (sov-lpj): request_multiplier MULTIPLIES the ext-trade backfill magnitude for flour-factory (k=4) and meat-facility (k=3) — the inflated deficit feeds market.rs:667 import when a domestic seller cannot cover. Not a conservation break (money pairs with goods) but raises this bug's priority: hoarding is victimless AND import-amplified in any city with a freight station.

comments.author: sim-implementer
comments.text:
FIXED in commit 7721cdd. Design landed: the ext-trade BUY block moves ahead of the dispatch-creation loop in Market::make_trades and no longer credits capital; an import becomes an ordinary Dispatch whose seller is the SoulID::FreightStation (BuildingInfos::set_owner registers freight stations, so find_trade_place/door_pos already work for them). The border is debited at Loading and the buyer credited at ToDestination arrival, same as any domestic trade. The export half is untouched.

SCOPE ADDITION, and it was load-bearing: the fix alone is NOT shippable. Without a reachability check every TestCtx/production city creates import dispatches to the hardcoded START_COMMANDS station at ~(4300,6300), which no truck can reach; those sit in ToSource forever and 9 of 48 tests went red. So find_external (economy/mod.rs) now filters to stations whose door is within DISPATCH_LANE_CUTOFF of a driving lane. That constant is the 50.0 literal DispatchOne::query already used, now named and shared. This is the reachability check the lead's 2026-08-26 comment asked for.

SUBSTRATE FACT worth keeping: DispatchOne::query resolves DispatchQueryTarget::Pos with map.nearest_lane(pos, kind, Some(50.0)). A building whose door is >50 units from a driving lane can NEVER be offered a vehicle. Map::nearest_lane with cutoff None falls back to the globally nearest lane and effectively never returns None, so only the cutoff path bites.

TWO EXISTING TESTS WERE PASSING ON THE TELEPORT — this is the finding worth more than the task:
1. retail::scenario_dead_truck_tosource_cancels_without_leak asserted 'the second delivery must complete cleanly' (buyer capital == 5). Verified on a clean tree: at that point the seller's sell order is None, so no domestic match was possible at all — the 5 units were the ext-trade credit. The delivery it claimed to prove never happened. Rewritten to assert its stated claim (no truck left in Dispatcher::reserved_by) directly.
2. ledger::scenario_ledger_exttrade_double_spend drives make_trades with a stub |_| Some(ext) naming mk_soul(...), which owns no building; the bakery's background flour import to it can never leave ToSource (door_pos None). Now drains on its own item via a new drain_dispatches_of helper in hoarding.rs.

Also found, NOT fixed and not this ticket: with a real sell order re-posted, that retail scenario's freshly spawned truck reaches DispatchState ToSource with a truck assigned and then sits at VehicleState::Driving at a fixed position for 6000 ticks without moving. Separate vehicle-substrate stall (unpark/Transporter collider), unrelated to the market seam.

Full suite after: 48 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored. Mutation proof for the new test (same-tick credit restored): 'an imported good must NOT be in the buyer's capital on the tick it was matched' left:4 right:0.

comments.author: kornai-economist
comments.text:
PHASE 4 ECONOMY SIGN-OFF (kornai-economist) on 7721cdd: SIGN OFF WITH CONDITIONS.

VERDICT PER QUESTION

1. Shortage IS restored, and it is real shortage, not a one-tick delay. The import is now an ordinary Dispatch competing for the SAME city-wide truck pool as every domestic delivery. Magnitudes: UP_DT=20ms (50 ticks/s, common/src/timestep.rs:3), truck max speed 6.0 u/s (transportation/vehicle.rs:64) = 0.12 units/tick; DISPATCH_DWELL_TICKS=3 (market.rs:133). A 200-unit station-to-factory leg is ~1700 ticks, plus the ToSource leg. companies.lua sets n_trucks=1 on every company, so the pool is one truck per enterprise and every import contends with every domestic delivery. When Dispatcher::query returns None the dispatch waits in ToSource with NOTHING debited (market.rs:828-830). That is a queue in the Kornai sense, not a delay. The core loop is no longer inert where a freight station exists.

2. The border is still an UNBOUNDED SOURCE in quantity. advance_dispatches debits the FreightStation seller at ToSource arrival (market.rs:847) with no stock and no reservation, so its capital goes negative without limit. Bounded only by transport. For 1.0 I ACCEPT this: transport is the binding constraint and it is the one the Planner can act on. But it is NOT the right long-run model. Kornai (The Socialist System, 1992) separates the SOFT domestic budget constraint from the HARD external one -- convertible-currency scarcity is the classic hard bound on a socialist economy, and it is the reason import substitution and forced domestic substitution happen at all. The bound belongs on freight-station THROUGHPUT (units per tick per station), which is also the Workers and Resources precedent (border/customs stations move goods at a vehicle loading rate, never instantly). SUCCESSOR TICKET, not this one.

3. NO PRICE SIGNAL introduced. money_delta = -(ext_value * qty) is applied at economy/mod.rs:104 as gvt.money += delta, with no affordability check anywhere in the tree (the only other money sites are world_command.rs:225 construction cost and mod.rs:54 wages). Government money can go negative; nothing gates on it. Imports are rationed by truck availability and by find_external picking the nearest REACHABLE station -- distance and capacity, never willingness to pay. Consistent with 'domestic clearing is money-free; the single rouble exists only at physical border clearance'.

4. The Planner's detection loop is HELPED. A hoarder's withdrawal now has a visible victim: downstream enterprises sit at capital 0 with an in-flight Dispatch, and the import itself is an inspectable Dispatch row with a FreightStation seller. The lie is still inferred (requested vs recipe consumption), not read off a badge. No regression to the sov-lpj panel constraints.

5. The find_external reachability filter (economy/mod.rs:68-83) is CORRECT ECONOMICS. An unreachable border is a closed border; a station promising deliveries no truck can make is exactly the teleport in another costume. I accept the scope addition. Two caveats, neither blocking: (a) the filter tests 50 units to ANY driving lane, not route connectivity, so a station on a disconnected road island still passes and its dispatches stall in ToSource forever -- recoverable if the road is later joined, so it degrades and never terminates, but it is invisible; (b) a city whose only station is unreachable now silently gets no external trade at all, with no Planner-facing signal. Both want a readout, not a code change here.

6. ACCEPTANCE CRITERION IS MET, not approximated. ledger::sov_abs_ext_trade_import_is_physical builds a reachable station, asserts capital(soul,cereal)==0 on the tick the border matched, asserts the Dispatch exists with a SoulID::FreightStation seller, and only then drives it to arrival. That is 'unmet for at least one tick in a city WITH a freight station'. 48/48 pass on this worktree (cargo test -p simulation, 30.97s). Mutation evidence is the implementer's claim (capital left:4 right:0); I did not re-run it -- evidence-auditor owns that re-proof. The trailing assert!(ticks > 0) is tautological given the earlier capital==0 assertion; harmless, the earlier assertion is the real guard.

TWO FINDINGS THE DIFF CREATES, NEITHER BLOCKING

F1 -- MY sov-lpj DYNAMICS RULING NEEDS AN AMENDMENT. I ruled the hoard BOUNDED at (k-1)*c because buy_until tops up and stops. buy_until (market.rs:421) reads capital ONLY; it does not count in-flight dispatches. With an import now taking ~2000 ticks instead of 0, a hoarder that has already been filled re-posts on each production cycle and STACKS imports: for flour-factory k=4, amount 1, successive cycles post 1, then 2, then 3, so up to 6 units can be in flight against a target of 4. Steady-state hoard therefore exceeds k*c wherever a reachable border exists. An honest company (k=1) never stacks: it consumes to capital 0 and stalls. So the honest=0 / dishonest>0 discrimination SURVIVES and is if anything amplified. I accept it -- repeat requisitioning under unreliable delivery is Kornai-true behaviour. But the 'bounded at (k-1)*c' claim now holds only in a city with no freight station, which is exactly how sov_lpj_flour_factory_hoards_bounded_no_freight_station is written. Do not generalise that test's numbers.

F2 -- THE BORDER OUT-COMPETES DOMESTIC SUPPLY BY ONE TICK. The domestic matching pass runs first within make_trades, so domestic has priority -- but only for the single tick in which the order is posted. extract_if (market.rs:621) then removes every surviving non-human buy order and hands it to the border. An enterprise therefore never queues on a domestic producer that will have stock next tick; it queues on the border instead. Shortage is preserved (the queue is just a different queue) so this is not a violation, but it makes the border the DEFAULT supplier rather than the residual one, which inverts the planned-economy ordering. Pre-existing shape, now load-bearing. Successor ticket.

WHAT I REJECTED / WHAT MUST NOT BE REMOVED

G1 -- the human carve-out. market.rs:622 extract_if predicate !matches!(s, SoulID::Human(_)), guarded by retail::scenario_human_order_never_fills_via_external_market. Households must never clear at the border; that would be a money gate on a need.
G2 -- the ORDERING. The ext-trade buy block must stay ABOVE the dispatch-creation loop. Moving it back below reinstates the teleport with no compile error. sov_abs_ext_trade_import_is_physical is the only thing that catches it. Neither may be deleted or weakened without a fresh economy sign-off.
G3 -- no capital is credited in the ext-trade buy block. The negative assertion is now enforced by the test, not merely written in an AC.

STILL OUT OF SCOPE AND STILL A TELEPORT: the EXPORT half (market.rs:706-733) still debits seller capital and credits money in the same tick with no Dispatch. Surplus leaves the city having moved nowhere. It does not corrupt the hoarding signal (hoards are on the INPUT side; sell_all only posts production items) but it means output storage pressure never bites where a reachable station exists, so recipe storage_multiplier halts are unreachable there. Explicitly outside sov-abs; needs its own ticket.

STANDING CAVEAT UPDATED: my rule that any hoarding demonstration must run in a city with NO freight station is DOWNGRADED, not obsolete. A demonstration may now run with one, but it must constrain the truck pool or the station distance, or assert on delay and queue length rather than on permanent denial -- with plentiful trucks and a near station the backfill is still eventually complete, so the shortage is a delay and not a denial. The existing no-station test stays as the clean bounded-hoard proof.

comments.author: logistics-modeller
comments.text:
logistics-modeller Phase-4 movement sign-off on 7721cdd: SIGN OFF WITH CONDITIONS.

ACCEPTED, core fix. An import now creates an ordinary Dispatch and credits the buyer only at ToDestination arrival. The falsification test for the nothing-teleports pillar -- zero vehicles must mean zero stock changing hands -- now passes on the IMPORT path. No dispatch storm: Market::buy (market.rs:413) inserts into a map keyed by soul, and buy_until is re-posted only from recipe_act, which recipe_should_produce gates on capital -- so a starving enterprise does NOT re-post while its import is in flight. One import dispatch per (enterprise, item) per need-cycle, not per tick. Verified at goods_company.rs:32-57.

VIOLATION, pre-existing, NOT introduced here, must be filed as this ticket's sibling. The EXPORT half still teleports. market.rs:723 does *cap -= qty_sell with no Dispatch, after the dispatch loop. Goods leave the seller's building and reach the border in the same tick, having moved nowhere -- the exact mirror of the defect just fixed on the import side. With zero vehicles, stock still changes hands on that path. 'Ext trade is physical' is currently half true.

CONDITION 1, truck pool. base_mod/companies.lua gives n_trucks = 1 to factories only; stores get zero and the freight station gets zero. Imports draw from that same pool and are taken exactly when domestic supply is absent -- so in a young or shortage-struck city imports are the DOMINANT dispatch source, and the round trip to a single border station is the longest trip on the map. Dispatcher::query is FCFS by dispatch index with no ranking, so long import trips crowd out short domestic hops -- the classic unprioritised-assignment throughput collapse. requirements/movement.md commits to ranking by deficit priority and meaningful distance; that is not present. This degrades (dispatches queue in ToSource) rather than breaks, so it does not block. MITIGATION I ACCEPT, and it is the modelled answer: give the freight station its own vehicles, matching $VEHICLE_STATION on the reference install's station types, so border transport does not consume the city's factory trucks.

CONDITION 2, the reachability filter -- ACCEPT AS A NECESSARY CONDITION, REJECT THE CLAIM THAT IT IS A REACHABILITY TEST. map.nearest_lane(door, Driving, Some(50)) is proximity, not connectivity. A station 40m from a lane on a disconnected road component passes and strands every dispatch. The real connectivity test already exists and is stronger: DispatchOne::query (dispatch.rs:264-293) runs a BACKWARD BFS over the lane graph from the target lane and only returns a truck graph-connected to it. So the substrate already refuses the delivery; the filter only stops the PROMISE, and only for the no-lane-at-all case. It does fix the actual START_COMMANDS station, so keep it -- but do not describe it as reachability.

CONDITION 3, and this is the damaging consequence of Condition 2. With a lane-proximate but graph-disconnected station: query returns None every tick, the dispatch sits in ToSource/None FOREVER (neither ToSource arm has a countdown), and the buy order was already extract_if-removed at match. Capital is never credited, recipe_should_produce stays false, recipe_act never runs, buy_until never re-posts. The enterprise is permanently and silently dead AND DOES NOT RECOVER when the player later connects the road. That is a never-game-over failure at enterprise scale with no planner-visible signal. sov-abs materially ENLARGES the unbounded ToSource surface I flagged on sov-6qx: before this commit imports created no dispatch at all; now every unmet enterprise need enters the one state with no bounded exit. MITIGATION I ACCEPT: a bounded ToSource/None timeout that re-posts the buy order via Market::buy before removing the dispatch -- the caller undoing its own bookkeeping, per the sov-6qx rule.

MINOR, also under dispatch.rs:163 register() still uses the literal 50.0 rather than DISPATCH_LANE_CUTOFF, so the commit's 'both call sites agree by construction' is one site short of true. Same value today.

Verified: cargo test -p simulation in /home/caio/sov-wave-market-wt, 48 passed 0 failed 1 ignored, 58.11s.

comments.author: ledger-invariant-checker
comments.text: ledger gate (ledger-invariant-checker), commit 7721cdd: CONSERVED on quantity. Border debit and buyer credit are the same Dispatch.qty: capital[FreightStation] -= qty at ToSource arrival (market.rs advance_dispatches), capital[buyer] += qty at ToDestination arrival, once; the match credits nothing and Unloading credits nothing. The border is an ACCOUNTED infinite source - its negative capital row is the import ledger, so total_qty (capital sum + in-flight) is conserved across an import. Teardown traced: buyer demolished at Loading/ToDestination -> Market::remove routes the truck home -> Returning arrival credits capital[FreightStation] += qty, border made whole; truck dies -> declared logged loss, no re-credit; buy order consumed exactly once (domestic match removes it from buy_orders before extract_if). Probe: default START_COMMANDS station door (4297.4, 6315.3) has nearest_lane(Driving, 50) == None, so with the new filter a FRESH GAME HAS NO IMPORT BORDER until the player builds a reachable station - intended by this ticket but a large gameplay change, confirm with the lead. TWO LATENT ITEMS, neither a mint: (1) money and goods are now decoupled - gvt.money += money_delta fires at match (economy/mod.rs:104) while goods arrive many ticks later or never; demolish the buyer mid-flight and the border keeps both the goods and the money. Fix if wanted: apply an import's money_delta at ToDestination arrival. (2) buy_until (market.rs:421) reads raw capital and does not know about in-flight incoming, so a company completing a recipe mid-flight re-posts and draws a second import from an infinite source. Conserved, but over-supply. Also note buy_until's 'qty - c as u32' underflows if c<0; negative capital rows are now routine (the border) - safe only because nothing calls buy_until/sell_all on a FreightStation soul.

comments.author: kornai-economist
comments.text:
KORNAI PHASE-0 RULING — sov-lpj: how request-inflation is declared and arises

VERDICT: HYBRID, but with a hard sequencing rule. Ship the STATIC Lua-declared
propensity for 1.0. Design the sim modulation so it is ADDITIVE later; do NOT
build it now. Reasons and rejections below.

== 1. THE AXIS RULING ==

REJECTED: pure emergent inflation (sim raises requests in response to
experienced shortage) as the 1.0 mechanism.

Kornai is on the lead's side theoretically -- hoarding IS a response to supply
uncertainty ("the firm... strives to build up reserves of input stocks",
Economics of Shortage, on the hoarding-shortage vicious circle). But three
things kill it as the 1.0 mechanism:

(a) OBSERVABILITY. A globally emergent rule makes every enterprise inflate by
roughly the same amount at roughly the same time. The Planner cannot detect a
liar when everyone lies identically -- the discrepancy stops being a signal and
becomes a constant offset on the whole economy. Detection needs VARIANCE across
enterprises, and variance needs a per-prototype declaration. This is the
"observable" test from the model: a deception the player cannot distinguish
from background is noise, not gameplay.

(b) It is a FEEDBACK LOOP, and the shortage signal it would read is currently
untrustworthy (see section 4). An emergent rule wired to a broken scarcity
signal produces either runaway inflation or none.

(c) SCOPE. The charter binds. An adaptive-expectations layer is a system, not a
field. Nothing in charter 1.0 §Resources-and-production commits to it.

REJECTED: a per-company random roll at spawn. It gives variance but it is not
authored, not reproducible across saves for the same city, and gives the
Planner nothing to learn -- the player can never build a model of WHICH
enterprises lie, only re-check all of them every time. That is chores, not
inference.

ACCEPTED: static per-prototype declaration, sim reads it at recipe_init and
recipe_act. Authored variance across the 26 companies. Reproducible.
Learnable ("the meat-facility always over-orders"). Cheapest thing that makes
the loop real.

== 2. DATA SCHEMA SKETCH ==

Lua, on the RECIPE table (base_mod/companies.lua), NOT on the company:

    recipe = {
        consumption = {{"cereal", 1}},
        production  = {{"flour", 10}},
        duration = "100s",
        storage_multiplier = 5,
        request_multiplier = 3,     -- NEW, optional, default 1
    }

Rust: `prototypes/src/types/recipe.rs` -- add to `struct Recipe`

    /// How much input this enterprise REQUESTS per cycle, as a multiple of what
    /// its recipe actually consumes. 1 = honest. >1 = inflates its requirement
    /// and hoards the surplus. There is no honesty flag: the Planner infers
    /// dishonesty from stock that outruns consumption.
    pub request_multiplier: i32,   // default 1 when absent

parsed with the existing get_lua pattern, defaulted (NOT `get_lua(...)?` --
absent must mean 1, or all 26 companies break).

Sim wiring, `souls/goods_company.rs:21-27` and `:56-60`: the two existing
`.requested(soul, item.id).unwrap_or(item.amount as u32)` sites become the
requested value derived from `item.amount * recipe.request_multiplier`, with
`Market::set_requested` called ONCE at `recipe_init` so `Market::requested()`
becomes the single readable source for the panel. Do not compute it in two
places; the panel must read the same number the buy order used.

WHY ON THE RECIPE, NOT THE COMPANY: `requested` is per-item and only means
anything against a consumption amount. Recipe is where `consumption` and
`storage_multiplier` already live, and `recipe_init`/`recipe_act` already take
`&Recipe` and nothing else. A field on GoodsCompanyPrototype would have to be
threaded separately into both functions for no gain.

WHY A MULTIPLIER, NOT AN ABSOLUTE: with an absolute, a recipe amount change
silently turns an honest company dishonest. A multiplier keeps honesty
expressible as exactly one value (1) that survives rebalancing.

Per-item override is NOT needed for 1.0. All 26 companies consume 1-3 items at
amount 1; a whole-recipe multiplier expresses everything the current data can
show. If a later recipe needs to hoard cereal but not flour, add
`{"cereal", 1, request = 3}` then. Do not build it now.

== 3. MAGNITUDES -- and the important dynamics finding ==

CRITICAL: with `buy_until` (market.rs:414-420), a static multiplier produces a
BOUNDED hoard, not a growing one. buy_until tops up to N and stops. Steady
state for a company with consumption c and multiplier k is a standing stock
that oscillates in [k*c - c, k*c]: it holds k*c, consumes c, re-orders c.
The surplus is `(k-1)*c`, CONSTANT, reached after one delivery cycle.

This is the single most important number in this ticket and the acceptance
criteria must be written against it. "Surplus accumulates without bound" is
NOT what this mechanism does and a test asserting growth will fail.

Is a bounded hoard true to Kornai? YES, and this is the honest answer: the
firm's target reserve level is a stock, not a flow. What grows without bound in
Kornai is the SHORTAGE the hoard causes elsewhere, not the hoard itself. The
hoard is a permanent withdrawal of `(k-1)*c` units per hoarding enterprise from
the pool available to everyone else. That withdrawal is the gameplay.

Recommended 1.0 values, against the real base_mod data:
- Default 1 for all 26 companies (honest is the norm; a shortage economy where
  EVERY enterprise lies has no signal).
- Exactly 2-4 hoarders, on prototypes deep in the bread chain, where the
  Planner can trace the consequence downstream to a queue:
    * flour-factory (companies.lua:36, consumption cereal 1, production flour
      10) -- `request_multiplier = 4`. Standing hoard 3 cereal.
    * meat-facility (companies.lua:577, consumption raw-meat 1) --
      `request_multiplier = 3`. Standing hoard 2 raw-meat.
  Keep the bakery HONEST (consumption flour 1): it is the only store with
  production and the only item humans actually buy (bread, buyfood.rs:73). The
  contrast the panel needs is bakery-honest vs flour-factory-inflated one step
  upstream.
- Do not exceed 4. At amount 1 and storage_multiplier 5 the production-side cap
  is `capital - reserved < amount*(sm+1)` = 6; a request multiplier above the
  storage cap makes the enterprise permanently idle-with-full-larder, which
  reads as a bug, not a lie.

== 4. WHAT MAKES THE HOARD BITE -- the blocking dependency ==

A hoard is only meaningful if the withdrawn units were SCARCE. Verified on this
tree today (market.rs:650-680):

- The free-goods leak IS FIXED: `find_external` returning None now `continue`s
  BEFORE `*capital.entry(buyer) += qty_buy` (market.rs:667-671). Unmatched
  enterprise buy orders are no longer granted free when there are no freight
  stations. Good -- shortage exists in the early game.
- BUT once a freight station exists, every unmatched non-human enterprise buy
  order is satisfied instantly from ext-trade: capital credited at market.rs:671
  with NO Dispatch (the dispatch loop at market.rs:604 has already run over
  `all_trades[dispatch_start..]`; ext trades are pushed after it). Goods
  teleport, and the enterprise never experiences shortage.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS TICKET: the hoard is invisible in any city with a freight
station, because nobody downstream ever goes short -- ext-trade backfills them
for free at the border price. The Planner sees a fat larder with no victim. The
mechanic is technically present and dramatically inert.

I am NOT asking sov-lpj to fix that. I am asking that it be filed and that
sov-lpj's acceptance be written to demonstrate the hoard in a NO-freight-station
city, so the ticket cannot be closed against a build where scarcity is bypassed.
File the teleport as a separate bead (successor to sov-ledger-exttrade-cbh).

== 5. THE FIVE DISCREPANCIES -- what 1.0 needs ==

REQ-PRODUCTION-001 names request, receipt, consumption, surplus, age.
For 1.0, in sim state:

MUST EXIST (1.0):
- REQUEST -- `Market::requested()`. Exists. This ticket gives it a real value.
- CONSUMPTION -- derived, `recipe.consumption[i].amount`. Exists; no new state.
- SURPLUS -- derived, `capital - reserved - consumption`. No new field. The
  panel differences it. Do NOT add a stored surplus field; a stored one can
  drift from the truth and the whole point is that the number is inferred.

DEFER (post-1.0, or later ticket -- each is a new accumulator, i.e. new state
that must be serialized, migrated and kept consistent):
- RECEIPT (cumulative delivered) -- a new per-company per-item counter. Adds
  save-format surface. It is a nicer signal than surplus but it is not needed:
  with a static multiplier, surplus alone separates honest from dishonest
  unambiguously (honest surplus = 0 in steady state, dishonest = (k-1)*c > 0).
- AGE (how long stock has sat) -- requires per-unit or per-lot timestamps, i.e.
  turning capital from a scalar into a queue. That is a substantial change to
  the Market representation and is the single most expensive of the five. It is
  the RIGHT long-term signal (stagnant stock is the true tell) and it is where
  the emergent version eventually lives, but it is not 1.0.

Ruling: THREE of five for 1.0 (request, consumption, surplus), two deferred.
This still satisfies the binding sentence "let the Planner infer hoarding
without an honesty flag" -- inference from three quantities is inference.

== 6. MODEL CHECKS ==

1. Clears by queue, not price? YES. `request_multiplier` changes a QUANTITY on
   a buy order. No Money anywhere on this path; `Trade.money_delta` stays
   Money::ZERO for domestic matches (market.rs:528). A richer enterprise gets
   nothing faster. CONSISTENT.
2. Preserves shortage? STRENGTHENS it, and is in fact the first mechanism in
   the game that manufactures shortage endogenously rather than from
   under-building. This is Kornai's hoarding-shortage vicious circle made
   playable. CONSISTENT -- conditional on section 4.
3. Failure degrades? YES. A hoarded input means the downstream plant idles and
   the queue lengthens. No termination path is introduced. CONSISTENT.
4. Preserves the incentive to lie? This is the one weakness, stated plainly:
   a STATIC multiplier is not an incentive, it is a fact. The enterprise does
   not choose to lie; it was authored lying. Honesty is not costly-or-cheap, it
   is just a number. The core loop's EMOTIONAL truth -- "this is rational
   behaviour under the incentives, not villainy" -- is asserted by the fiction,
   not produced by the sim.
   I accept this for 1.0 anyway. The Planner-facing half of the loop (catch it
   from observable state) is fully real with a static field, and that is the
   half the player touches. The enterprise-facing half (choose to lie because
   honesty gets you shorted) is where the emergent version belongs, post-1.0,
   and section 2's schema is deliberately shaped so it can arrive as
   "request_multiplier becomes the FLOOR/propensity, sim raises it under
   experienced shortage" without a data migration.
   State this trade-off in the bead. Do not let it be discovered later as a
   surprise.
5. Observable? YES, and by INFERENCE not readout, provided the panel shows
   requested and true consumption as separate numbers and does NOT show a
   "dishonest: yes/no" badge or a pre-computed inflation factor. The player
   must do the subtraction. Hard constraint on the downstream UI story
   (sov-hoard-panel-mko).

== 7. ACCEPTANCE-SHAPING CONSTRAINTS FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION BEAD ==

A. `request_multiplier` is OPTIONAL in Lua and defaults to 1. A parse that
   requires it breaks all 26 existing companies. Test: an unmodified company
   prototype still loads.
B. At least two shipped prototypes in base_mod/companies.lua declare
   request_multiplier > 1 (recommend flour-factory 4, meat-facility 3), so a
   running game -- not a fixture -- contains hoarders. This is the AC that
   sov-lpj exists for.
C. `Market::set_requested` gains at least one PRODUCTION caller. Test that
   fails if it goes back to test-only: assert requested() != None for a
   company spawned through company_soul in a live sim.
D. The surplus assertion must be BOUNDED, not growing: after N>=2 delivery
   cycles, an enterprise with multiplier k and consumption c holds stock in
   [k*c - c, k*c], and an honest one holds <= c. Mutation proof: set the
   hoarder's multiplier to 1 and the test must fail.
E. Demonstrated in a city with NO freight station. If ext-trade can backfill,
   the hoard has no victim and the test proves nothing about shortage.
F. NO honesty flag, NO stored surplus field, NO derived "inflation percentage"
   in sim state. Request and consumption are stored/declared; surplus is
   differenced at read time.
G. NO Money on any touched path. Negative assertion, enforced not merely
   written: assert money_delta == Money::ZERO for the domestic matches in the
   scenario.
H. Do not touch `storage_multiplier` semantics. request_multiplier bounds the
   INPUT buy order; storage_multiplier bounds the OUTPUT cap
   (goods_company.rs:41). They are the W&R $STORAGE_IMPORT / $CONSUMPTION
   distinction and must stay separate.

Two W&R notes: W&R has no field expressing "requests more than it consumes" --
confirmed, this is our invention, nothing to copy. But W&R's separation of
$CONSUMPTION (rate) from $STORAGE_IMPORT (inbound buffer, per transport class,
e.g. asphalt plant: $CONSUMPTION gravel 25 / $STORAGE_IMPORT
RESOURCE_TRANSPORT_GRAVEL 30) is the exact precedent for keeping our declared
request separate from our declared consumption. We are adding a third
quantity -- the REPORTED requirement -- that W&R does not have, and that is
precisely the design's contribution.

-- kornai-economist, Phase 0 consult, verified against working tree 2026-08-26

- sov_lpj_requested_is_set_by_production_recipe_init (AC C): spawns a real flour-factory via company_soul, asserts requested()==Some(4) (1*4). PASSES.
- sov_lpj_flour_factory_hoards_bounded_no_freight_station (AC D/E/G): real flour-factory (k=4,c=1) fed by a real bakery-as-seller (manual Market injection for supply only), driven by the ordinary company_system tick loop, converges to [3,4]. Money assertion: exact equality to money_before over 20k ticks (no humans -> no upkeep, no freight station -> no ext-trade credit possible). PASSES.
- Mutation proof done and then REMOVED (test file only ships the two above): with request_multiplier forced to 1 on a cloned Recipe driven manually via recipe_init/recipe_act on a fabricated buyer soul, the same bound assertion failed with 'flour-factory must converge to the bounded hoard [3, 4], got 0' -- confirms the wiring is genuinely sensitive to the multiplier, not just to the freight-station removal.

MAJOR FINDING, not in the original brief: TestCtx::new() is NOT freight-station-free. Simulation::new_with_options (lib.rs) unconditionally replays a hardcoded START_COMMANDS script that builds a real RailFreightStation + ExternalTrading zone on every single sim, test or production. market_update's find_external closure (economy/mod.rs) does world.freight_stations.iter().min_by_key(distance) with NO reachability check and NO distance cutoff -- so that station is always the (only) candidate and always matches, no matter how far away or road-disconnected a test's own buildings are.

This means hoarding.rs's EXISTING scenario_0151 (cited in my brief as the AC D reference) also silently ext-trades against this default station -- I traced its --nocapture output and saw 'A trade was made! ... seller: FreightStation ... money_delta: -1$' inside that test's own delivery loop. Its bounded-hoard assertion still happens to pass, but not purely from the domestic request_multiplier mechanism the kornai ruling describes -- ext-trade backfill is also active underneath it. AC E ('no freight station') is NOT achievable in this harness by simply avoiding WorldCommand::MapBuildSpecialBuilding(RailFreightStation) -- it has to be actively demolished. remove_building() alone is also insufficient: it deletes the map building but leaves the FreightStationEnt entity alive in world.freight_stations for one more tick (freight_station_system only kills it after noticing its building is gone), so find_external still matches it that tick. My inflation.rs::remove_default_freight_station() does WorldCommand::MapRemoveBuilding + one ctx.tick() + asserts world.freight_stations.is_empty() before returning -- this is the only way I found to get a genuinely freight-station-free TestCtx. Recommend a follow-up bead for hoarding.rs's SCENARIO-0151 to adopt the same helper, since its AC intent (isolate the domestic multiplier effect) is currently confounded.

Also recommend (separate from this ticket, not fixed here): find_external should have a distance cutoff or road-reachability check -- right now ANY test or any city, no matter how isolated, silently has a working export market the moment the default station exists.

comments.text: Update after lead ruling on electricity blocker: (1) ELECTRICITY FIXED. Wired build_company_at (local to inflation.rs) to accept connected_road: Option<RoadID>, threaded a real RoadID from an inline project()+make_connection() call, and spawn an unstaffed solar-panel (base_mod: type=solar-panel but SolarPanelPrototype derefs to a real GoodsCompanyPrototype, prototypes/src/prototypes/solar.rs -- spawns through the same build_company_at/company_soul path, no recipe to gate on, n_workers=0 + no zone painted gives raw_productivity=1.0 for free, no coal chain needed since power_production is scaled by workforce/zone only per goods_company.rs, never by recipe progress). recipe_act now genuinely fires -- confirmed, stock moves. (2) SECOND BUG FOUND AND WORKED AROUND: synthetic bakery seller's cereal capital was silently draining to 0. Root cause in economy/market.rs ~686-699: the seller-surplus-to-external-trading computation does *cap -= qty_sell UNCONDITIONALLY before checking find_external().is_some() -- with no freight station (AC E) that check always fails, so the Trade record is skipped but the capital deduction already happened with zero accounting. This is the exact defect this file's module doc already named ('silently ext-trades against it too', re: hoarding.rs SCENARIO-0151) but I didn't know it also erases capital unaccounted until I hit it live. Filed as sov-dii per lead (outbound twin of sov-abs). Worked around from the test side only, did NOT touch market.rs: sell(..., stock: 1_000_000) instead of stock: 0, since stock is what gates that computation (qty_sell = free_qty - stock never goes positive when stock==qty). (3) OPEN, HANDED TO debugger PER LEAD RULING: dispatches never complete. Trace: tick 24013 dispatches=[(ToDestination,1)], truck Driving. SAME dispatch still (ToDestination,1) at tick 62673 -- 38,000+ ticks later, never delivered -- while stock keeps monotonically draining (3->2->1) as later recipe_act firings pile more stuck dispatches on top. DispatchState::ToDestination's only exit (market.rs ~927) is ve.it.has_ended(0.0) on the truck's Itinerary; truck shows Driving (not vanished/lost) but itinerary apparently never completes. comments.author: debugger
comments.text: DEBUGGER FINDING: the ToDestination wedge is NOT an itinerary/dispatch-state-machine bug. Confirmed by instrumenting simulation/src/transportation/road.rs::calc_decision/calc_front_dist (reverted, git diff clean): every truck near the factory door (x~126) is permanently speed=0 with a live, valid Route itinerary (never WaitForReroute) blocked by ANOTHER VEHICLE dead ahead (calc_front_dist confirms is_vehicle=true, group=Vehicles every sample). Root: market.rs's Unloading-complete branch (~987) already has a ponytail comment admitting this: 'leave the truck Driving wherever it stopped instead of re-parking... upgrade to RoutingStep::Park... if idle trucks start blocking traffic.' That idle truck sits mid-lane at the factory door forever (Itinerary::NONE, state=Driving, never re-parked), and every subsequent dispatch's truck queues nose-to-tail behind it. The vehicle-vs-vehicle gridlock breaker (Panicking after front_dist<1.5 + flag self-match) never fires in 62k+ ticks (zero 'gridlock!' log lines) because propagation needs the tail vehicle's flag to round-trip through a chain via one-tick-lagged transport_grid_synchronize, and it never converges while new trucks keep queuing behind the permanently-idle one. CONFIRMED by mutation: changed the Unloading-complete branch to cbuf_vehicle.kill(v) instead of ve.it = Itinerary::NONE -- dispatch cycle immediately started completing (dispatches=[] then re-cycling ToSource/ToSource, stock reached upper bound 4, which the unmutated run never did in the sampled window). Mutation reverted. NOT the same defect as sov-jcl (that ticket is about Outbound Loading retry with no route; this is a completed dispatch's truck becoming a permanent physical obstruction). SUGGESTED: implement the RoutingStep::Park spline machinery the comment already names, or at minimum route the truck a short distance off the through-lane to a parking spot before dropping its itinerary.

PRE-EXISTING - reproduced on an unmodified tree (1 in 5 runs), NOT introduced by ITER-0000.

SYMPTOM: 'cargo test -p simulation' with default parallel threads segfaults intermittently (SIGSEGV, no Rust backtrace - a raw crash, not a panic). Reproduces ~1-in-3 to 1-in-5.

ROOT CAUSE: crate::init::init() (simulation/src/init.rs:33) pushes into 'static mut' INIT_FUNCS / GSYSTEMS / SAVELOAD_FUNCS with no synchronization. Every TestCtx::new() called it unconditionally, so concurrent test threads race on those pushes. rustc already warns here: 'creating a mutable reference to mutable static ... undefined behavior'.

PARTIAL FIX ALREADY IN TREE: TestCtx::new() now guards the init::init() call with std::sync::Once (simulation/src/tests/mod.rs). This REDUCES but does NOT eliminate the crash - some other unsynchronized global path is also involved and was not chased, to respect the do-not-touch-adjacent-code rule.

WORKAROUND until fixed: run 'cargo test -p simulation -- --test-threads=1'. All ITER-0000 verification used it.

WHY P1: the iterative-development spine treats sentinel scenario runs as evidence. A suite that segfaults 1-in-5 produces a confidently wrong signal - a green run proves little and a red run gets blamed on the wrong change. Fix before the sentinel corpus grows.

TRAP: do not 'fix' this by making the tests single-threaded in CI config and calling it done. That hides the UB rather than removing it; the static mut pattern is the defect.","status":"open","priority":1,"issue_type":"bug","created_at":"2026-08-22T15:40:56.339073861Z","created_by":"caio","updated_at":"2026-08-22T15:40:56.339073861Z","source_repo":"soviet-simulator","source_repo_path":"/home/caio/soviet-simulator","compaction_level":0,"original_size":0,"dependency_count":0,"dependent_count":0},{"id":"sov-pillar-assertions-ugb","title":"The design pillars have no runtime assertions","description":"Both pillars were violated in shipped code and no test noticed.

"Nothing teleports" and "never game over" are stated in CLAUDE.md, encoded as prose in ACs, and enforced NOWHERE at runtime.

EVIDENCE: the ext-trade buy block credited a buyer their full requested quantity whenever find_external returned None - which it does whenever world.freight_stations is empty, the normal early game. Every unmatched buy order was granted free, every tick, unpaid, and absent from EcoStats. Scarcity, the entire pressure source of the design, was switched off. It compiled, passed review, and passed every test. Found only when a specialist agent traced conservation across the seam (commit fdfabca).

The conservation invariant in tests/scenarios/ledger.rs is the first assertion of a pillar in the codebase and it only covers quantity.

PROPOSAL: give each pillar a cheap standing assertion the sentinel corpus runs every iteration.
  - nothing teleports: no capital increases without either a completed dispatch unload or a declared production/import source. Generalises ledger.rs beyond a hand-built pair of souls.
  - never game over: no code path terminates a run or produces an unrecoverable state; unmet need must always degrade.
  - clearing by queue, never by price: no Money read gates a physical flow. Partly a grep, better as a runtime assertion.

Cheaper than it sounds and it catches the class of bug that survives code review because the code is correct - it is the DESIGN that is violated.

title: The design pillars have no runtime assertions
description:
Both pillars were violated in shipped code and no test noticed.

"Nothing teleports" and "never game over" are stated in CLAUDE.md, encoded as prose in ACs, and enforced NOWHERE at runtime.

EVIDENCE: the ext-trade buy block credited a buyer their full requested quantity whenever find_external returned None - which it does whenever world.freight_stations is empty, the normal early game. Every unmatched buy order was granted free, every tick, unpaid, and absent from EcoStats. Scarcity, the entire pressure source of the design, was switched off. It compiled, passed review, and passed every test. Found only when a specialist agent traced conservation across the seam (commit fdfabca).

The conservation invariant in tests/scenarios/ledger.rs is the first assertion of a pillar in the codebase and it only covers quantity.

PROPOSAL: give each pillar a cheap standing assertion the sentinel corpus runs every iteration.
  - nothing teleports: no capital increases without either a completed dispatch unload or a declared production/import source. Generalises ledger.rs beyond a hand-built pair of souls.
  - never game over: no code path terminates a run or produces an unrecoverable state; unmet need must always degrade.
  - clearing by queue, never by price: no Money read gates a physical flow. Partly a grep, better as a runtime assertion.

Cheaper than it sounds and it catches the class of bug that survives code review because the code is correct - it is the DESIGN that is violated.

title: job-opening reserves stock but never releases it
description:
market.rs:334-336 reserves for EVERY match. market.rs:363 then skips dispatch creation for job-opening (`if kind != ItemID::new("job-opening")`). The dispatch is the ONLY thing that ever decrements `reserved` (market.rs:505) or debits capital (market.rs:503).

So for job-opening: acquire happens, release never does.

Sequence: company C does produce(job_opening, 5) then sell_all (goods_company.rs:166-167). Five humans each buy 1 (human.rs:269). Five matches -> reserved[C] = 5, sell order emptied, but capital[C][job-opening] stays at 5 forever instead of falling to 0.

CURRENTLY SILENT: no production reader of capital(soul, job_opening) outside tests.

LIVE TRAP: any future re-post of the job-opening sell order (rehiring after a worker dies) hits cap_seller - already_reserved = 5 - 5 = 0 < 1, and THE COMPANY CAN NEVER HIRE AGAIN.

FIX: release the reservation immediately for items that get no dispatch, or do not reserve on that branch.

BONUS - false comment: market.rs:358 claims a human buyer owns no building for a truck to route to. human.rs:272 calls set_owner(house, soul), so door_pos DOES resolve for humans. The conclusion (skip dispatch for job-opening) still stands on its other reason, but the stated premise is wrong and will mislead the next editor.
close_reason: commit fdfabca: job-opening debits at match time instead of reserving, since it never gets a dispatch and the dispatch is the only release path. Guard scenario_ledger_job_opening_reserve_leak seen FAILING first (left: 3, right: 0) then passing. Also fixed the false comment about human buyers owning no building (human.rs:272 set_owner).

title: sov_ie6 dead-truck test: the appended pool check is vacuous
description:
Carried forward from a ledger-invariant-checker comment on sov-abs before both tickets closed. Recording it as its own issue so it is not lost inside a closed ticket's comment thread.

simulation/src/tests/ -- the sov_ie6 dead-truck test. Its FIRST half is real and load-bearing: dispatch cancelled, reserved == 0, capital == 10. The APPENDED pool check is not.

WHY IT IS VACUOUS: the test destroys the truck via world.vehicles.remove(dead_truck), so all_trucks never contains the dead id afterwards. A leaked reserved_by entry for a non-existent entity blocks no LIVE truck, so the assertion 'every live truck must still be reservable' is true either way -- with the leak and without it. It cannot fail, so it proves nothing about the leak it appears to be testing.

CONTRAST, the shape that gets this right: sov_jcl_outbound_loading_route_failure_is_bounded asserts handed_out == reachable_trucks with reachable_trucks >= 2 and NO vehicle destroyed. That one genuinely detects a leaked reserved_by entry, and was confirmed non-vacuous at its gate.

TWO ACCEPTABLE FIXES, either is fine:
1. Assert the dead id IS handed out, which actually proves it left reserved_by; or
2. Drop the pool check and change the comment to say the ToSource cancellation is covered by the reserved/capital assertions only.

Do NOT just delete the assertion silently -- the comment above it currently claims coverage the test does not provide, and that claim is the actual defect.
acceptance_criteria: Either the pool assertion is rewritten so that removing the reserved_by cleanup makes it FAIL (mutation-proven, failure pasted), or it is removed and the surrounding comment corrected to state exactly what the test does and does not cover. The test name must appear in the 'running N tests' output of the run used as evidence.

title: recipe.duration of 0 gives infinite production progress, not a panic
description:
Found by reviewer 2026-08-28 at the sov-k3w Phase-4 gate. simulation/src/souls/goods_company.rs:205 computes progress += productivity * DELTA / recipe.duration.seconds() as f32. This is FLOAT division, so a duration of 0 yields +inf rather than panicking: progress >= 1.0 on every tick, and the enterprise produces at unbounded rate forever.

Same silent-wrong-meaning class as sov-k3w, but strictly worse to detect, because there is no panic to catch it and no error anywhere -- the game just runs with a factory that ignores its own recipe time.

LATENT: no base_mod recipe currently has duration 0. P3 rather than P2 because the sign-wrap siblings are more reachable by a plausible typo, and duration is written in a unit-bearing form that makes 0 less likely.

Fix belongs in the same validate() loop as sov-k3w and its storage_multiplier sibling.
acceptance_criteria: validate() refuses a recipe duration of 0 with a named error. A test drives it through the real parse+validate path via prototypes::try_parse_prototypes and sees it refused. Mutation-proven with the failure pasted, and the test confirmed present by name in the 'running N tests' line.
close_reason: Zero-duration refusal landed (5c4d96e): validate() rejects recipe.duration 0 + sov_0o0_zero_duration_is_refused via try_parse_prototypes. Gates: prototypes validation 2 passed, snw unregressed.

title: A city that loses all external trade gets no Planner-facing signal
description:
Raised as non-blocking caveats by kornai-economist (ruling 5) and logistics-modeller (Condition B), Phase-4 2026-08-28.

Two silent-failure surfaces, both introduced or enlarged by sov-abs:
1. If a city's only freight station has no driving lane within DISPATCH_LANE_CUTOFF, find_external returns None and ALL external trade stops. Nothing tells the player. This is the default state of a fresh map (see the START_COMMANDS finding).
2. A stalled dispatch escalates only to log::warn!, which no player sees. requirements/movement.md requires stalls to escalate to a planner-visible bottleneck event.

The economics of refusing an undeliverable import are correct and are not in question -- what is missing is the readout. Both advisors said this wants a readout, not a code change in the market.
acceptance_criteria: The HUD shows external-trade availability and the count of stalled dispatches. Proven by an eyeballed frame plus a public sim accessor, per the UI lane's evidence rule.

title: Bound the border on freight-station throughput
description:
kornai-economist ruling 2, Phase-4 sign-off on sov-abs 2026-08-28. ACCEPTED FOR 1.0 as-is; this is the successor ticket the ruling asked for, not a defect report.

simulation/src/economy/market.rs:847 debits the FreightStation seller with no stock and no reservation, so its capital goes negative without limit. kornai-economist accepts this for 1.0 because transport is the binding constraint and it is the one the Planner can actually act on.

It is not the right long-run model. Kornai (The Socialist System, 1992) separates the SOFT domestic budget constraint from the HARD external one; an unbounded border collapses that distinction. The bound belongs on freight-station THROUGHPUT in units per tick, which is also the Workers and Resources precedent.

Do not implement this as a price or affordability gate -- clearing by price is on the charter's Never list.
acceptance_criteria: Freight-station throughput is a declared per-tick capacity; a scenario demanding more than that capacity shows the excess QUEUING rather than being refused or priced out.

title: DispatchOne::unregister leaks reserved_by for a truck destroyed while reserved
description:
logistics-modeller finding 6, Phase-4 2026-08-28. A leak, not a wedge. Minor and pre-existing.

First, the REFUTATION so it is not re-investigated: 'Dispatcher::update never purges a removed entity' is FALSE. simulation/src/world.rs:80-83, VehicleEnt::sim_drop calls Dispatcher::unregister for every removed truck.

The real residual is narrower. map_dynamic/dispatch.rs:218-224, DispatchOne::unregister early-returns when 'positions' has no entry, and reserve (:211) REMOVES the entry from positions. So a truck destroyed WHILE RESERVED keeps its id in reserved_by forever.

Inert for query (the id is no longer in lanes) and the market frees it on the next tick in practice, so nothing wedges. Worth closing anyway because it is exactly the shape that made retail::scenario_dead_truck_tosource_cancels_without_leak unfalsifiable.

Also noted, same area: map_dynamic/dispatch.rs:163 DispatchOne::register still uses a bare 50.0 rather than DISPATCH_LANE_CUTOFF. Different semantics (vehicle-to-lane, not target-to-lane) so not a duplication bug, but it is the same number and will drift. Fix in the same edit.
acceptance_criteria: unregister clears reserved_by even when positions has no entry, and a test destroys a reserved truck then asserts reserved_by no longer names it. Mutation-prove by restoring the early return.
close_reason: Wave-2 green (sim suite 96 passed 0 failed). See commits a3e57ce/34358bd-range.

title: The border out-competes domestic supply by one tick
description:
kornai-economist finding F2, Phase-4 2026-08-28. Not a pillar violation -- the queue is simply a different queue -- but it changes who the default supplier is.

Domestic matching runs first, but only within the tick an order is posted. simulation/src/economy/market.rs:621 then hands every surviving non-human buy order to the border via extract_if. So an enterprise never queues on a domestic producer that will have stock NEXT tick; it goes abroad instead.

The intended shape is the border as the RESIDUAL supplier, not the default one. Fix shape: let an unmatched order age for N ticks before it becomes eligible for the border.
acceptance_criteria: A scenario with a domestic producer that gains stock one tick after an order is posted shows the order filled DOMESTICALLY, not by import.
close_reason: Wave-2 green (sim suite 96 passed 0 failed). See commits a3e57ce/34358bd-range.

title: MAX_RETURN_ROUTE_RETRIES of 20 ticks is 0.4 seconds at 1x
description:
logistics-modeller Condition A on sov-jcl (166b1cf), Phase-4 2026-08-28. Tuning, not correctness -- it was explicitly not a block.

common/src/timestep.rs:3 sets UP_DT = 20ms, so the sim runs 50 ticks/s. MAX_RETURN_ROUTE_RETRIES = 20 is therefore 0.4 SECONDS of wall clock at 1x speed.

Itinerary::route fails transiently while the map is being edited, and 0.4s sits comfortably inside a single player road-drag. Bulldoze one segment and every truck city-wide that happens to be mid-Loading silently loses its load. The bound was chosen for a PERMANENT trigger (the buyer is gone); the outbound trigger is usually TRANSIENT.

Recommended: 250-500 ticks (5-10 seconds).

Note also, from ledger-invariant-checker: the comparison is 'retries + 1 >= MAX', so it fires after 19 attempts rather than 20. Harmless off-by-one, worth correcting in the same edit.
acceptance_criteria: The constant is raised with a comment stating its wall-clock duration at 50 ticks/s, and a test proves a dispatch survives a route failure lasting longer than the OLD bound.
close_reason: Wave-2 green (sim suite 96 passed 0 failed). See commits a3e57ce/34358bd-range.

title: bincode free functions use a different config from saveload::Bincode; mixing them corrupts saves
description: Raised by researcher 2026-08-28 as a GUARD RAIL, not a defect that has happened - flagged as prospective and currently clean. VERIFIED AT SOURCE: bincode-1.3.3/src/config/mod.rs:15-18 and lib.rs:106-114 - the free functions bincode::serialize()/deserialize() use FIXINT encoding with AllowTrailing, while DefaultOptions, which common::saveload::Bincode uses, is VARINT with RejectTrailing. The two write streams the other cannot read. Grep confirms ZERO direct `bincode::` uses outside common/src/saveload.rs today; the ticket exists to keep it that way, because the failure mode is a corrupt save rather than a compile error. CONTEXT that makes this crate dangerous: bincode is positional and schema-less - no field names, no defaults, no skips - so adding, removing or REORDERING a field in any type reachable from a saved resource invalidates every existing save. And the version gate at simulation/src/lib.rs:404-415 only WARNS and ignores the patch field, so 0.6.0 and 0.6.9 both load silently. Nothing currently refuses a save it cannot correctly read.
acceptance_criteria: A lint, test or documented rule prevents direct bincode:: use outside saveload.rs, and the version gate either refuses an incompatible save or the doc states plainly why warning is enough.

title: egui-inspect-derive panics in the proc macro: contributors get a build failure with no error message
description: Found by researcher 2026-08-28 reading the widget lane at source. A proc macro that panics displays NO error to the user - the build simply fails without saying why. egui-inspect-derive currently panics at inspect_macro/mod.rs:68, :115, :190 and :210, and unwraps parses at :11, :121, :135 and :138. Every one of those is a mystery build failure for whoever adds a field to an inspected struct. The correct form is a spanned syn::Error::to_compile_error() (https://docs.rs/syn/latest/syn/struct.Error.html), which points at the offending token and says what is wrong. SIBLING, same lane, same shape - a panic on a live path: goryak widgets run inside the frame loop and call ctx.layout.get(ctx.dom.current()).unwrap() at roundrect.rs:102, scroll.rs:152 and :388, progress_bar.rs:65, imagebutton.rs:163, interact_box.rs:112 and sized_canvas.rs:86. A widget should degrade to a no-draw rather than unwrap, because never-game-over applies to the renderer too. NOTE ON EVIDENCE GRADE: this lane has no recorded defect history at all - no agent-memory directory, no prior bd bug, nothing in 120 commits. These are source reads from today, not lessons that cost time. goryak also has ZERO tests across 22 files.
acceptance_criteria: The derive macro emits spanned compile errors instead of panicking; a struct with an unsupported field shape produces a readable error naming the field. The goryak unwrap sites either degrade to no-draw or carry a stated reason why the invariant cannot fail.

title: Adopt pinned wgpu-profiler v0.17.0 in place of the hand-rolled gpu_timing module
description:
Deferred adoption decision from the sov-dda.1 spike. The spike is answered; only the swap remains, and it is not urgent because the hand-rolled module now has measured numbers on real hardware.

## Steps to Reproduce
Not a bug. Read the spike evidence at tag archive/sov-dda-1-wgpu-profiler (commit 69ffed1), which holds the working wiring against wgpu 0.20.1.

VERIFIED BY THE SPIKE, against the pinned crate sources -- re-derive before trusting, per the repo's standing rule:
- profiler.rs resolves num_resolved*QUERY_SIZE, so the never-reset-slot class of Vulkan UB that sov-abc fixed CANNOT occur by construction.
- begin_pass_query at src/profiler.rs:262-275 plus GpuProfilerQuery::render_pass_timestamp_writes at src/profiler_query.rs:74-84 produce exactly the wgpu::RenderPassTimestampWrites our gpu_timing.rs::writes() hand-builds, and need only Features::TIMESTAMP_QUERY -- the SAME feature bar, not a higher one.
- begin_query_internal at src/profiler.rs:685-694 checks device.features() itself and degrades to no timer; GpuProfilerSettings::enable_timer_queries=false makes every call a no-op with lazy resource creation. Opt-in-and-inert is native, not bolted on.
- scope() takes &self (src/profiler.rs:131-136), so it works inside the existing rayon in_place_scope parallel render at gfx.rs:736-763 with no change to device or queue ownership.
- COST: Cargo.lock gains exactly ONE package. parking_lot and thiserror 1.0.61 were already present, and cargo tree --workspace --duplicates reports no wgpu duplicate.

WHAT WE WOULD LOSE and must reimplement as a thin layer: min/median/max PassTimingSummary aggregation. wgpu-profiler does not provide it, and it is what makes the capture output readable.

WHAT WE WOULD GAIN: collect_frame currently blocks on device.poll(Maintain::Wait) every armed frame, serialising CPU and GPU and distorting the very pass overlap it is measuring. wgpu-profiler uses map_async with max_num_pending_frames in flight and returns None until ready.

BASELINE TO BEAT, measured on this hardware 2026-08-28 with the hand-rolled module, medians over n=30 on AMD Radeon RX 7800 XT (RADV NAVI32) at 1280x720: main 93.2us, ssao 33.2us, fog 28.0us, depth_prepass 25.5us, background 24.4us, shadow_cascade_0 14.2us, cascades 1-3 about 10.5-10.9us.

TRAP: the capture currently reports 12 passes but times only 9. pbr_prepass, ui_blur and gui produce no timing. Establish whether that is the written-mask correctly skipping passes that did not run, or a real gap, BEFORE swapping -- otherwise the swap inherits an unexplained difference and gets blamed for it.

Depends on feat/sov-uy2-capture landing first; that branch is where gpu_timing.rs lives.
Scope: engine/ only. Owner lane: engine-implementer.
acceptance_criteria: wgpu-profiler is pinned to an exact version with its licence verified from the shipped LICENSE file, not the manifest field alone. cargo tree --workspace --duplicates shows no wgpu duplicate. A capture run on the RX 7800 XT reports non-zero per-pass medians for at least the nine passes the hand-rolled module timed, and those medians are pasted beside the baseline above for comparison. min/median/max aggregation still appears in the capture output. The hand-rolled gpu_timing module is deleted, not left beside its replacement. engine_demo capture_contract tests still pass.

title: gen_exterior_house retry loop is unbounded
description:
wiring-auditor finding on the sov-bo3 gate, 2026-08-27. PRE-EXISTING, not caused by the sov-bo3 fix — do not block that merge on it.

simulation/src/map/procgen/building.rs:32 opens 'retry: loop. retry_cnt only reseeds the RNG; it never terminates the loop. There are now six continue 'retry paths, including the new None arm the sov-bo3 fix added for a corrupt skeleton.

Each retry generates a different polygon, so it terminates in practice. But the sov-bo3 fix traded an OOM kill for an UNBOUNDED RETRY rather than a bounded fallback. Under the 'Never game over' pillar an infinite retry is a hang, which is also a terminated game from the player's seat.

Decide deliberately: bound the retry count and fall back to a trivial placeholder mesh, or justify in a comment why unbounded is safe here.
acceptance_criteria: Either the retry loop is bounded with a documented fallback that yields a usable mesh, or a comment at building.rs:32 justifies why unbounded retry cannot hang, backed by an argument about polygon generation. A test that forces repeated skeleton failure and shows the loop terminates.

title: TestCtx determinism check unstable on transport_grid: FnvHashMap serialize order not round-trip-stable
description: Found during sov-lpj fix pass (sim-implementer, 2026-08-26). TestCtx::check_determinism() fails on the transport_grid key with 10 spawned humans over ~20k ticks, holds with 5 humans over 46k. Cause (read from vendored source): TransportGrid = flat_spatial::Grid (transportation/mod.rs:72); flat_spatial-0.6.1 SparseStorage.cells is a fnv::FnvHashMap (storage.rs:31). Bincode serializes HashMap in bucket-iteration order, which is not stable across encode-decode-encode once entries churn — same logical content, different bytes. TRAP: this makes the harness's hash-compare a flaky false-negative source at high entity counts; tests currently dodge it by using fewer humans. Not fixable from test files; needs a BTreeMap-backed storage, a canonical-order serialize wrapper, or excluding transport_grid from the hash.
acceptance_criteria: A test spawning 10+ humans over 20k+ ticks passes check_determinism repeatedly, or transport_grid is excluded from the hash with a comment citing this issue.
close_reason: Wave-2 green (sim suite 96 passed 0 failed). See commits a3e57ce/34358bd-range.

title: Extract try_return_to_seller shared by Market::remove and advance_dispatches
description:
Ponytail shrink identified by the opus reviewer on sov-dispatch-wedge-ab4 round 3. The dead-buyer arm of Market::remove (market.rs ~316-368) and the Loading buyer-gone branch of advance_dispatches (~market.rs:872-905) both do the same thing: door_pos(seller) -> Itinerary::route from the truck's position -> on success set the truck's itinerary and transition to Returning, on failure log::warn + dispatcher.free + drop the dispatch. Extracting a shared helper is roughly -45 lines including two comment trims.

DEFERRED DELIBERATELY, not forgotten. Reason (lead ruling 2026-08-26): it is a pure refactor of a conservation-critical function that holds two fresh gate signoffs -- ledger-invariant-checker CONSERVED (which verified Market::remove arm-by-arm and left the file byte-identical) and opus reviewer APPROVE-WITH-FIXES. Re-opening it buys 45 lines against invalidating that baseline, with no behavioural failure driving it.

Do this only when Market::remove is being changed for a real reason anyway, so the gates have to re-run regardless. If you take it: the two sites differ in that advance_dispatches counts return_route_retries against MAX_RETURN_ROUTE_RETRIES and Market::remove does not (it gets one attempt); do not accidentally give the remove path retries it never had, and do not drop the bound from the advance path.
acceptance_criteria: try_return_to_seller extracted and called from both sites; cargo test -p simulation still 42/42 green; the ledger-invariant-checker gate re-run returns CONSERVED; the retry-bound asymmetry between the two call sites is preserved or its change is deliberate and documented.
close_reason: Wave-2 green (sim suite 96 passed 0 failed). See commits a3e57ce/34358bd-range.

title: Retail claim-overwrite release is unsound once a second human-purchasable item exists (debug_assert is a release no-op)
description:
market.rs:503-531. When a human's RetailClaim is overwritten, the displaced claim's reservation is released using the per-kind loop's LOCAL 'reserved' map, guarded only by debug_assert_eq!(old.kind, kind) -- which compiles to nothing in release builds.

Sound TODAY only because buyfood.rs:82 is the sole issuer of human buy orders and hardcodes bread, so old.kind always equals kind. The moment a second human-purchasable item exists, an overwrite across kinds silently decrements the WRONG market's reserved row in release builds: one seller's stock is unreserved without cause and another's stays frozen. Silent, no log, invisible to the ledger accountant (it is a reservation defect, not a capital one).

TRIGGER: any change that makes a human buy something other than bread. Fix at that time: look the correct SingleMarket up by old.kind instead of using the loop-local map, and turn the debug_assert into real branching.

Found by ledger-invariant-checker 3rd pass on sov-dispatch-wedge-ab4; explicitly flagged NOT a blocker for that ticket and left latent by lead decision.
acceptance_criteria: Either (a) the release path looks the displaced claim's market up by old.kind rather than relying on the enclosing per-kind loop, with a test that overwrites a claim across two different item kinds and asserts both sellers' reserved rows are correct in a release-semantics build; or (b) a compile-time or runtime invariant makes a cross-kind overwrite impossible and is documented at the call site.

title: Give TestCtx a seed and a fast tick before the journey harness grows
description:
Two gaps found while reviewing the walking-skeleton harness plan.

1. NO SEED. SimulationOptions exposes only terrain_size and save_replay. JOURNEY-0001's final observable claims 'identical seed and inputs yield identical ledger figures', but there is no seed field - today that can only mean 'identical construction'. Either add a seed or reword the observable.

2. TICK COST. TestCtx::tick() does a full bincode encode + decode + per-key hashes() comparison EVERY tick. That is exactly the determinism guarantee we want, but it will dominate runtime on a multi-hundred-tick journey. Add a tick_fast() without the round-trip and keep the checked tick for boundaries.

Not blocking ITER-0000, which is short. Becomes painful as journeys lengthen.
close_reason: commit 2fcfd94: SimulationOptions gained seed:u64 threaded to RandProvider in the WorldCommand::Init handler (world_command.rs:332), replacing the hardwired private const RNG_SEED=123. Fast tick added: check_determinism() split out of tick(), advance_ticks(n) checks every 25th tick and always the last. Verified cargo test -p simulation -- --test-threads=1 -> 22 passed.
